title: 49ers wanted to keep Shanahan accident quiet, and some in the media complied
summary: Saturday's news that 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan had been in a serious car accident was surprising, to say the least.
full_text: Saturday's news that 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan had been in a serious car accident was surprising, to say the least. Although he's dealing with more than a few significant physical issues, including a severe concussion, the injuries were not life-threatening, and it appears that he's on a path to recovery. There's a separate issue that's hard to ignore regarding the accident itself. It happened on July 14. The 49ers managed to keep it from being reported for 11 days. It possibly would still be a secret today; the disclosure coincided with the first day of the team's 2026 training camp. And, in hindsight, the effort to get the word out seems to have been engineered. The 49ers posted their statement regarding the accident at 12:00 p.m. ET on Saturday . Adam Schefter of ESPN posted his first tweet on the situation exactly one minute later, at 12:01 p.m. ET . The ESPN article about the accident was published at 12:02 p.m. ET . Nick Wagoner, who covers the 49ers for ESPN and who shared credit with Schefter for the story, reposted Schefter's tweet at 12:03 p.m. ET . Why would ESPN hold the information until the 49ers disclosed it? Beyond the obvious fact that the NFL now owns 10 percent of ESPN (which means the 49ers own 1/32nd of the 10 percent), this kind of negotiated reporting isn't uncommon. Given that ESPN had information that wasn't in the 49ers' release ( e.g. , injury details and news from local law enforcement about the other driver not being injured, the finding that alcohol or drugs were not a factor, and the decision that no one should be cited for the crash), it's fair to wonder if ESPN made a deal with the 49ers to hold the news until the team announced it — possibly in exchange for receiving the full specifics about Shanahan's injuries. Others who cover the 49ers knew about it, too. Before the news was released, Tim Kawakami of the San Francisco Standard dropped a hint: "I think there's going to be some news later this morning." Kawakami later admitted that he was aware of the situation, but that he didn't report it because he " knew about 15% of the details ." Still, he apparently knew 100 percent of the fact that there was an accident. Not every detail related to the story needed to be reported, especially when plenty of the basic information about the collision was available from public sources. News regarding events that entail the involvement of the police and/or other first responders rarely gets held. It's public information. (For example, news regarding Tony Romo's recent arrest was shared as soon as Fox News 6 in Wisconsin obtained the public arrest detention report.) In this situation, the conduits for publicly-available information to the general public either were asleep at the switch or made a deliberate choice not to perform one of the core functions of journalism. Brokering a deal (either in exchange for more facts or because the team asks nicely) to hold publicly-available information until the team decides to disclose it isn't journalism. It's the antithesis of journalism. But it's hardly uncommon in sports. Whether it's an exercise in trading favors or ensuring that the organization being covered doesn't freeze out a reporter who failed to go along with the plan, it happens all the time. This is just the latest example of it. As Jay Glazer of Fox told me years ago, true journalism in sports involves finding out the stuff they don't want us to know, not reporting something that's going to be announced in five minutes. Implicit in finding it out is, after doing so, finding a way to report it. Shanahan's accident happened on a public roadway. Public agencies responded to it. Basic information about the situation was publicly available. And folks who publicize relevant information to the public for a living chose not to do it until they got the go-ahead from the 49ers. That's not how it's supposed to work. Reporters owe a primary duty to their audience, not to the entities they cover. In sports, that line started to blur when leagues and teams began hiring reporters to cover them. Twenty years later, that line is long gone.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan attends roughly 30 minutes of 49ers' practice on Sunday
summary: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan is recovering from various injuries sustained in a July 14 car accident.
full_text: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan is recovering from various injuries sustained in a July 14 car accident. He'll be participating in training camp on a limited basis, due to the aftermath of a severe concussion. Via Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area , Shanahan was on the practice field for roughly 30 minutes on Sunday. He watched most of the 11-on-11 portion of practice, with G.M. John Lynch. They were positioned deep behind the secondary. It's unknown when Shanahan will be cleared to resume full duties. Assistant head coach Chris Foerster is serving as head coach in Shanahan's absence. The 49ers open the season against the Rams on September 10 in Melbourne, Australia.
author: Mike Florio

title: Drake Maye: Jared Wilson's done "a great job of understanding" what goes into playing center
summary: A.J.
full_text: ' A.J. Brown's arrival in New England has led to a lot of discussion about how quarterback Drake Maye will adjust to playing with a new No. 1 wide receiver, but it's not the only adjustment that Maye will be making as the team prepares for the 2026 season. The Patriots traded Garrett Bradbury to the Bears this offseason and that means 2025 third-round pick Jared Wilson will move over from guard for his second season. That process will include getting comfortable with Maye as well as getting comfortable making blocking calls on the line, which are both things that Maye believes will go more smoothly because Wilson had the chance to watch Bradbury do the job last year. "I think Garrett, you get to know a center for a year, and you get to know his little things, how he likes things, if he's going left and I'm going right, how it works, little under center things and how he understands mic points," Maye said, via a transcript from the team. "But Jared, he's smart. He's real smart. I wanted him to play with me in college. He went to the SEC. I don't blame him, but, I think he's done a great job of understanding what comes with playing center. You got to be loud. You got to be, “me and you, it's our show.” So, I think he's done a great job. Just getting used to little things under center, how he likes to do silent cadence and stuff like that. But he's got a great feel for the cadence. And he saw Garrett do it last year, which is a great look for him." The Patriots' offensive line play in their Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks left much to be desired and there was room for improvement all season. Getting Maye and Wilson into a groove will be crucial to finding that improvement once they get back into game action this fall.
author: Josh Alper

title: Trent Williams tries to "soak it in" as he nears end of career
summary: When left tackle Trent Williams agreed to a new two-year contract with the 49ers this offseason, he said he believes that it will be the final one that he signs.
full_text: ' When left tackle Trent Williams agreed to a new two-year contract with the 49ers this offseason, he said he believes that it will be the final one that he signs. Williams turned 38 this month and he said that he expects the 2027 season to be his final one as an active player. On Sunday, Williams was asked if that mindset has led him to take on a different approach to this training camp. "I wouldn't say it changed my urgency, but it does change my mind frame a little bit," Williams said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "Like, instead of just coming to work, I actually try to soak it in . I just don't know. Obviously, you know, it could be my last two years. It's probably the plan." Williams was a second-team All-Pro last season and remains a vital part of the 49ers' plans for 2026, so any moments of contemplation about the big picture of his career will play out alongside his preparation to continue playing at a high level for a team hoping to make a long run in the postseason.
author: Josh Alper

title: Drake Maye: Christian Gonzalez's main focus is football, not his contract
summary: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez wants a new contract, but he's not sitting out training camp to get one.
full_text: ' Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez wants a new contract, but he's not sitting out training camp to get one. Drake Maye appreciates that. Maye, the Patriots' quarterback and team captain, said that Gonzalez is one of the players he most looks up to, even though they're exactly the same age — Gonzalez turned 24 last month and Maye turns 24 next month — because Gonzalez has such a businesslike approach. “I think that shows his main focus, and that’s football," Maye said. "He’s the best corner in the league, in my opinion. He's not a big rah-rah guy, he does it his own way, but he does it at the highest level, so I'm glad to be his teammate. We're around the same age, and I tell him . . . Gonzo is someone I look up to, even as the same age. I look up to how he does things. How he handles himself." Maye said one of the reasons the Patriots have had success is the way they practice against each other, which includes Maye throwing to A.J. Brown, with Gonzalez in coverage, on the first day of training camp. "I think it’s great to see him out here playing around," Maye said. "You saw it in the locker room before, everybody was wondering what’s Gonzo gonna do? First play he’s guarding A.J. in man coverage. That’s the Patriots.”
author: Michael David Smith

title: Daniel Jones says he feels "really good" and is ready to go for training camp
summary: Jones suffered a torn Achilles tendon on December 7.
full_text: '' Colts quarterback Daniel Jones says he is feeling no ill effects from the torn Achilles tendon that ended his 2025 season. Jones joined the ESPN booth for the NFL Flag Championships in Indianapolis and said he'll be 100 percent for the Colts' first training camp practice on Wednesday. "I feel good. Really good. Excited to get going. We report tomorrow, first practice Wednesday, so good to go. I'm excited to get rolling," Jones said. Colts head coach Shane Steichen was also at the NFL Flag Championships and said he's been thrilled with Jones' work this offseason. "He looks great. He's attacked the rehab process, as good as it gets," Steichen said. "He'll be a full participant." Jones was having a solid season before he suffered the injury. He signed a two-year, $88 million contract this offseason to remain with the Colts.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean McVay: Outside expectations won't change the Rams' approach
summary: The Rams have a good problem, even if the only good problem is no problem.
full_text: ' The Rams have a good problem, even if the only good problem is no problem. Outside expectations are sky-high. Even though the Rams haven't been to the Super Bowl in five years, they're the favorite to emerge from the NFC and to win the whole thing. Coach Sean McVay addressed the high bar the Rams are facing in his Saturday session with reporters. "The last time I checked, none of that stuff means anything," McVay said. "It's what's great about the league. People care, there's a lot of attention, but this is the greatest team sport there is. We've got to come together as a team. We've got to stay humble. There's a lot of stuff in the midst of the journey that we don't control, but I think our ability to be connected, to be courageous, to handle the storms when they do come up and be inside out more than ever before is going to be really important. "But we're not going to allow the outside expectations to change the way that we approach every day with the way that we work, the way that we enjoy it, have the appropriate mindset and energy. And that's something that I think is really important for us to represent and I think that's more felt than anything else. And so that's what we're going to do, but none of those things mean anything. They don't win games, and how can we be present, stack days, and enjoy the opportunity to come together as a team? We're not going to let external expectations inhibit our ability to go swing and be courageous.” The challenge is to get the players to ignore the outside chatter, and to accept the fact that, every week, they'll get the absolute best that every opponent will have to offer. Even with a wide array of uniforms, the one constant is the target they'll have on their backs. Along with a schedule that has them in prime time for seven games — and that has them playing on a Wednesday, a Thursday, a Friday, multiple Sundays, and multiple Mondays.
author: Mike Florio

title: PFT Live returns on Monday, July 27
summary: The hiatus flew by, as it always does.
full_text: ''' The hiatus flew by, as it always does. The slow time was never really all that slow. While PFT Live was off, I filled the void with 28 episodes of #PFTPM — mostly from the Olive Garden alternate studio. (Except on the days when I couldn't find my photo ID.) Tomorrow, we're back. And it'll be the start of the tenth year with Simms as the primary co-host. We'll have plenty to discuss, with training camps open and lots of news to discuss and analyze. Join us at 7:00 a.m. ET on Peacock, NBCSN, SiriusXM 85. Or via podcast, wherever you get your podcasts. For our friends in the UK and Ireland, we'll be back on Sky Sports. Whenever they decide to re-air the live show. (They don't tell us.) If you're a regular, you know what to expect. If you're not, there's no time to start like now. It's a real, authentic, unscripted conversation about anything and everything we decide to talk about. We'll have pre-planned topics to discuss, but it's always subject to change — especially if news breaks during the show. If news breaks after the show and it's worthy of discussion, #PFTPM re-enters the conversation. From the Olive Garden set. As long as I can find my photo ID.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jacoby Brissett on signing his new deal: I'm glad it's over with
summary: Jacoby Brissett got himself a $10 million raise, negotiating the deal himself, but serving as his own agent cost him sleep.
full_text: '' Jacoby Brissett got himself a $10 million raise , negotiating the deal himself, but serving as his own agent cost him sleep. The Cardinals quarterback said the stress was limiting him to three hours of sleep a night. "It's your livelihood; it’s business ; and it's part of this game," Brissett said Sunday, via Darren Urban of the team website. "You want to be out there with the guys and that causes another stressor. I'm glad it's over with." It took the entire offseason, which Brissett skipped the voluntary portion of, and into training camp before Brissett got what he wanted. The team's presumptive starter was scheduled to make a max $5.39 million in 2026, with only $1.5 million guaranteed. "It definitely got dark a couple of times," Brissett said. He said wanting a raise was about "having respect for yourself." Now, he begins the process of winning the job. He is the favorite, but coach Mike LaFleur has promised only that Brissett will work with the starters on Tuesday. Brissett will have to beat out Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck to start Week 1. The hard part, though, is done. "After the sleep I get tonight," Brissett said, "I'll go back to three hours of sleep for work purposes now."
author: Charean Williams

title: Mike Macdonald on Hard Knocks: "We are proud of who we are and how we do things"
summary: The Seahawks will defend their second Super Bowl championship by welcoming Hard Knocks cameras and microphones into practice for the first time.
full_text: ' The Seahawks will defend their second Super Bowl championship by welcoming Hard Knocks cameras and microphones into practice for the first time. Coach Mike Macdonald has no reservations about doing so. Asked on Saturday whether he has noticed the NFL Films crew, Macdonald said this: “A little bit, yeah, a little bit. I’m mic’d up right now. I’ve got to get used to that. I told the guys they are going to capture what we do, and they do a great job of doing that. Let’s be us. We want them to capture us. We are proud of who we are and how we do things, so there is really no reason to try and change anything or try to be something we are not. Probably by tomorrow, the next day, probably won’t notice it, honestly.” It's the right attitude, mainly because there's no way around it. Their ticket had been pulled; they're this year's Hard Knocks guinea pig. Why fight it? But, yes, Macdonald will need to get used to wearing a microphone. And he'll need to remember to turn it off before going to the bathroom . Hard Knocks debuts earlier than usual, with the first episode landing on Tuesday, August 4 — before the Hall of Fame game.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chris Foerster: Coaching the 49ers in Kyle Shanahan's absence is "really a group thing"
summary: With 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan limited at training camp due to a severe concussion suffered in a recent car accident, assistant head coach/offensive line Chris Foerster is running the team.
full_text: ' With 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan limited at training camp due to a severe concussion suffered in a recent car accident, assistant head coach/offensive line Chris Foerster is running the team. In his first media session with reporters on Sunday, Foerster made it clear he's not doing it alone. “It's really a group thing," Foerster told reporters. "The title puts me in this position, and I was very grateful that [General Manager] John [Lynch] and Kyle felt that some of the things I could take the lead on, like this right here. But there's other things, for example, our team meetings. Instead of me running every team meeting, we'll split up on offense and defense and [defensive coordinator] Raheem [Morris] and [offensive coordinator] Klay [Kubiak] will do things. Maybe we'll have [special teams coordinator Brant] Boyer lead one and cover different things. "Kyle, one of the greatest things he does is how he leads a team meeting and talks football. Teaches the team football, teaches the team everything, you know? That’s going to be more of a group effort than ever. It’s not going to all fall on me. As far as certain things, we’ll all take a piece, and that’s how this thing’s going to be done. Truly, when John said what the release said, that listed my name but then said it’s going to be done by all the assistants.” Foerster was asked when he knew he'd be temporarily in charge. “When did the statement come out?" Foerster said. "That's when I saw my name, OK? That's when I saw my name. I knew that we'd all have to pick up the slack. So, I knew that once Kyle wasn't — we didn't know. You just don't know. Every day the thing could flip and he can do more and more. So we just don't know how it's going to be. So when I saw my name on it, I said, ‘Oh, OK. It's going to be that.’ But it was going to be the group effort. We always knew that. We were talking for days before. 'What if he couldn't do it?' Klay, Kyle, Raheem, Boyer and I, we were all talking about how we could fill in the blanks if needed. And then obviously yesterday they said, ‘You’re going to be doing the pressers.’ I said, ‘Well, I don't think I'm doing the pressers.’ And then, well, here I am, so.” He was nevertheless "fired up" to learn he had gotten the assignment. "Not from the standpoint of 'I'm fired up' from the standpoint of, ‘Oh, Kyle's down, this is my big chance.’ No, it's I love the opportunity to help. What I learned a long, long time ago, I believe leadership is you serve in leadership. You help people by serving. And servant leadership is any way I can help. Any way I can help Kyle, any way I can help the 49ers, any way I can help John Lynch, any way I can help my players. Any way I can help you guys. Anything I can do to help. That's where I get a charge out of life. I learned that through a lot of difficult times in my life, being that way. So this is another opportunity to stand up here. And you guys that were here before, I like getting up here and talking about football. It's not about me. I like talking ball. I like sharing football. I think it's a great game, it's a great sport and a lot of people don't understand it. And if you have a chance to learn a little more, I like to talk about it because I love the game.” He said that Shanahan told him, "'Hey, you do whatever you want. I have a lot of confidence in you. You know how we do things. You do whatever you want to do and if you don't want to do it, delegate it to somebody else, man.’ He said, ‘You just do what you feel is right and lead that way.’ He said, ‘I trust that you'll do anything you want to do and anything you want to delegate, delegate.'" Foerster began delegating on Sunday. "I delegated this morning's team meeting out to offense and defense," Foerster said. "We decided to do it that way today instead of doing a team meeting. And we'll see as we go each week, each day what it is. That’s about it right now." It really is unclear how long it will take for Shanahan to return. Foerster may have committed an unintended slip by saying "each week." This suggests it may not be a short absence for Shanahan. At this point, the duration isn't known. It all depends on how long it takes for Shanahan's concussion symptoms to clear. Until then, Foerster is running the show. But he has made it clear he'll be leaning on others to help fill Shanahan's void.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals, Jacoby Brissett strike a new deal
summary: Brissett reportedly will have a base salary of $15.5 million with a max payout of $21 million.
full_text: ' The Cardinals and quarterback Jacoby Brissett have resolved their differences. Via ESPN, the team and Brissett have reached an agreement on a new deal. Brissett signed a two-year deal in 2025 to serve as Kyler Murray's backup. Brissett was thrust into the starting role during the regular season. He entered 2026 as the default QB1. And so he needed to be paid that way. Ian Rapoport of ESPN reports that Brissett will have base compensation of $15.5 million , with a chance to make $21 million. Even with the upside, it's the low end of the veteran starter scale. But it's much more than the $6.5 million APY under his prior deal. Brissett didn't hold out of training camp, but he hadn't been participating in 11-on-11 drills. Now, he'll start putting in the work to be the starter for the coming season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams place G Justin Dedich on NFI list, DB Al'zillion Hamilton on PUP list
summary: The Rams opened training camp this weekend, but a couple of players aren't ready to practice at this point.
full_text: ' The Rams opened training camp this weekend, but a couple of players aren't ready to practice at this point. The team announced that they have placed guard Justin Dedich on the non-football injury list. Defensive back Al'zillion Hamilton is on the physically unable to perform list and both of the players can be activated at any point this summer. Dedich appeared in 16 games and made six starts for the Rams last season. He also played in all three of their playoff contests and started against the Panthers in the wild card round. Hamilton signed with the Rams after going undrafted out of Fresno State this year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos put LB Jordan Turner on NFI, G Nick Gargiulo on PUP
summary: The Broncos announced a pair of roster moves on Sunday.
full_text: '' The Broncos announced a pair of roster moves on Sunday. Linebacker Jordan Turner has been placed on the non-football injury list and guard Nick Gargiulo has been placed on the physically unable to perform list. Both players still count against the 90-man roster and can be activated at any point in training camp. The Broncos have their first practice of camp on Wednesday. Turner signed with Denver after going undrafted last year. He appeared in seven regular season games and two playoff contests while seeing the majority of his playing time on special teams. He had eight tackles in those contests. Gargiulo was a 2024 seventh-round pick, but has not played in any regular season or postseason games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots put Gabe Jacas on non-football injury list
summary: The Patriots signed second-round pick Gabe Jacas this weekend, but the rookie is not ready to start practicing with the team.
full_text: ' The Patriots signed second-round pick Gabe Jacas this weekend, but the rookie is not ready to start practicing with the team. Jacas was placed on the team's non-football injury list on Sunday. Jacas missed offseason work while dealing with injuries, including a knee issue that required surgical intervention. The linebacker will not practice with the team until he's off the list and he can be activated at any time. The Patriots put Harold Landry on the physically unable to perform list last week, so they are without a pair of their pass rushing options in the early days of training camp. The team also announced that wide receiver Jeremiah Webb was placed on injured reserve to create space for Jacas on the active roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions place Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph on PUP list
summary: A pair of safeties are set to start Lions training camp on the physically unable to perform list.
full_text: A pair of safeties are set to start Lions training camp on the physically unable to perform list. The team announced on Sunday that Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph have both been placed on the list. Tight end Tyler Conklin is also on the list as the team nears their first practices of the summer. Branch tore his Achilles last December and head coach Dan Campbell said in June that he has not had any setbacks in his recovery. Campbell declined to set a target date for his return to action, however. Joseph missed 11 games with a knee injury in 2025. Campbell said "I honestly do not know " when Joseph will be back when he gave his most recent update on the safety's condition.
author: Josh Alper

title: After OWI arrest, Tony Romo withdraws from Texas State Open
summary: Tony Romo has yet to say anything publicly since Thursday's arrest in Milwaukee for suspicion of operating while intoxicated.
full_text: Tony Romo has yet to say anything publicly since Thursday’s arrest in Milwaukee for suspicion of operating while intoxicated. For now, his actions are doing the talking. Via Michael Garcia of KETK, Romo has withdrawn from this week's Texas State Open. It will be held at the Cascades Country Club in Tyler, starting on Tuesday, July 28. The club confirmed that Romo has removed himself from the event. His arrest happened after he competed in a golf event in the Milwaukee area. The former Cowboys quarterback and CBS analyst is due in court on September 21. He was arrested after performing poorly in standard field sobriety testing. It's still unclear whether he submitted to breath testing. Romo has previously participated in the Texas State Open nine times .
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike LaFleur on Jacoby Brissett deal: Now we can move on with football
summary: Brissett is set to start practicing with the first team on Tuesday.
full_text: ' Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett's bid for a new contract ended on Sunday. Brissett is now set to make a base salary of $15.5 million, which better reflects his standing as the team's likely No. 1 quarterback to open the 2026 season. Head coach Mike LaFleur did not commit to Brissett serving in that role, but he said he will be working with the starters when the team holds its first padded practice of the summer on Tuesday. LaFleur also said that he's happy to eliminate a reason to think or talk about anything other than football. "It hasn't been a distraction by any means ," LaFleur said, via the team's website. "We have very much mature and professional players. We have a mature roster. Never thought it was ever a distraction but it's one less thing we have to talk about, or that they have to read about. We can move on with the football aspect of it." Brissett's contract stance kept him away from the team for the voluntary portion of the offseason program, but the Cardinals will be banking on his experience helping him to streamline the process of getting acclimated to the offense ahead of Week 1.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jerry Jeudy pushes back against characterization of video regarding QB preference
summary: On Sunday, a video emerged that purported to show Browns receiver Jerry Jeudy stating his preference at quarterback.
full_text: On Sunday, a video emerged that purported to show Browns receiver Jerry Jeudy stating his preference at quarterback. Jeudy has responded to the viral clip. First, it's important to watch the video . There's a skip. After the question appears on the screen regarding his choice at the position, the image jumps. After the edit, Jeudy flashes four fingers, which is being interpreted as Jeudy wanting Deshaun Watson to get the job over Shedeur Sanders. Here's what Jeudy had to say, on Twitter: "I don’t speak on decisions that aren’t mine to make. I support my teammates/Brothers, I do my job, and control what I can control. Let’s stop creating narrative that aren’t there for likes and clicks. I bet this won’t go viral because it’s too positive/real for y’all." Again, the video isn't reliable. It skips before Jeudy holds up four fingers. He could have been answering any question. It's impossible to conclude with any degree of certainty that he was answering the question of which quarterback he prefers. And he's right. It's not his decision to make. Why would he state a preference before training camp even opens? Jeudy needs to be ready to work with, and get targeted by, whoever wins the job.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaguars place OL Cole Van Lanen on PUP list
summary: The Jaguars put a pair of offensive linemen on their physically unable to perform list ahead of the start of their training camp.
full_text: ' The Jaguars put a pair of offensive linemen on their physically unable to perform list ahead of the start of their training camp. They announced that Cole Van Lanen and Garret DiGiorgio have been placed on the list. Both players will be ineligible to practice until they are off of it and they can be activated at any time. Van Lanen closed out the 2025 regular season as the team's starting left tackle, but he injured his knee in Week 18. He started 10 games overall and has played 50 games for Jacksonville over the last four seasons. DiGiorgio started at guard and tackle while at UCLA. He signed with the Jaguars after going undrafted this year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Signing with Washington "intriguing" to Stefon Diggs
summary: A recent report indicated five teams have been keeping tabs on free agent wide receiver Stefon Diggs heading into free agency and there's now word of a team that has caught Diggs's eye.
full_text: A recent report indicated five teams have been keeping tabs on free agent wide receiver Stefon Diggs heading into free agency and there's now word of a team that has caught Diggs's eye. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that the prospect of joining the Commanders is " intriguing " to the veteran wideout. The presence of quarterback Jayden Daniels is a major part of the draw for Diggs, who grew up outside Washington in Maryland and attended college at the University of Maryland. There's no word if the Commanders share the interest, but they have been linked to a possible move for Brandon Aiyuk throughout the offseason. That's unlikely to happen as long as Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' reserve list , however, and Diggs is another option to upgrade the No. 2 receiver spot alongside Terry McLaurin in their offense. Diggs caught 85 passes for 1,013 yards and four touchdowns with the Patriots last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Trent Williams: Nick Bosa looks better than he did before he tore his ACL
summary: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa avoided the physically unable to perform list to open training camp and his performance in the first day of practice impressed one of his longtime teammates.
full_text: ' 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa avoided the physically unable to perform list to open training camp and his performance in the first day of practice impressed one of his longtime teammates. Bosa tore his ACL in Week 3 of the 2025 season, but left tackle Trent Williams said on Sunday that one wouldn't know that from watching him on the field. "I see him every day, I can’t tell he had an injury and came back from anything," Williams said, via Cam Inman of the Bay Area News Group. "Most people with an injury that catastrophic, you can see it with something, like with atrophy in leg. Bosa looks better than he did before he got hurt .” It's the third time that Bosa has recovered from a torn ACL — he tore his right one for the second time last season — and that experience likely helped him with his approach to this round of rehab. Williams's review suggests that experience could pay off for the 49ers defense come September.
author: Josh Alper

title: Fernando Mendoza: I'm competing with, not against, Kirk Cousins
summary: Fernando Mendoza signed his rookie deal last week and that leaves the quarterback with nothing to focus on other than football when the Raiders open training camp this week.
full_text: ' Fernando Mendoza signed his rookie deal last week and that leaves the quarterback with nothing to focus on other than football when the Raiders open training camp this week. The first overall pick will continue to learn head coach Klint Kubiak's offense while, per a recent report, getting a sprinkling of work with the first team. Kirk Cousins is expected to get the rest of the work with the starters and one of the storylines of Raiders camp will be whether the rookie can push past the veteran to become the team's starter. During an appearance on the team's Upon Further Review podcast, Mendoza cast that competition as a cooperative effort by saying that they will "be competing with each other, not competing against each other" over the coming weeks. "Competing with each other [is] pushing each other to be the best quarterback we can possibly be for the Las Vegas Raiders, and to enable [us] to then win as many games as possible," Mendoza said. "Against [is] withholding information, wishing maybe not the best intent on somebody." The team's upcoming practices will show how open the competition for the top job in Las Vegas will be this summer and Mendoza will have to make the most of his time as a backup if that is how things play out to start his career. He said that "there's just so many different intricacies" to the offense and that he's looking forward to the chance to learn from Cousins, Kubiak and anyone else who has something to offer. "It's basically all in the palm of my hand and I just need to take advantage of it," Mendoza said. The Raiders' future is pinned to Mendoza making the most of the chances that come his way and this summer's work is going to be centered on making sure he's as ready as possible whenever they do call his number.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nathaniel Hackett's "definitely a rookie" remark about Jeremiyah Love is getting overblown
summary: We're in the business of finding and sharing and analyzing interesting remarks from anyone in the NFL ecosystem.
full_text: '' We're in the business of finding and sharing and analyzing interesting remarks from anyone in the NFL ecosystem. But certain supposedly controversial comments aren't really as big of a deal as some may interpret them to be. Case in point: Cardinals offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett is catching some heat for comments he made on Saturday about rookie running back Jeremiyah Love. "He's definitely a rookie , and — as we've talked about," Hackett said. "And he'll keep growing every single day. I'm very excited for him. All those guys. Not just him." The broader context has to be considered, especially since Hackett specifically added "as we've talked about." Earlier in the session, Hackett addressed the challenges that first-year players face when training camp opens. The question related to the things that are different for rookies. "Everything you can imagine," Hackett said. "I mean, coming to this league is — I mean, just the speed is so different. You talk about the speed, being in a new building. . . . [I]t's a whole new environment. New people to work with, and definitely new playbooks that are very, very intricate. Due to the fact of all the things that we see and all the different — I mean, just our defense out there. I mean, you get almost everything and more. Which is great, because it helps you for the season, but for a young player to have to be able to adjust and learn just basic system and then apply it to different defenses. It takes some time. So heads are spinning right now, especially after two days, but I think it'll just get better and better. That's the goal." Hackett wasn't dismissing or minimizing Love. He's a rookie. Like the rest of the rookies. Everything is different. Everything is new. "Heads are spinning," as Hackett said. Training camp is the time to slow, and eventually to stop, the spinning. They have plenty of time to get Love ready to go. For now, after only two days, he's beginning the adjustment. That's all it means. Which makes the comment not nearly as alarming as some are making it out to be.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers bring back DL Kevin Givens
summary: Defensive lineman Kevin Givens spent the last seven seasons with the 49ers and he'll have a chance to make it eight in a row.
full_text: Defensive lineman Kevin Givens spent the last seven seasons with the 49ers and he'll have a chance to make it eight in a row. The 49ers announced that they have signed Givens to their 90-man roster on Sunday. Defensive lineman Evan Anderson was waived in a corresponding move. Givens signed with the 49ers as an undrafted free agent in 2019. He played in one game as a rookie, but saw action in 65 regular season and playoff games over the next four years. He played in eight games in 2024 and had two tackles in five appearances last year. Givens has 104 tackles, 18 tackles for loss, 8.5 sacks, a forced fumble and two fumble recoveries across all the games he's played for the 49ers and will try to add to that total this fall.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ed Policy: Packers will bring more "major events" to Lambeau Field
summary: On Friday, Packers president and CEO Ed Policy reiterated his concern about the basic financial differences between a publicly-owned team and the 31 privately-held franchises.
full_text: '' On Friday, Packers president and CEO Ed Policy reiterated his concern about the basic financial differences between a publicly-owned team and the 31 privately-held franchises. The situation raises the stakes for the Packers when it comes to finding ways to raise money. One easy way to do that is to have more events at Lambeau Field. Policy said that's coming. "We are focusing on having more major events — non-Packers games at Lambeau Field," Policy said, via Kelly Hallinan of NBC 26. "They're good for us. They do generate revenue, but they're also great for our community and for the regional and local economy. "We do want to focus a little more on college football games and premier soccer games. They're just a little bit easier on our field and easier for the field to bounce back from. But we will host concerts from time to time. We're very pleased with the Luke Combs concert. It was actually two back-to-back concerts that we held for the first time in Lambeau Field, and we hosted, I believe, approximately 93,000 people. "So we are putting more effort toward those events. Very excited about having the Notre Dame-Wisconsin game coming here on September 6th. But we'll continue to look at those. There'll be college football games, premier soccer games, there could be a winter event coming up. We'll see, we're working on that potentially." Policy mentioned the field. The Packers do a great job, in a bad climate, of keeping their field pristine. They'll need to be able to keep doing that. But it's a way to make more money that doesn't make it more expensive to attend Packers games — and that doesn't entail selling the naming rights to Lambeau Field. Which the Packers absolutely do. It's found money. It's a lost opportunity. And even though some regard Lambeau Field as hallowed ground, Green Bay Packers, Inc. isn't a religion. It's a business. And it should behave like one, especially if the person in charge of the business is worried that changes to how NFL business is done could eventually give the Packers the business.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers are cooperating with NFLPA investigation of Nic Scourton's ACL tear
summary: On the first day of 2026 training-camp practice, Panthers linebacker Nic Scourton suffered a season-ending ACL tear.
full_text: ' On the first day of 2026 training-camp practice, Panthers linebacker Nic Scourton suffered a season-ending ACL tear. Given that it happened during the mandatory, five-day acclimation period, the NFL Players Association is investigating the situation . Via Mike Kaye of the Charlotte Observer , a Panthers spokesperson said on Sunday morning that the team is aware of the situation and will cooperate with the NFLPA . The investigation begins, and possibly ends, with a review of the video of the injury. That will show whether Scourton was doing something that the CBA prohibits in the early days of training camp. The rules aren't nearly as specific as they could be. Some have suggested that this would be an occasion to create more precise standards aimed at giving players who have been away from football for more than a month a chance to ease their bodies back into practicing, before the pedal is fully pressed against the metal. If Scourton's injury happened under circumstances that comply with the current rules of the five-day acclimation period (and there's currently no reason to think otherwise), the mere fact that an ACL tear happened so early in the process suggests that there should be tighter restrictions for the first official day that the players are practicing. Everyone should want that — players, teams, and the league. The best players should be available to play in as many games as possible. While injuries are inevitable when the games are played, no player should ever be lost for the entire season during a no-contact practice to open camp.
author: Mike Florio

title: Despite no second contract, Puka Nacua apparently won't be holding in
summary: Off-field issue complicates Nacua's effort to get a new deal.
full_text: The current Collective Bargaining Agreement makes it harder than ever for a player who wants a new contract to hold out. As a result, the vast majority of players who are waiting for their next deal will hold in, showing up for training camp but not risking injury at practice until the ink is drying on the last page. Rams receiver Puka Nacua, who has had three stellar seasons and who is little more than seven months away from free agency, apparently won't be holding in. “Oh, he'll practice, yes," coach Sean McVay told reporters on Saturday when asked about Nacua. "My understanding is everybody's going to practice and be ready to go." Nacua is due to make $5.767 million this year. Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, drafted the same year as Nacua, has gotten a contract that pays a record-setting $42.15 million annually. Complicating Nacua's situation is the off-field issues that emerged during the offseason. It has put Nacua in a far different posture. He's grateful for the support he has gotten from the Rams. And if he's not extremely leery about what could happen with the civil lawsuit alleging that he bit a woman on New Year's Eve, he should be. The latest reporting on the case mentioned the possibility of Nacua entering a diversion program, which would open the door to a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy. That fact alone significantly complicates Nacua's negotiations with the Rams. A suspension would likely void his guarantees, unless the contract specifically carves out the incident that gave rise to the lawsuit and potential diversion program. Even if the Rams would be willing to do that, such a concession will come with a price, likely in the form of less total money under the contract. Regardless, Nacua has far greater value than $5.767 million. He has been every bit as good, if not better, than Smith-Njigba. At Nacua's best, no receiver in the NFL is better. Surely, efforts have been made by Nacua's agents to get him the security he has earned. But if the security is going to come with an asterisk due to the lingering off-field problem, it's not really security. Nacua's only viable option is to move forward. To have another great year. To hope that his incredibly physical style doesn't lead to an injury that hampers his long-term value. And to hope that the off-field situation can be wrapped up efficiently and as favorably as possible, so that he can get the contract he already deserves after the 2026 season. Unless, of course, the Rams decide to take advantage of a franchise tag that, for receivers, falls far below market value. The situation reveals the very real financial consequences of off-field misconduct, alleged or actual. Even if Nacua is fully cleared, the mere existence of the allegation has bogged down his effort to receive the contract his performance merits, and it forces him to play for less than he's worth while risking the kind of injury that would keep him from ever getting paid the way he already should be.
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons put sixth-rounder Anterio Thompson on NFI list
summary: The Falcons are gearing up for the start of training camp later this week and part of their preparation includes a roster move involving one of their draft picks.
full_text: '' The Falcons are gearing up for the start of training camp later this week and part of their preparation includes a roster move involving one of their draft picks. The NFL's daily transaction report for Saturday shows that they placed defensive tackle Anterio Thompson on the non-football injury list. Thompson was a sixth-round pick in April. Thompson played at Iowa, Western Michigan and Washington over the last three seasons. He had 30 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks for the Huskies in 2025. Falcons rookies reported to camp on Friday. Veterans are due on Tuesday with the first practice of camp scheduled for Wednesday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ranking QB changes by expected impact: Can Kyler Murray get Vikings back to the playoffs?
summary: From Kirk Cousins in Las Vegas to Malik Willis in Miami, we rank the impact of the five new starting quarterbacks set to take over in 2026
full_text:
Quarterback is the most criticized position in the NFL , which is why multiple franchises find new starters every offseason. Last year, the Tennessee Titans , New York Giants and New Orleans Saints drafted players they hope can be the face of their respective franchises in the near future, while the Indianapolis Colts took a swing on Daniel Jones to replace Anthony Richardson . We also saw the Seattle Seahawks sign Sam Darnold , who ultimately helped them win Super Bowl LX.
In 2026, there are expected to be five new starters at the quarterback position. Several of these players will have to earn the top spot on the depth chart, but they were brought in for a reason. The Minnesota Vikings, for example, expect to make the playoffs every season, and Kevin O'Connell is hoping his new quarterback can spark a turnaround. Then there are teams like the Las Vegas Raiders , who completely revamped their quarterback room as they begin a new era.
Which of these new signal-callers are set up for success in 2026? Below, we will rank the quarterback changes by expected impact, and give some projected final stats courtesy of the CBS Sports fantasy football team.
CBS Sports' fantasy football projected statline for Malik Willis : 3,096 passing yards, 25 TDs, 17 INTs
I think an interesting question is: what are the expectations for Malik Willis this season? It's not to get the Miami Dolphins to the Super Bowl, or the playoffs, or even to have a winning record. I also wonder what the chances are that Miami drafts a quarterback somewhere early in the first round next year. It appears to be a loaded class with players like Arch Manning, Dante Moore, CJ Carr and others.
The Dolphins are expected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL this season, as they have the second-longest Super Bowl odds at virtually every sportsbook. Willis has a star running back in De'Von Achane , but is throwing to Malik Washington , Jalen Tolbert , Tutu Atwell and Greg Dulcich . It doesn't look like a great situation.
Some Willis fans probably believe he can power this offense by himself, but we only have a small sample size to work with when analyzing him. The former third-round pick out of Liberty started one game last season for the Green Bay Packers , which they lost to the Baltimore Ravens , 41-24. Still, Willis completed 18 of 21 passes for 288 yards and one touchdown, while also leading the team in rushing with 60 yards and two more touchdowns. According to CBS Sports Research, he became the first quarterback to ever complete 85% of his passes while averaging 13 yards per attempt, and rush for 60 yards in a game (min. 20 pass attempts). Willis also became the first quarterback since Michael Vick in 2002 to throw for 100 yards and a touchdown in a first half with zero incompletions, and rush for a touchdown.
Willis didn't put up as massive numbers in his two starts with Green Bay back in 2024, but did win both games. Willis accounted for three touchdowns and zero turnovers in those starts. He proved he could run Matt LaFleur's system, and it will be up to offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik to make life easier for him.
CBS Sports' fantasy projected statline : 2,934 passing yards, 24 TDs, 16 INTs
The New York Jets had arguably the worst quarterback situation last season. The starter they brought in, Justin Fields , went 2-7 while averaging 6.2 yards per attempt. The Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos in London, where Fields threw for just 45 yards, set the sport of football back decades. Backup quarterback Tyrod Taylor won just one of his four starts, then rookie Brady Cook lost all four of his starts.
The Jets now turn to a familiar face in Geno Smith, who is coming off one of the worst seasons of his 13-year career. Not only did the 35-year-old go 2-13 as the Raiders' starter, but he also led the league in sacks taken (55) and interceptions (17). It was a disaster, but I would argue that Smith is upgrading his situation, going from Sin City to New York.
The Jets definitely have a better offensive line than the Raiders did in 2025, with Olu Fashanu, Dylan Parham , Josh Myers , Joe Tippmann and Armand Membou . The Jets also have legit weaponry with Breece Hall , Garrett Wilson , Omar Cooper Jr . and Kenyon Sadiq . I certainly don't view Smith as one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL, but I do view him as an obvious upgrade from what the Jets had last year. He had two 4,200-yard passing seasons in three years with the Seahawks. If Smith can just rely on his playmakers and take care of the football, the Jets will average more than 263 yards of total offense in 2026.
CBS Sports' fantasy projected statline : 3,460 passing yards, 24 TDs, 10 INTs
There is a quarterback battle going on in Atlanta, but Michael Penix Jr. is coming off a third ACL tear, while the Falcons quickly pursued and signed Tua Tagovailoa . The CBS Sports fantasy team believes Tagovailoa is going to see extensive action in 2026 compared to Penix.
When paired with Mike McDaniel, Tagovailoa looked like an efficient point guard for a high-powered passing attack. Most of the time. His 44 wins were the most by a Dolphins quarterback since Dan Marino retired, and he led the NFL in passer rating in 2022, passing yards in 2023 and completion percentage in 2024. Then, last season happened. Tagovailoa threw a career-high 15 interceptions and averaged 6.9 yards per attempt, which was his worst mark with McDaniel.
Tagovailoa went 4-14 vs. teams with a winning record under McDaniel, and has clearly regressed since that big 2023 season. That's why it was a bit curious that the Falcons immediately pursued Tagovailoa as soon as the Dolphins swallowed an NFL-record $99 million dead cap hit just to cut him. With that said, all Kevin Stefanski wants is an effective point guard to run his offense, because it's full of talented playmakers such as Bijan Robinson , Drake London and Kyle Pitts . Can Tagovailoa play that role? We'll find out.
CBS Sports' fantasy projected statline for Kirk Cousins : 674 passing yards, 5 TDs, 4 INTs Fernando Mendoza's fantasy projected statline : 2,630 passing yards, 19 TDs, 16 INTs
The Raiders had one of their worst seasons in franchise history last year, finishing 3-14 under Pete Carroll, ranking dead last in scoring offense (14.2 points per game) and total offense (245.2 yards per game). Carroll's gamble to bring in Geno Smith did not work, as he threw more interceptions (17) than any quarterback in the NFL.
As we enter 2026, it's fair to hypothesize that the Raiders upgraded their quarterback room in a major way. Vegas signed veteran Kirk Cousins in free agency and drafted former Indiana star and college football legend Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick. The Raiders are expected to start Cousins to begin the season -- and perhaps their best-case scenario is if Cousins starts the entire year. If Cousins plays out the year, you can assume that means the Raiders were competitive and their quarterback was playing well enough to keep Mendoza on the bench. However, some believe Mendoza should start right away. Doug Pederson made an interesting case .
Cousins is coming off an overall disappointing two seasons with the Falcons, in which he went 12-10 as the starter, but he did step in for Michael Penix Jr . last season and help Atlanta end the year on a four-game win streak. Cousins averaged 219 passing yards per game and threw seven touchdowns compared to two interceptions during that stretch. He's about to turn 38-years-old, but Cousins showed he can still run an offense.
As for Mendoza, I'm not sure he was viewed as a generational, can't-miss prospect. But he was just the fourth player in the Common Draft Era to be selected No. 1 overall after winning the Heisman Trophy and a National Championship, joining Joe Burrow , Jameis Winston and Cam Newton . Mendoza led Indiana to a perfect 16-0 record. Pretty remarkable.
Our fantasy football projections indicate that Cousins will not be playing many games before…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Cardinals, Jacoby Brissett agree to one-year deal for $15.5 million, per report
summary: The deal could reach $21 million for the signal caller
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals have secured their starting quarterback. The Cardinals and veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett have agreed on a deal that will increase his 2026 compensation to $15.5 million guaranteed and up to $21 million with incentives, according to ESPN. The deal is a jump from the $4.88 million in base salary he was scheduled to make this season on year two of a two-year deal with the team.
The deal increased the number on the check, but did not add any years to the deal, meaning the 33-year-old is still set to become an unrestricted free agent after the 2026 season.
Brissett, who joined the Cardinals in 2025, skipped most of the team's offseason program as he sought out a new deal. As the team's practices began this week, he participated but did not do 11-on-11 drills. Cardinals coach Mike LeFleur said, despite missing time with the team, he feels confident in Brissett's understanding of the offense, as they look to bounce back from their 3-14 record last season.
"He's a smart dude, he's played a lot of football," LaFleur said . "It's learning a whole different language. I'm not going to put any kind of (timeline) on that. ... I like where he's at from a learning standpoint."
Last season, Brissett started 12 of the 14 games he appeared in, going 1-11 in those starts. It marked the most starts for the veteran since 2019, coming in for an injured Kyler Murray , who was released by Arizona and joined the Minnesota Vikings this offseason. Brissett finished the 2025 season with 3,366 passing yards, 23 touchdowns, a career high, and eight interceptions.
With Murray, the 2019 No. 1 overall pick, now off the depth chart, Brissett will be the team's starter heading into Week 1, after beginning last season as QB2. The team also has Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck in the QB room.
The Cardinals are Brissett's sixth team and seventh time moving squads, having done two stints with the New England Patriots , who drafted him at No. 91 overall in 2016. He played for the Indianapolis Colts from 2017 to 2020, spent one year with the Miami Dolphins , Cleveland Browns and Washington Commanders and then had a one-year second stint with New England in 2024.
Brissett holds the NFL record for the most completions in a regular-season game with 47, accomplished in 2025 with the Cardinals.
The Cardinals will begin their regular season on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 13.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: What happened to Brandon Aiyuk? How ex-All-Pro went from $120 million to on the outside looking in on NFL
summary: Aiyuk played just seven games for the 49ers after signing a massive extension in 2024
full_text:
It's been more than 600 days since Brandon Aiyuk last played an NFL game. The then-49ers star, just a few months removed from signing a four-year, $120 million deal, tore his ACL and MCL and suffered other knee damage when his knee hyperextended on an awkward hit in a Week 7, 2024 contest against the Chiefs .
Aiyuk's journey since has been anything but straightforward and has featured beefs with San Francisco, his now-ex agent, the NFLPA, Commanders quarterback (and former Arizona State teammate) Jayden Daniels . Aiyuk has been mostly closely tied to Washington this offseason as the team has no proven wide receivers behind Terry McLaurin .
The 49ers reported to camp for the 2026 season, and Aiyuk is once again absent. On Saturday, GM John Lynch offered an update on the situation, which only reinforced that it doesn't seem likely he'll be making his return anytime in the near future, as Aiyuk is still on the 'left squad' list, and Lynch didn't have much else to say about the receiver.
"I'm personally, and we as an organization, are going to focus on the players who are here," Lynch said. "We wish him well, we wish his family well."
As Aiyuk, 28, continues to wander a very strange and unique out-of-the-NFL wilderness, here's what made him such a good player, what caused his downfall and what's next.
The No. 25 pick in the 2020 NFL Draft , Aiyuk had an uneven start to his professional career. He caught 60 passes for 748 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie but was nearly invisible to start his second year, landing in Kyle Shanahan's doghouse.
"We know Aiyuk can be a weapon," Shanahan said in October 2021 . "That's why we've got him here. I'm a big fan of Aiyuk, but he's not there yet. He's still coming along. At times, he does it at a high level. We just want him to be a little bit more consistent, and I think his time will come. It's a matter of time."
Slowly but surely, Aiyuk worked his way out of the situation; he had 43 catches for 685 yards and four touchdowns over the team's final seven games of the regular season. Ahead of his third season, Aiyuk attributed the stop-and-start nature of the beginning of his career, in part, to the strange circumstances . Drafted amid the COVID-19 pandemic, Aiyuk spent limited time with the team ahead of his rookie year and admitted he didn't realize how hard he needed to work entering his second season.
Aiyuk posted what was then his best year as a pro -- 78 catches for 1,015 yards and eight touchdowns -- in 2022 and then truly broke out in 2023: 75 catches, 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. He earned second-team All-Pro honors. He is still the most recent player to have over 1,300 receiving yards on at least 17 yards per catch in a season. Beyond the box score numbers, ESPN rated him as the No. 1 overall pass catcher in its receiver metrics (based on "open," "catch" and "YAC" scores), and he was the No. 2 wide receiver per Pro Football Focus' grades.
1,300 receiving yards on 17+ yards per reception -- since 2020
The film matches all the numbers.
Aiyuk's ability to dominate over the middle of the field and win contested-catch balls on the perimeter made him a near-impossible player to guard. He looked like a dominant player on one of the NFL's best teams going forward.
After his All-Pro 2023, Aiyuk sought a contract extension heading into the fifth-year option season of his rookie deal. The entire process, though, was shaky at best. In March, GM John Lynch talked about wanting to keep Aiyuk long-term, but Aiyuk was unimpressed, posting, essentially, "Money talks, bullshit walks" on his Instagram story . In June, Aiyuk posted a video in which he told Daniels over FaceTime the 49ers "don't want [him] back."
Aiyuk demanded a trade in mid-July and began a training camp hold-in . The 49ers even reportedly had trade frameworks in place to send him to the Patriots or Browns , but Aiyuk did not accept the terms of a potential contract either team would offer. Eventually, in late August, Aiyuk signed a four-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers. At $30 million per season, it tied the fifth-largest average annual value for a wide receiver contract at the time.
Then came a slow start -- missing all of the preseason essentially didn't help, and there was even a clash with Shanahan regarding wearing the wrong shorts to practice -- and the knee injury.
Fast forward to 2025, and Shanahan never delivered a firm timeline on Aiyuk's potential return. Then, in November, The Athletic reported the 49ers had voided the $27 million of 2026 salary guarantees owed to Aiyuk due to the wide receiver failing to meet the obligations in his contract.
In December, the 49ers put Aiyuk on the reserve/left team list. Shanahan said he hadn't seen Aiyuk "in forever" and that Aiyuk had been "extremely distant." George Kittle relayed similar sentiments . Later that month, Aiyuk posted a video of himself driving 104 mph in a 40-mph zone near the 49ers' stadium. Aiyuk later apologized . In early June 2026, the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office issued a warrant for his arrest on a misdemeanor speeding charge .
In January 2026, Lynch said "I think it's safe to say he's played his last snap with the 49ers," regarding Aiyuk, days after the 49ers' season ended in the playoffs.
In free agency, the 49ers signed wide receivers Mike Evans and Christian Kirk . Following the NFL Draft, in which the 49ers drafted wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling , Lynch indicated he wouldn't just let Aiyuk walk without at least trying to find a trade partner and expressed no hurry to release the disgruntled wide receiver.
"Give us a call," Lynch said. "I think it's the prudent thing to do. He's an extremely talented player. He's been an extremely effective player in our league. The situation didn't work itself out here. That's not to say it can't be rekindled somewhere else. And we'd be happy to do something with anyone if the opportunity presented itself."
The 49ers' reluctance to release Aiyuk, though, has frustrated Aiyuk, and he aired that frustration throughout June, first calling the 49ers "little-ass boys" during one rant posted to Instagram. In another video, posted a few days later, Aiyuk called the 49ers "stupid."
"They mad 'cause they stupid," Aiyuk said. "They dumb. They mad that they paid me $50 million in eight months and then voided my guarantees for 2027. And I'm about to be on a new team in 2027. They mad at themselves for real. They acting like they mad at me, but they stupid ass mad at themselves."
Then, a few weeks later, Aiyuk posted a video repeatedly saying "Go Commanders," even while technically still on the 49ers. Aiyuk also posted, on other occasions, that his former agent (officially fired in June ) helped cause the strained situation, that Lynch showed up to his house and that the NFLPA did not give him adequate support.
All the while, Aiyuk still hadn't applied for reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list; he needed to first be reinstated before he and the 49ers could technically part ways. On July 2, Aiyuk posted a video of himself dancing with the caption "Mood cuz Im gone [sic] be a Commander soon."
Of course, that couldn't possibly be true, especially because a few days later, Aiyuk posted, "I will not be reinstating with [the 49ers] nor ever doing any kind of business with them."
He has recently been calling out Daniels -- seemingly his best and most important connection with Washington -- on social media while insisting he will land with the Commanders. Aiyuk also recently attacked the NFLPA , seemingly implying that the union did not have his back in his dispute with the 49ers and attempt to engineer his way to Washington.
Before he can land anywhere, though -- or even before teams can really consider trying to land him -- he must apply for reinstatement and be reinstated. Until then, he is no closer to returning to a football field than he has been for the past several months.
Aiyuk would be far from the first player…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Kyle Shanahan injured in car accident: 49ers coach to begin training camp in limited role
summary: Reports say Shanahan suffered a broken nose, three broken ribs, a broken hand, a concussion and required more than 40 stitches to his face after the July 14 crash
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have officially reported to training camp but will begin building the foundation for the 2026 campaign with their head coach limited. The team announced in a statement Saturday that Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week and suffered non-life-threatening injuries.
Shanahan, 46, will still participate in team activities, but on a limited basis. Assistant head coach Chris Foerster and the team coordinators will handle the bulk of the head coach duties while Shanahan recuperates. In a press conference on Saturday, 49ers general manager John Lynch told reporters that he does not expect Shanahan to miss Week 1 of the regular season.
Here is the full official statement from the 49ers:
"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care.
Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle head coach responsibilities during this period."
The accident occurred July 14 when Shanahan collided with an SUV near his Northern California home, per ESPN . While the injuries weren't life-threatening, they were significant. ESPN reported that Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs and his hand, suffered a severe concussion and needed more than 40 stitches to his face.
Shanahan was taken by paramedics to a local hospital and released later that day. The other driver was not injured, according to Palo Alto Lt. Nicholas Martinez. He also told ESPN that drugs and alcohol were not involved, and both drivers cooperated with law enforcement.
Since the crash, Shanahan has been recovering at home and informed the coaching staff of the incident on Tuesday. He has yet to be cleared by doctors for full coaching duties and won't be until his concussion symptoms subside.
Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay, who worked with Shanahan when they were assistants in Washington, said he's spoken to the 49ers coach since the car accident. McVay, a fellow NFC West coach, said Shanahan has a great perspective on the accident and on his recovery.
"I have talked to him. My thoughts and prayers are with him and his family, and I know he's got an incredible perspective on it all. And Kyle's a stud. I have as much respect for him as anybody and he's a friend of mine, and I love him and hope that he's going to have a great recovery," McVay said .
McVay expressed gratitude that the accident didn't have a worse outcome and noted that Shanahan's approach to his recovery is similar to how coaches run a team.
"Most importantly, thank God he and the other person involved are okay. Perspective is everything. We talk about that all the time as coaches, and everybody goes through different things," McVay said. "I think the most important thing is that he's on the road to recovery. His wife Mandy, and he's got a beautiful family, and I think any time that something like that happens, it shakes you up a little bit."
Shanahan is entering his 10th season as the 49ers' head coach. Since being hired in 2017, he has become one of the league's top coaches, compiling an 82-67 (.550) regular-season record and a 9-5 playoff mark. Under his leadership, San Francisco has made two Super Bowl appearances and is coming off a 12-5 regular-season campaign in 2025 that ended with a divisional-round loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks .

title: Jordan Devey dies at 38: Family says former NFL guard died by suicide
summary: Devey played seven NFL seasons with five teams, winning Super Bowl XLIX with the Patriots
full_text:
Jordan Devey , a former NFL guard and Super Bowl champion, has died at the age of 38. A GoFundMe established after his death to help support Devey's family says he died by suicide.
"Tragically, Jordan took his own life, leaving his family to navigate an incredibly difficult and heartbreaking time," the GoFundMe page reads.
Speaking with Fox 13 in Salt Lake City , Devey's mother, Leslie, said the family believes he "possibly suffered from CTE." However, the family said it will not be able to test for the neurodegenerative disease due to the nature of his death.
Following his death, Devey's wife, Lindsay, posted a photo of the offensive lineman in his hospital bed on what would've been their 15th wedding anniversary.
"We have filled the walls of our homes and hearts with countless memories, joys, struggles, and triumphs," Lindsay's Instagram post reads . "We brought 4 beautiful children into this world that have your eyes, freckles, and compassion. You were our hero and our hearts ache in your absence. We love you. We miss you. And as you said in your last words to me, 'we'll talk soon.'"
pic.twitter.com/tSyYejM8nO
Devey began his NFL career by signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2013 as an undrafted free agent out of Memphis. After spending the offseason with Baltimore, he joined the New England Patriots ' practice squad in early September. In 2014, he saw his first regular-season action, playing in seven games with four starts as New England went on to win Super Bowl XLIX.
The Patriots traded Devey to the San Francisco 49ers in the summer of 2015, where he saw the most playing time of his career. He appeared in 15 games with nine starts at guard. The Utah native then spent three seasons (2016-18) with the Kansas City Chiefs before finishing his career with the Las Vegas Raiders (2019) and Buffalo Bills (2020). In all, he appeared in 44 regular-season games with 21 starts.
