Over the next couple of weeks, the front office will have to whittle down 90 players to 53. Here’s my prediction of who those 53 players will be as training camp begins. Here are the first four versions: Version 1.0 Version 2.0 Version 3.0 Version 4.0 Quarterback (2) Joe Burrow Joe Flacco Cut: Sean Clifford, Josh Johnson Notes: Unless there’s some sort of catastrophic injury, the two guys on the roster will be Burrow and Flacco. Running Back (3) Chase Brown Samaje Perine Tahj Brooks Cut: Gary Brightwell, Kentrell Bullock, Jamal Haynes, Kendall Milton Notes: I think there’s a very small chance the Bengals could find a running back they like in free agency during camp to add to the three above. However, I also think Zac Taylor and Dan Pitcher are comfortable with Brown, Perine and Brooks. I also expect Brooks’ role to be expanded. Wide Receiver (6) Ja’Marr Chase Tee Higgins Andrei Iosivas Charlie Jones Mitchell Tinsley Kendric Pryor Cut: Xavier Johnson, Dohnte Myers, Jordan Moore, Noah Thomas, Ke’Shawn Williams Notes: Chase and Higgins are the best WR duo in the league. Higgins would be WR1 on almost any other team; he just happens to be teammates with the best wide receiver in the world. After them, though, there’s a considerable drop. The WR3 job is up for grabs, and could be a revolving door for the Bengals, based on the situation. I do think the Bengals keep six wide receivers and that WR6 job is up for grabs. Chase, Higgins, Iosivas, Jones and Tinsley are locks. Tight End (4) Mike Gesicki Drew Sample Tanner Hudson Erick All Jr. Active/NFI: Josh Kattus Cut: Cam Grandy, Jack Endries Notes: Gesicki is a tight end in name, but plays more like a slot receiver. Sample is used as an extra blocker more often than not, though watching him rumble forward with the ball is always incredible. Hudson has the trust of the coaches, and a healthy All could cut into the playing time of all of the guys ahead of him on the depth chart. Hopefully the Bengals would be able to keep Endries on the practice squad. Offensive Line (10) Orlando Brown Jr. Dylan Fairchild Ted Karras Dalton Risner Amarius Mims Cody Ford Jalen Rivers Andrew Coker Conner Lew Brian Parker II Cut: OT Javon Foster, OT Corey Robinson II, OT Christian Jones, G Liam Brown, C Jacob Bayer Notes: For the first time in Joe Burrow’s career, he’ll have the same offensive line lined up in front of him for two consecutive seasons. Risner joined the team during training camp last season and fit right in at right guard. Ford is their swing tackle right now. Defensive Line (9) DE Boye Mafe DT Dexter Lawrence II DT Jonathan Allen DE Shemar Stewart DE Myles Murphy DT Kris Jenkins Jr. DT T.J. Slaton Jr. DE Cashius Howell DT Landon Robinson PUP: BJ Hill Cut: DE Isaiah Foskey, DE Cedric Johnson, DT Howard Cross III, DT McKinnley Jackson, DT Jordan Jefferson Notes: Hill starting the season on PUP would have really thrown the Bengals for a loop had it not been for how active they were in free agency. They have Lawrence and Allen still, and Jenkins and Slaton as backups. When Hill returns, I expect he’ll be the 10th defensive lineman, and a cut will come from elsewhere. If Hill gets activated off PUP before final cuts, then things could get really dicey. Do they cut a promising rookie like Landon Robinson? Or does T.J. Slaton become a cap casualty? Linebackers (5) Demetrius Knight Jr. Barrett Carter Oren Burks Joe Giles-Harris Shaka Heyward Cut: Liam Anderson, Swayze Bozeman, Jack Dingle, Eric Gentry, Antwan Powell-Ryland Notes: The linebacker position was BAD in 2025, but both Knight and Carter were rookies, and they had a subpar defensive line in front of them. Now with Lawrence, the most double-teamed nose tackle in the league, occupying linemen, hopefully they’ll both have more space to move and do their jobs. However, if there’s a position where the Bengals could add a free agent during camp where they’d immediately make an impact, it’s at linebacker. Cornerback (6) DJ Turner II Dax Hill Jalen Davis Josh Newton Ja’Sir Taylor Tacario Davis Cut: Jalen Kimber, Bralyn Lux, Ceyair Wright Notes: The only other position I would have liked to see the Bengals add a free agent or a draft pick is at corner. I like Turner and Hill as the team’s two outside corners, and I think Davis can be a solid slot corner. The issue is depth at the position. If there’s an injury, and there often is, I feel like their lack of depth could be a problem. This is the other position I could see the Bengals adding a free agent during camp, especially if someone with a little experience is available. Safety (5) Bryan Cook Jordan Battle Kyle Dugger PJ Jules Daijahn Anthony Cut: Russ Yeast, Isaiah Nwokobia Notes: Cook’s signing was overshadowed by the team’s trade for Lawrence, but his addition could have just as much of an impact. The Bengals have struggled at safety since Jessie Bates left in free agency, but Cook, Battle and Dugger represent the best three they’ve had on the roster since the days of Bates and Vonn Bell. Special Teams (3) K – Evan McPherson P – Ryan Rehkow LS – William Wagner Cut: None Notes: No notes. What do you think? Sound off.

title: Tee Higgins nearly earns the top spot in best WR2 rankings
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have had one of the best, if not the best, WR2 in Tee Higgins across the NFL since Ja’Marr Chase was drafted back in 2021. Higgins has been regarded as a WR1 and WR1b on the Bengals for years, especially during his contract extension disputes, and has produced impressive numbers despite multiple […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have had one of the best, if not the best, WR2 in Tee Higgins across the NFL since Ja’Marr Chase was drafted back in 2021. Higgins has been regarded as a WR1 and WR1b on the Bengals for years, especially during his contract extension disputes, and has produced impressive numbers despite multiple injuries. However, heading into 2026, Sports Illustrated has a new name on top of the best WR2 list , and Higgins enters at number 2. “The perfect complement to Ja’Marr Chase, Higgins and Chase have formed the most consistent and highest-paid receiving duo in the league over the past five years. Since joining the Bengals as a second-round pick in 2020, Higgins has recorded two 1,000-yard receiving seasons and two double-digit receiving touchdown seasons. Had Higgins not missed multiple games due to injury in each of the past three seasons, he’d likely have even more 1,000-yard campaigns on his résumé,” SI wrote. “With Higgins and Chase out wide, the Bengals hold one of the best passing attacks in the NFL—especially when Joe Burrow is healthy—and Higgins is a pivotal part of that success as he hauls in contested catches and touchdowns. After all, there’s a reason Burrow vouched so heavily for both Higgins and Chase to get paid,“ SI continued. Higgins has officially been surpassed by Dallas Cowboys wideout George Pickens, who plays alongside their WR1 Ceedee Lamb. Sports Illustrated wrote that the Cowboys have two true WR1’s and Pickens could have an even bigger year in 2026 as he looks to solidify a contract extension in Dallas. No matter what, Higgins is one of the best wideouts in the league and is the perfect complement to Chase when healthy. If Higgins can put together a complete season in 2026, the numbers will show why I believe he is the best of the best.

title: Bengals Film Room: A healthy Connor Lew has a bright NFL future
summary: We all love Ted Karras, but he isn’t getting any younger. Matt Lee: Gone Seth McLaughlin: Gone So, the Cincinnati Bengals went back to the draft to find the heir apparent, and in typical Bengals fashion, they targeted a player who had first round buzz prior to a season-ending injury. Let me introduce you to […]
full_text: AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 11: Connor Lew #75 of the Auburn Tigers lines up against the Georgia Bulldogs during the second quarter at Jordan-Hare Stadium on October 11, 2025 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images We all love Ted Karras, but he isn’t getting any younger. Matt Lee: Gone Seth McLaughlin: Gone So, the Cincinnati Bengals went back to the draft to find the heir apparent, and in typical Bengals fashion, they targeted a player who had first round buzz prior to a season-ending injury. Let me introduce you to Connor Lew. Brick wall pic.twitter.com/5s6JicL06y — Matt (@CoachMinich) April 29, 2026 First, let’s talk about the anchor. The defensive tackle initially takes an angle toward the guard, but when he counters back at the center, Lew stops him in his tracks. Lew has a strong base that he maintains while he is on the move in pass protection. Connor Lew pic.twitter.com/QbfwhqXQNK — Matt (@CoachMinich) April 29, 2026 Here, we get a good look at Lew’s footwork. The defender tries to go right, then tries to go left, but Lew is always there to stop him. As the quarterback scrambles one direction, Lew buries the defensive tackle in the opposite direction. Lew Pass Pro pic.twitter.com/Fon7PsEoh0 — Matt (@CoachMinich) April 29, 2026 Here Lew puts it all together. He has a nice kick step (which is not something you often talk about with centers) to get out and block the 2i. This is after throwing a strike of a snap, mind you. The defender tries to come back inside and cross Lew’s face, and he succeeds. Lew loses some ground, but he gets himself back in position and stops the rush cold. Lew vs 0 pic.twitter.com/u2LuWmduPJ — Matt (@CoachMinich) April 29, 2026 It’s extremely difficult to solo run block a head up defensive tackle because you don’t know what gap the are trying to get in and often nose tackles will just fight against pressure. In this clip, Lew takes on the 0 tech on a zone block to the left. When the running back cuts back to the gap to Lew’s right, Lew shows great strength to hold on to the block and leave the hole open. Dr. Lew pic.twitter.com/ynecZHLtFx — Matt (@CoachMinich) April 29, 2026 Now here is a clip where Lew makes a down block on a linebacker who is standing up in the B gap. Again, let’s go back to the beginning of the play to fully appreciate this. First, Lew must throw a perfect strike between his legs as he does on every play. So now he is starting with his hand between his legs, and he must move laterally two gaps over in order to pick up a defender who is presumably faster and quicker than he is without giving up any ground. All in a day’s work. The Bengals’ future at center is very bright indeed.

title: Bryan Cook is coming home to fix the Bengals defense
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals had a huge defensive problem over the past couple of seasons. So when free agency hit, they did not hesitate to land one of the top players at a huge position of need. A player they knew from their own backyard, former Kansas City Chiefs safety Bryan Cook. Bryan Cook Cap Status […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 15: Bryan Cook #6 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrates after a play during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on September 15, 2024 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals had a huge defensive problem over the past couple of seasons. So when free agency hit, they did not hesitate to land one of the top players at a huge position of need. A player they knew from their own backyard, former Kansas City Chiefs safety Bryan Cook. Bryan Cook Height: 6´1¨ Weight: 210 pounds Age: 26 years old College: Cincinnati Hometown: Cincinnati, Ohio Experience: 4 seasons Cap Status Cook signed a three-year contract worth up to $40.25 million with $14 million guaranteed this offseason. He has just over a $10.6 million cap hit this season, according to Over The Cap. He accounts for 3.37 percent of the cap this year and is the 12th highest-paid safety as of writing. Background Most Bengals fans may remember Cook more for the two years he spent at the University of Cincinnati in 2020 and 2021. Especially the 2021 season, when he was part of the team that earned a spot in the College Football Playoffs. He was a first-team All-American Athletic Conference selection that season as well. Bryan Cook is a HUGE upgrade at safety for the Bengals defense. Physical, rangy, dependable tackler, and a great pre-snap communicator. pic.twitter.com/tbj5EyH5fF — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 15, 2026 He was drafted by the Chiefs in the second round of the 2022 draft. He earned a starting role in 2023. He missed the last five games of the 2023 season, but has started every other game since the start of 2024. He has 148 solo tackles, 15 passes defended, three interceptions, and four tackles for a loss over his career. He was the fourth-highest-rated safety at PFF in 2025. A big area of improvement will be that he only missed his tackle 5.6 percent of the time. We will touch on that in the next section as well, though. 2026 Outlook It is hard to see Cook not once again being one of the top safeties in the NFL. It comes as he will be replacing what I will refer to nicely as a poor fit with Geno Stone. Stone was meant to be a ball hawk and create turnovers. Instead, he was a liability at tackling, which Cook is pretty much the opposite of. Bryan Cook highlights starting with some pretty insane range to get outside of the numbers from the opposite hash. Some great processing and anticipation while also showing up as a physical force. pic.twitter.com/Awv40xhLW3 — mike (@bengals_sans) March 9, 2026 Cook is still a great coverage safety. PFF had him ranked as the sixth-highest-rated safety in coverage last year. What Cincinnati fans will notice more of is his ability to get ball carriers down in the open field, which was a rarity among most defenders last season. The underrated aspect Cook should bring is leadership to the defensive side of the ball. He is a guy who has been to the top of the mountain and knows how a championship-winning defense prepares. It is certainly an aspect that side of the ball has needed a bit more of the past couple of years. I mean, sometimes it is that simple: Cook is a premier player at his position. It was a huge position of need for the Bengals. It was a perfect match, and it should play out well for both parties. Signing Bryan Cook in FA was huge. He might end up being an even better signing than Trey Hendrickson was in 2021. Cook earned an 83.5 PFF grade, ranking 4th among safeties. He brings a dynamic we really haven’t had since Jessie Bates. Rangy, versatile, elite attacking… pic.twitter.com/Iai4qXNXIt — 937Bengals 🐅 (@BengalsinDa937) April 15, 2026 Bengals Reacts Who is the Bengals’ biggest rival currently? In this week’s Bengals Reacts survey, 43% of voters said the Baltimore Ravens are Cincinnati’s biggest rival, while 30% went with the Steelers. This survey was brought to you by FanDuel Sportsbook .

title: Browns fans expecting this duo to start on the interior offensive line
summary: The Cleveland Browns may have acquired a lot of new offensive linemen this offseason, and we feel pretty good about who the starting offensive tackles will be, as well as Zion Johnson being at left guard. But what about center and right guard? Our Reacts poll this week included several options for who might start […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 03: Elgton Jenkins #74 of the Cleveland Browns looks on during the Cleveland Browns OTA Offseason Workouts at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 03, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns may have acquired a lot of new offensive linemen this offseason, and we feel pretty good about who the starting offensive tackles will be , as well as Zion Johnson being at left guard. But what about center and right guard? Our Reacts poll this week included several options for who might start at center and right guard. We know that OL Elgton Jenkins is supposed to take one of those spots, but depending on which spot he’s in, who goes in the other spot? The top projection — with 50% of the vote — sees Elgton Jenkins at center, with last year’s part-time starter Teven Jenkins at right guard. Not too far behind, at 35%, sees rookie Parker Brailsford at center, and Elgton Jenkins at right guard. One of the players with the least expectations to start seems to be KT Leveston. One dark horse scenario that we didn’t consider much yet could also see Tytus Howard , who is the starter at right tackle, moving inside to guard with Dawand Jones starting at right tackle. That combination might give the Browns the starting five with the highest potential, but it’s also a lot of moving pieces to try make happen, especially with Jones’ injury history. The Browns are still heavy underdogs to make the postseason, at 70/1 compared to the other teams, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

title: Browns still looking for help at defensive end
summary: The Cleveland Browns will begin the post-Myles Garrett era this week when veterans report for training camp. In place of the reigning Defensive Player of the Year will be Jared Verse, who, while not on the same level as Garrett, is no slouch, as he has posted 99 pressures since entering the league as a […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns Jared Verse (8) runs a drill as teammates defensive end Julian Okwara, Khordae Sydnor, Alex Wright and Adin Huntington look on during team OTAs at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus of the Cleveland Browns in Berea, Ohio on June 2, 2026. | Mike Cardew / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The Cleveland Browns will begin the post-Myles Garrett era this week when veterans report for training camp. In place of the reigning Defensive Player of the Year will be Jared Verse, who, while not on the same level as Garrett, is no slouch, as he has posted 99 pressures since entering the league as a first-round selection in the 2024 NFL Draft. Verse does not have to do it alone, of course, as the Browns are banking on Alex Wright and Isaiah McGuire to step up and be more than support players while Verse does all the heavy lifting. Wright, for one, is not shying away from the challenge as he explained during Organized Team Activities in June : “Somebody gotta take control, like somebody has to take charge. So, just trying to step into that role. It just don’t have to be me; it could be all of us. But I’m taking on that ownership; just because (Myles is) gone, that doesn’t mean the standard that he set since he’s been here, since he was a rookie, is going to change. We are all still going to work and be a top defense; we’re still going to just work our butts off.” That is all very exciting, but general manager Andrew Berry did try to add another edge rusher as the club originally agreed to a deal with free agent A.J. Epenesa, only to see him fail the team’s physical and eventually sign with the Philadelphia Eagles. Berry is reportedly still on the hunt, according to cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot : The Browns are still in the market for a veteran defensive end to add to the rotation and make up for the loss of former Bills edge rusher A.J. Epenesa, who failed their physical before signing with the Eagles. Ideally, the Browns would like to have one in place before the start of camp, but they might have to wait a bit to find their man. The problem is, the list of available players has some familiar names on it, but they are not necessarily all that exciting. Some of the options include: Joey Bosa, who had five sacks, five forced fumbles, and 42 quarterback pressures last season with the Buffalo Bills. At this stage in his career, he is nothing more than a situational rusher, but that could fit what Cleveland is looking for. Jadeveon Clowney, who was with the Browns in 2021 and 2022. Since then, Clowney has been one-and-done with the Baltimore Ravens, Carolina Panthers, and Dallas Cowboys. He was productive last season with the Cowboys in posting 8.5 sacks and 32 quarterback pressures, and could fit as a rotational pass rusher in Cleveland. Haason Reddick, who has trended downward in each of the past two seasons after a four-year stretch that saw him average 12.5 sacks a season. He was with the New York Jets in 2024 along with new defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg (the Jets linebackers coach), so the familiarity could be a potential asset. Kyle Van Noy, who spent the past three seasons in Baltimore, so he is familiar with the teams in the AFC North. His production fell off last season, but he is dependable, having played at least 13 games every season since 2017, which is always a nice bonus. Those are just a few of the names that reside on the various lists of available free agents . How much interest the Browns would have in any of them is unknown, as is whether or not any of them would want to play in Cleveland in what could be another long season. Berry could also be waiting to see how undrafted free agents Tyreak Sapp or Logan Fano look during the preseason before making a move. If one or both flash enough for the coaching staff, then perhaps Berry does not make a move for an aging player on a one-year deal. But the Browns signaled earlier this summer that they are looking for another rotational player at defensive end, so even if one of these veterans is not an option, Berry may still have a move to make before the season opens on September 13 in Jacksonville. What do you think, Browns fans? Are you content with the current group of defensive ends? Or do you want the Browns to bring in another option? Let us know in the comments.

title: Cleveland Browns training camp 2026: OL preview, Part 1 – Who starts at offensive tackle?
summary: Next up on our training camp preview is the offensive line position. Because Cleveland completely overhauled their offensive line from top to bottom this offseason, we’re not previewing the starting five offensive linemen first. Instead, we’re focusing on who the top candidates at offensive tackle are. Part 2 will focus on the top candidates on […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Spencer Fano #55 of the Cleveland Browns runs a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Next up on our training camp preview is the offensive line position. Because Cleveland completely overhauled their offensive line from top to bottom this offseason, we’re not previewing the starting five offensive linemen first. Instead, we’re focusing on who the top candidates at offensive tackle are. Part 2 will focus on the top candidates on the interior of the line, and then Part 3 will focus on the back end of the group. 1. Spencer Fano – Rookie OT Height: 6-6 | Weight: 315 lbs | Age: 23 Experience: Rookie | College: Utah With the ninth overall pick in this year’s draft , the Browns selected the top offensive lineman on the board in Utah’s Spencer Fano . Sincer Joe Thomas retired after the 2017 season, Cleveland has been looking for their next top-tier left tackle. They took their first stab at it when they made Jedrick Wills a first-round pick, but he produced mediocre results. After Wills, a few stop-gaps have been in place. It was thought that maybe Dawand Jones could be the left tackle of the future, but he’s had a combination of injury and consistency issues. Fano has a lot of talent and potential, but he also isn’t expected to be an All-Pro from Day 1 at left tackle. There were some who believe he’d perform better at right tackle or a guard position to begin his career, but Cleveland is going to have him anchor the left side of the line right away, and I don’t have a problem with that, considering the rest of the roster makeup. Here are some other features the DBN staff has written on Fano over the offseason: Everything you need to know from childhood to NFL draft (Barry Shuck) Spencer Fano, OT, Utah stats, awards, and scouting report (Jared Mueller) Why Spencer Fano is a perfect fit for Cleveland’s offensive line (Matthew Wilson) Final Roster Odds: 100% 2. Tytus Howard – Starting OT Height: 6-5 | Weight: 320 lbs | Age: 30 Experience: 8 years | College: Alabama State The first sign that Cleveland was revamping their offensive line this offseason came in early March, when they sent a 5th round pick to the Houston Texans in exchange for Tytus Howard . The move also came with a 3-year, $63 million extension. Howard was solid in pass protection for Houston, with 93 games started by the former first-round pick. His run blocking is merely average, but after injuries plagued former right tackle Jack Conklin for years, Andrew Berry really placed a premium on durability. Cleveland has a proven veteran and a first-round pick anchoring their tackle positions, which gives them confidence that they don’t have to worry about those spots for several years. Barry Shuck also did a write-up on everything you need to know about Howard . Final Roster Odds: 100% 3. Dawand Jones – Competing OT Height: 6-8 | Weight: 374 lbs | Age: 24 Experience: 4 years | College: Ohio State The most interesting player on the Browns depth chart this camp might be Dawand Jones . When I think of Jones, I think, “He’s a starting caliber player.” But the Browns went out and acquired two starters this offseason for the tackle positions. I don’t see Cleveland putting him at guard. Him being a swing tackle — the primary backup who can play either tackle position — would seem to suit him in the final year of his contract, especially when you consider the fact that he’s suffered three season-ending injuries in his first three years. However, offensive line coach George Warhop did not want to label him the team’s swing tackle yet back in June, on the insistence that he wants to see if they they can find a starting spot for Jones . Where? The best shot of that happening would be if Howard, who has experience at guard, kicks over to be the starting right guard, and then Jones starts at right tackle. I wouldn’t have a problem with that possibility, so we’ll see if that becomes a storyline as camp goes along. Jones also earned a proven performance escalator this offseason , which Cleveland promptly took away , something that typically hasn’t been a good sign for the long-term prospects of a player with a team. Jones could also be a trade candidate, but with the depth issues faced the past few years, I don’t know if they want to just give away their solid depth now. Final Roster Odds: 99% 4. KT Leveston – Backup OT Height: 6-4 | Weight: 335 lbs | Age: 26 Experience: 3 years | College: Kansas State At the end of training camp last year, the Browns acquired KT Leveston from the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for a 7th round pick in 2028. He was originally a 7th round pick by the Rams in 2024. After some struggles initially at tackle, Leveston was one of the team’s linemen who got better as the season went along. He’s still listed as a tackle for now, but talk this offseason has picked up about his potential at right guard: KT Leveston is built for a phone booth at guard. His hands are incredibly strong, and he plays with tremendous effort and leverage. At tackle, he struggles at times kicking back against elite NFL pass rushers. Put him inside at guard, let him get his hands on defenders in the run… https://t.co/sN1eA7J5h0 — Lance Reisland (Coach Riz) (@LanceReisland) June 10, 2026 Earlier in minicamp, as Cleveland tries to find their best five offensive linemen, they gave Leveston some work at tackle, and Todd Monken had some nice praise for what he showed on tape. It goes to show you that as a young player in a losing season, those incremental gains can pay off huge from what people see of you: “We do like his power and his toughness, from what we’ve seen from last year, obviously we don’t see it here. Last year when he got a chance to play, you could see that running off the football, his aggressiveness, finishing plays, you love that about him. Those kinds of guys you’re always trying to find a spot for.” Final Roster Odds: 90% 5. Austin Barber – Rookie OT Height: 6-7 | Weight: 320 lbs | Age: 23 Experience: Rookie | College: Florida If the Browns do feel comfortable with moving on from a guy like Dawand Jones this year, look no further for the reason than Austin Barber . Cleveland selected him in the third round of this year’s draft . With a solid camp, there wouldn’t be a starting role for him, but it’s possible he could be viewed as the team’s swing tackle from the get-go. While some analysts like Dane Brugler had wondered if Barber should move inside, when the Browns took Barber, DBN’s Matt Wilson noted in our staff chat that Barber was his favorite offensive tackle in the draft, and believes he should stick outside as opposed to moving inside. He already has looked the part this offseason: The first thing that stands out about rookie offensive tackle Austin Barber, #58, is his sheer size. Just a mammoth, athletic looking player. full_text: Most of us already knew that former Cleveland Browns EDGE rusher Myles Garrett lived in Wadsworth, Ohio. We just have never actually been invited for tea and crumpets there. Make that sweet tea, sliced tomatoes, and brisket. RELATED: GARRETT IS GONE. WHAT DOES IT MEAN GOING FORWARD? Now that Garrett has been traded into the NFC with the Los Angeles Rams , he requires a new pad, close to all of the Hollywood types. His old digs? Now listed on Zillow for sale. One thing Garrett has is money. Lots of it. But surprisingly, his house and adjacent two acres are only appraised at $2.1 million. In 2025, Garrett inked an extension worth $160 million. So, one might assume his home would look like a hotel from a drone cam, but it is actually quite modest. The reason is that Garrett had the house built a year after he was drafted in 2018. That first deal was for $30,41 million, plus a $20.25 million signing bonus. And although he has gotten more wheelbarrows for his cash, he has remained in the same house during all these years with the Cleveland Browns. Frugal? Modest? Or just comfortable with where he chose to be, and stayed that way? The home has five bedrooms and six bathrooms, with 4,300 square feet of living space. Some portions of the home are two-story, with two staircases. There is also a grand office, a spa, a full gym, a theater, a custom bar, walk-in closets, and a bonus room used for gaming. Only a portion of the property has been cleared and comes with a metal front gate. As far as the exterior, parts include stone along with an adjacent three-vehicle garage. Stone work is also on both sides of the electric gate. Right after the Browns traded Garrett, he signed a restructured contract for five years that will pay him $208.2 million, with $37 million fully guaranteed ⁠this year and $99 million guaranteed through the 2028 season. Garrett was the first overall pick in the 2017 NFL draft and played nine years with Cleveland. He has been voted to the Pro Bowl seven times, selected First Team or Second Team All-Pro another seven times, won the Deacon Jones Award in 2025, named the “NFL Defensive Player of the Year” twice, and was a member of the NFL All-Rookie Team. With Garrett selling his custom-built home, this means that after his career is over, he is unlikely to be headed back to Northeast Ohio despite making this statement two years ago , around the time he purchased a piece of the Cleveland Cavaliers: “I’m not gonna sell my house and pack up and leave,” Garrett said of Cleveland. “I definitely plan to be here for a long time. I’ll start a family here. I’m not just gonna rip and run once things are over and I hang up the cleats. I’m gonna be here supporting the Cavs, supporting the Browns for a mighty long time.” Since the news of Garrett’s home going on the market went public , the listing on Zillow has been taken down, but it is listed with The Elli Group . In the pictures connected with the listing, you can see some of Garrett’s collectibles, along with dinosaur-related themes, and a few Browns related objected sprinkled around the house, including a child-sized jersey hanging above the washer and dryer set. Are you surprised Garrett sold his house after his statement 2 years ago? Do you think he sells his stake of the Cavs soon as well? Join the conversation! title: Browns offensive line remains uncertain despite all the roster additions
summary: The NFL season is slowly approaching, as teams are beginning to report to training camp. For the Cleveland Browns, the rookies have already reported, with veterans required in town early this week. The team has undergone multiple changes this offseason; the most noticeable is the offensive line. The Browns have essentially replaced the entire offensive […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Spencer Fano #55 of the Cleveland Browns runs a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL season is slowly approaching, as teams are beginning to report to training camp. For the Cleveland Browns, the rookies have already reported, with veterans required in town early this week. The team has undergone multiple changes this offseason; the most noticeable is the offensive line. The Browns have essentially replaced the entire offensive line from last season , with two rookies potentially starting. The free agency acquisitions, signing guards Elgton Jenkins (who could also play center) and Zion Johnson, as well as trading for tackle Tytus Howard, were all brought in to help bolster this line. With the moves that Cleveland made to improve the offensive line, the question everyone asked was whether the team did enough to improve one of the weakest offensive lines in football last season. It’s not an understatement to say that many of the Browns offensive problems last year stemmed from lackluster offensive line play. With instability at the tackle spots and deteriorating play on the interior, Cleveland’s offensive line struggles were more of an issue than people want to admit; blaming quarterbacks and coaches is way more fun. Browns GM Andrew Berry is known for attacking position groups that are the weakest. Berry has done this multiple times during his tenure in Cleveland, and this year he’s done it with the offensive line. In terms of the tackle spots, trading for Howard was the first domino that fell. Howard was the lone bright spot on a struggling Houston Texans offensive line and brings versatility, as he can play both guard and tackle. The same can be said for Jenkins. Before tearing his ACL, Jenkins was a two-time Pro Bowler with the Green Bay Packers. Jenkins is primarily a guard, but the Packers chose to move him to center this past season; while the results were less than ideal, that is the role he could play in Cleveland as well. When healthy, Jenkins has proven he can be a quality starter. The team’s biggest splash this free agency was signing Johnson, who also played on a struggling offensive line with the Los Angeles Chargers, and is likely going to start at the left guard position. Spencer Fano, who the Browns drafted in the first round of the 2026 NFL draft, is the cornerstone of this offensive line. Fano, who was one of the top prospects in his class, has the versatility to be kicked inside if necessary, but it’s likely he will be the team’s starting left tackle for the future. Parker Brailsford, who the team drafted in the fifth round, could potentially start at center for the team. Austin Barber was also drafted, adding another young tackle option. On paper, this unit is better than last season’s group. Versatility is what stands out for the archetype of players that the Browns acquired. Multiple players that can play different positions. However, it’s a valid question if Cleveland did enough to improve the unit. Center Tyler Linderbaum was a highly coveted offensive lineman in free agency, but he chose to sign with the Las Vegas Raiders. Linderbaum would’ve made sense for the Browns due to his familiarity with current head coach Todd Monken and his scheme, but his price tag would’ve been too hefty for the team to pay, and it would’ve crippled the rest of the unit in terms of paying for other players. Overall, this unit looks improved, but time will tell if the moves made in free agency and in the draft will pay dividends. Do you think the Browns offensive line is improved, much improved, or similar as last year’s unit? Join the conversation! summary: 4 young Cowboys ready for expanded roles in 2026- Terence Watson, Cowboys Wire Pay more attention to these names heading into the 2026 season. full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 25: Brevyn Spann-Ford #89 of the Dallas Cowboys carries the ball before the NFL game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images 4 young Cowboys ready for expanded roles in 2026- Terence Watson, Cowboys Wire Pay more attention to these names heading into the 2026 season. Phil Mafah When a running back brings the size and power Mafah does to the table, it’s only natural to find ways to get him on the field and let him wear down opposing defenses. Fans likely would have seen more from the young back last season if not for the shoulder injury that sidelined him until the season finale, in which he punched in a goal-line touchdown. That’s the type of role Mafah needs to carve out for himself as he battles for more snaps this year. Dallas would love to keep starting running back Javonte Williams fresh and healthy throughout the season, and one way to accomplish that is by handing more of the goal-line work to Mafah. At 6-foot-1 and 232 pounds, he has the frame to punish defenders and move the pile in short-yardage situations. It benefits everyone involved. Williams takes fewer unnecessary hits, while Mafah gives the Cowboys a true battering ram in the red zone, someone capable of turning tough yards into touchdowns. Brevyn Spann-Ford Like Mafah, Spann-Ford enters the season behind an established starter in Jake Ferguson. However he managed to carve out a role for himself last year as Dallas’ primary blocking tight end. This season presents an opportunity to expand that role. With Luke Schoonmaker’s standing on the roster far from secure, Spann-Ford has a chance to climb the depth chart if he proves he can be a more consistent receiving threat. The red-zone portion of training camp could be the perfect place to make that statement. Standing 6-foot-7, Spann-Ford presents matchup problems few defenders are equipped to handle near the goal line. Rather than limiting him to blocking duties in those situations, Dallas should look for ways to take advantage of his size and create mismatches in the passing game. He’s shown reliable hands when given opportunities, and expanding his role as a receiver could help the Cowboys become more efficient inside the 20. Before that happens, though, he’ll need to overtake Schoonmaker and establish himself as the clear TE2. 3 Cowboys on the roster bubble who could steal the show in training camp- Maitland Rutledge, The Landry Hat Roster cuts are on the horizon. 3. Traeshon Holden, WR If Cowboys fans should keep an eye on one unknown receiver during training camp, it’s Traeshon Holden. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy and KaVontae Turpin make up the top of the depth chart, but the fifth WR spot is up for grabs. That spot could be Holden’s if he has just as good a camp as he had last year. Whenever Holden was on the practice field last summer, he made plays. The biggest was a one-handed catch in the back of the end zone on a Joe Milton throw . He also had long catches in the preseason games against the Rams and Ravens. That prompted Dallas to sign him to the practice squad. While he did not see the field in the regular season, he enters camp as one of the favored young receivers to make the team. Dallas brought in veterans like Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Denzel Mims, and Tyler Johnson, but there is no guarantee they make the team. Time is also running out for Jonathan Mingo. Despite all the competition around him, Holden should have a spot at least on the practice squad again if he catches everything thrown his way like last year. Dallas Cowboys 2026 Training Camp Calendar, Dates, & Preseason Schedule- Josh Sanchez, Sports Illustrated Mark these dates; football is fast approaching. Dallas Cowboys 2026 Training Camp Schedule July 27 : Team Charter arrives in Oxnard July 28 : Opening Press conference (11:00 a.m. PDT) July 29 : First practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) July 30 : Open practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) August 1 : Opening Ceremony (11:15 a.m. PDT) August 3 : First padded practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) August 4 : Open practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) August 6 : Open practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) August 8 : Open practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) August 9 : Open practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) August 11 : Joint practice at LA Rams (TBD) August 13 : Open practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) August 15 : Dallas at Seattle (5:00 p.m. PDT) August 17 : Open practice (11:45 a.m. PDT) August 18 : Joint practice with New Orleans (2:00 p.m. PDT) August 22 : Dallas at Arizona (7:00 p.m. MST) August 22 : Return to Dallas ( Saints 08/28 @ 7:00 p.m. CDT ) Christian Parker Could Create an Unexpected Reunion in 27′- Cody Warren, Inside The Star Looking further down the road. Parker Will Get His Chance to Prove Himself I don’t want this to get twisted into Parker being halfway out the door. He hasn’t earned anything yet. I can be rough on defensive coordinators and I think most fans are with me. One week the new guy is a genius, and the next week, after a running back breaks loose for 140 yards, we all want him escorted out of The Star by security. That’s the life of a coach for the Cowboys. The good is good, but bad is the worst in the league for us fans. We can’t operate like that, but we do. We need to give Parker enough time to build his defense instead of patching together someone else’s defense. If the first year is bumpy, we ride those bumps like driving on Oklahoma roads. I want to see if the defense improves, and whether the young guys are developing. Let’s see if his plan makes sense in December, and if it does, keep building… The Dan Quinn Connection is a Whole Thing This hypothetical only works if Washington falls apart, Quinn gets fired and Parker eventually takes a head coaching job. I know that’s a lot of dominoes to fall. Still, Quinn and Schottenheimer aren’t strangers who shared a hallway once. They coached together with the New York Jets in 2007 and 2008 , then reunited in Dallas in 2022 and 2023. Daily discussion question: What is your bold prediction for training camp?

full_text: Will any Cowboys player be under the microscope more than Tyler Guyton in this year’s training camp? The former first-round pick is entering Year 3 with lingering questions about his long-term viability, and even talk of his starting job being up for grabs. Background Years in NFL: 2 Acquired by: 2024 1st-round pick Guyton was drafted about a month after longtime bookend Tyron Smith left the Cowboys in free agency. Like Smith in 2011, Guyton came out of college with plenty of raw athletic potential but the need for technical development. He wasn’t necessarily going to start as a rookie, but veteran Chuma Edoga got hurt in the early preseason and thrust Guyton into duty. His own injuries cost him two games and limited much-needed practice work in other weeks, and it showed with on-field struggles. Guyton was benched from Weeks 14-17 when Edoga returned from injury. Coming off a better camp last year, Guyton was the full-time starter. He showed improvement overall, but still had too many breakdowns in pass protection and penalties. Injuries became an even greater issue, costing Guyton seven games. Now his durability is as much a concern as his long-term development, creating plenty of angst around him ahead of this critical third season. Contract Status Years Left: 2 2026 Cap Hit: $3.59 million Probably about a week or so after next year’s draft, Dallas will have to decide if it’s going to exercise the fifth-year option on Guyton’s contract. Given how much he’s already played, and assuming full-time starts in 2026, that one-year salary will likely be around $20 million. That’d be a huge jump from his rookie compensation, so how this season goes is paramount to the Cowboys’ decision. 2026 Projections Role: Starting LT Roster Chance: 100% During OTAs, Brian Schottenheimer said that Guyton and fellow third-year prospect Nathan Thomas are competing to be the starting left tackle. Based on how the practice reps went, and other chatter from around the team, it’s clear that it’s still Guyton’s job to lose. But that Schottenheimer was willing to put that out there, with a specific alternative name in mind, indicates that Guyton’s hold on that job isn’t nearly as firm as most other starters’. Dallas put additional heat on Guyton with fourth-round rookie Drew Shelton, who is another exceptional athlete that needs time to develop. Shelton won’t be contending with Guyton and Thomas this year, but could be interesting in 2027. And depending on what the Cowboys do with Guyton’s fifth-year option, next season could be a contract year for him. So far this offseason, all of the reports around Guyton are positive. He’s been praised by veteran leader Tyler Smith and offensive coordinator Klayton Adams for his approach and progress. We’ve seen clips of his training with offensive line guru Duke Manyweather. As long as he can stay healthy, Guyton seems poised to make that crucial third-year leap. If he does, Thomas and Shelton, along with most critics, will be swatted away like flies. Guyton realizing his potential, with Tyler Smith already an All-Pro and Tyler Booker seemingly on his way, would be a massive step forward for the entire offensive line. It would allow the Cowboys to focus on helping Terence Steele when he needs it, and allow for even more explosiveness in the passing game with cleaner pockets. Still, all that potential isn’t guaranteed production. The Cowboys have been open about their concerns with the competition talk and the Shelton pick. Guyton’s third season will decide if that chatter ends, or if Dallas becomes even more aggressive about its future at left tackle. title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 49
summary: It is Day 49 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Unknown date; Washington, DC, USA; FILE PHOTO; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Roger Staubach (12) in action against the Washington Redskins at RFK Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Malcolm Emmons-Imagn Images It is Day 49 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Get ready for Day 49 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a rivalry win that helped push the Cowboys toward one of the most famous postseason runs in franchise history. Dallas hosted Washington in Week 13 of the 1975 season, with both teams fighting in a crowded NFC East playoff picture. The Cowboys entered at 8-4, Washington at 8-4, and this game carried real wild-card weight. Saturday, December 13, 1975 — 4:30 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 31, Washington 10 The start was ugly for Dallas. Washington scored 10 points in just 32 seconds during the first quarter, and Roger Staubach heard boos from the Texas Stadium crowd after an early interception gave Washington a short field. For a team that had already lost the first meeting in overtime at RFK Stadium, this had the feel of a dangerous spiral. Instead, Staubach settled down and turned the game around. The response came quickly. Staubach hit Golden Richards on a quick sideline throw, and Richards shook off Mike Bass to turn it into a 57-yard touchdown. That play woke up the Cowboys and cut Washington’s lead to 10-7. From there, Dallas began to turn the game from a rivalry scare into a rivalry statement. Before halftime, special teams created another opening. Randy Hughes recovered a fumbled Washington punt by Larry Jones, giving Dallas a short field. On third down from the four-yard line, Tom Landry called a quarterback draw, and Staubach powered through contact at the goal line for the touchdown. He was taken to the locker room afterward for treatment on injured ribs, but Dallas had the lead, 14-10. The game stayed tighter than the final score suggests, but the Cowboys eventually put it away late. Staubach led a 75-yard fourth-quarter drive and capped it with a five-yard touchdown pass to Preston Pearson, pushing the lead to 24-10 with just over five minutes left. Then, 18 seconds later, Charlie Waters intercepted backup quarterback Randy Johnson and returned it 20 yards for a touchdown. What had been a tense rivalry fight suddenly became a 31-10 Dallas win. This game belongs on the countdown because it was one of the key late-season steps before the “Hail Mary” postseason. Dallas improved to 9-4, effectively knocked Washington backward in the wild-card race, and clinched at least a wild-card spot. Two weeks later, the Cowboys would beat Minnesota on Staubach’s famous pass to Drew Pearson, then crush the Rams in the NFC Championship Game before heading to Super Bowl X. #Cowboys vs #Washington 1975 Week 13 Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 31, Washington 10 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/VaU6fJvcLE — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) July 25, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Charlie Waters’ 20-yard interception return touchdown came only 18 seconds after Preston Pearson’s touchdown catch. That sequence turned a 17-10 battle into a 31-10 final. title: Cowboys were allegedly very interested in Brendan Sorsby
summary: It is basically NFL training camp season and that is very exciting for obvious reasons. full_text: Texas Tech's Brendan Sorsby looks on during the spring football game, Friday, April 17, 2026, at Jones AT&T Stadium. | Nathan Giese/Avalanche-Journal / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images It is basically NFL training camp season and that is very exciting for obvious reasons. Consider that this is the last weekend where there will be no Dallas Cowboys activity of any time through the end of this year and, well, exciting is sort of putting it lightly. Football in general is running right down the track. Most conferences in the world of college football have had their media days and soon enough our Saturdays will be full, too. Over this past offseason there was one storyline that bounced back and forth between the collegiate and professional aspects of football as Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby fought to be able to play after gambling allegations led to a host of issues for him. At one point Sorsby was reportedly considering entering the supplemental draft, but he ultimately elected to back out and will be eligible for the 2027 NFL Draft at large. It isn’t low-hanging fruit to say that the Cowboys may be interested in him. ESPN’s Todd Archer wrote about the unusually quiet offseason for the Cowboys , and when he did he revealed that the team was very interested in Sorsby around the time of the supplemental draft situation. When Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby put his name in the supplemental draft, multiple sources said the Cowboys had high interest even with the gambling issues that surrounded Sorsby. Prescott is signed through 2028, so an attempt to potentially find his successor at what could have been a lower-than-expected price would have made sense even if it drew added attention to the Cowboys’ quarterback room. Ultimately, the NFL declined to hold a supplemental draft — denying Sorsby’s eligibility this year. It makes sense for the Cowboys to begin looking for a successor to Dak Prescott. Dak is, after all, the longest-tenured player on the team and he is the longest-tenured starting quarterback in the entire league with respect to the team he plays for (Aaron Rodgers obviously isn’t playing for the Green Bay Packers). Practically speaking, financially more than anything, Prescott is at least going to be quarterbacking the Cowboys through the 2027 season and looking at future options is the responsible thing to do. On the subject of 2027, the draft class that Sorsby is a part of is expected to be particularly deep at quarterback in a way that recent classes haven’t been. The top of it may feature Texas’ Arch Manning, but there will be options all the way through. Perhaps we can consider this a sign that Dallas is going to seriously consider drafting a quarterback next year. Maybe it will wind up being Sorsby. Who knows. What do you think?

title: Cowboys need to become very aggressive
summary: The Dallas Cowboys could use a mantra to live by for the upcoming 2026 NFL season and there could be none better fitting than the Cobra Kai motto from the movie The Karate Kid (1984), “strike first, strike hard, no mercy”. This motto symbolizes ruthless determination and toughness, something we all love to see more […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys could use a mantra to live by for the upcoming 2026 NFL season and there could be none better fitting than the Cobra Kai motto from the movie The Karate Kid (1984), “strike first, strike hard, no mercy”. This motto symbolizes ruthless determination and toughness, something we all love to see more from the Cowboys this year. Like we learn from the movie though, there is a fine line that could lead to unethical behavior if not managed/incorporated properly. But, in such a physical sport like professional football, the “strike first, strike hard, no mercy” mindset pretty closely incorporates everything a team/individual needs in order to be at their ultimate best. The Cobra Kai teaching represents a mindset of assertiveness and dominance and prioritizes a good offense over defense, which sharply contrasts from the Miyagi-Do style that emphasizes defense, balance, and moral discipline. Based on the way the Cowboys rosters constructed, the Cobra Kai model seems to fit best and we will explain why by breaking down it further below. Strike first Act before your opponent can react, take initiative in any confrontation The “strike first” part of Cobra Kai’s motto obviously seems to apply more to Dallas’ offense more than their defense, but can definitely be incorporated for both. Offensively, striking first means putting the opposition on their heels by scoring early and often. With the weapons Dak Prescott has at his disposal in both the running and passing game, this should be one of the higher scoring units in the entire league. But as we’ve seen, they don’t always score early . Defensively striking first applies as well. Acting before the opponent can react is all about taking the initiative and disguising coverages pre-snap to create confusion/hesitation. This would allow Dallas’ defense to hopefully play with more confidence and aggressiveness. Strike hard Deliver powerful, decisive attacks to overwhelm the opponent The “strike hard” part of Cobra Kai’s motto seems to apply more to the defensive side of the ball than the offense, but again, it can be incorporated in both. Let’s start with the defense this time. Striking hard defensively means playing physically at the point of attack, in coverage, and especially when tackling. That means playing and hitting hard from the snap of the ball until the officials blow the whistle, making their presence known. Offensively, striking hard starts with the offensive line being physical in both the run game and in pass protection, with the physicality rippling through the rest of their playmakers when running routes/blocking in the passing game, or on the ground when running the ball. No mercy Aim to dominate and in the conflict quickly, show no hesitation or compassion The “no mercy” part of Cobra Kai’s part of motto applies both individually and to the team as a whole from the players to the coaching staff. The “no mercy” mindset is how the Cowboys should play this year. That means everyone being relentless in the pursuit of complete domination against any opposition throughout the ballgame on a play-by-play basis. It means pounding opponents into submission and enjoying it, both quickly and efficiently. This part of Cobra Kai’s motto could lead to unfortunate penalties or overaggressive play, which is why finding the right balance when showing “no mercy” could be difficult. But, finding the right balance could be a difference maker for the teams overall attitude/mindset. What movie or show would you have the Cowboys adopt as their mantra?
author: Brian Martin

title: Why the 2025 Cowboys pass rush was better than you’ve been told
summary: The Cowboys’ pass rush was better than its 35 sacks suggest. In fact, when measuring total pressures rather than sacks, Dallas’ front seven ranked sixth in the NFL in 2025. Surprised? Read on. It used to be that the key to slowing down modern offenses was to get pressure on the passer. The assumption was […]
full_text: The Cowboys’ pass rush was better than its 35 sacks suggest. In fact, when measuring total pressures rather than sacks, Dallas’ front seven ranked sixth in the NFL in 2025. Surprised? Read on. It used to be that the key to slowing down modern offenses was to get pressure on the passer. The assumption was that if the quarterback is pressured or hurried, it’s much more likely he’ll make a mistake and turn the ball over or make enough bad passes to get off the field. Of course, pressuring the passer only works if your secondary is any good. And the 2025 Cowboys secondary was the exact opposite of whatever “good” is. Not breaking any new ground here but the three 2025 secondaries that consistently stand out for just absolutely smothering passing games in zone coverage when I'm charting WRs: – Seahawks – Chargers – Eagles Team that stood out for doing whatever the opposite of that is: -… — Matt Harmon (@MattHarmon_BYB) July 22, 2026 In the NFL, pressure has traditionally been measured by sacks. And at first glance, the 2025 Cowboys pass rush wasn’t very good, ranking only T22nd with 35 sacks. But considering that NFL QBs last year only held the ball between 2.2 – 2.5 seconds on average, just penetrating the pocket and pressuring the QB to throw early must be considered a success for the defense. So to get a true feel for the effectiveness of the pass rush, you’ve got to measure a defense’s ability to pressure the quarterback, either in form of sacks, hits, or hurries. And that’s exactly what we’re going to do today. We’re first going to look at the total pressures generated by the interior D-line, then the pressure generated by the edge rushers, and then try to figure out what both of it means for 2026. In addition to sacks, the folks at Pro Football Focus (PFF) also keep track of QB hits and QB hurries. By their definition, a hit is when a QB is knocked down but not sacked, a hurry is when a QB is forced to move in the pocket in some other way than simply stepping up in the pocket to throw. Add up all three and divide the sum by the total pass rushing snaps and you get a number which we’ll call pressure percentage . Across the NFL last year, interior defenders averaged a pressure percentage of 7.8%, while edge defenders averaged a 11.8% pressure percentage. Interior Defenders On paper, the Cowboys got a big boost when they added Quinnen Williams in the middle of the season last year, But did his addition actually lead to improved numbers for the D-line? Boy, did it ever! Not only did he elevate the whole unit from a pressure percentage of 9.3% to 11.5%, he was immediately the best player of the unit with a 16.4% pressure percentage. And here’s the part where it gets really interesting: the Cowboys defensive tackles ranked No. 1 in pressure percentage in the NFL last year. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } 2025 team ranking by DI pressure percentage Rank Team PRSH PRSS PRSS% 1 DAL 1,370 143 10.4% 2 DEN 1,670 168 10.1% 3 LA 1,511 150 9.9% 4 TEN 1,130 112 9.9% 5 NE 1,346 132 9.8% 6 SEA 1,451 139 9.6% 7 PHI 1,430 130 9.1% 8 KC 1,007 89 8.8% 9 MIN 1,348 118 8.8% 10 TB 1,530 133 8.7% … 15 NFL Avg. 41,730 3,260 7.8% … 32 SF 1,041 51 4.9% Without Williams, and with a 9.3 pressure percentage, the Cowboys DI was already a top 10 unit. But with Williams, the unit finished as the No. 1 unit in the league for the entire season, even topping out at an average pressure percentage of 11.5% in the second half of the season. But it’s not all about Williams. If you look at Osa Odighizuwa’s numbers, and the 49ers’ ranking in the table above, it becomes clear why that trade happened – but you’ve got to wonder whether the Cowboys were fleeced in a trade that gave them a third-round pick for one of the top DI players in the league. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } TOP 10 DI players 2025 (min 150 PRSH) Rank (out of 113) Player Team PRSH PRSS PRSS% 1 Quinnen Williams (DAL) DAL 195 32 16.4% 2 Jeffery Simmons TEN 465 64 13.8% 3 Zach Allen DEN 555 73 13.2% 4 Chris Jones KC 494 63 12.8% 5 Osa Odighizuwa DAL 420 52 12.4% 6 Milton Williams NE 293 36 12.3% 7 Jowon Briggs NYJ 320 38 11.9% 8 Jer’Zhan Newton WAS 228 27 11.8% 9 Christian Barmore NE 428 50 11.7% 10 Kobie Turner LAR 477 55 11.5% … 32 Kenny Clark DAL 462 44 9.5% 40 Quinnen Williams (NYJ) NYJ 215 19 8.8% 99 Solomon Thomas DAL 233 12 5.2% The table above also raises another question: who is going to replace the 64 pressures Odighizuwa and Solomon Thomas combined for last year? Williams will obviously take up part of the slack, but that’s only if he maintains last year’s pace in Dallas. If he regresses to his Jets pace, that gap becomes even bigger, and Kenny Clark is likely maxed out already. The Cowboys added two additional DTs in free agency, but their strength might not be about creating pressure, at least not if you’re going by last year. Jonathan Bullard: 116 pass rush opportunities, 3 pressures, 2.6 PRSS% Otito Ogbonnia: 72 pass rush opportunities, 3 pressures, 4.2 PRSS% The last piece in the puzzle is rookie LT Overton, but the fourth-round pick may be more of a project than a contributor for the next one or two years. Perhaps scheme is the answer, perhaps more production from the edge rushers is the answer, but the hole that Odighizuwa leaves won’t be easy to fill. Edge Rushers We saw that the interior defenders sit at the top of the league with their 10.4 pressure percentage. Might the edge defenders also be better than they are widely perceived? title: Cowboys news: Things to look for at training camp
summary: Cowboys to Oxnard 2026: What to watch for at training camp – Cody Warren, Inside the Star Pay attention to these storylines when the Cowboys open camp. Cowboys training camp starts July 28th in Oxnard, California, and I’m ready for the guessing and speculation about players and positions to start. We’ve spent the entire offseason thinking […]
full_text: OXNARD, CA - AUGUST 05: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer slaps hands with his players during the Los Angeles Rams - Dallas Cowboys joint Training Camp on August 05, 2025, at the River Ridge Playing Fields in Oxnard, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cowboys to Oxnard 2026: What to watch for at training camp – Cody Warren, Inside the Star Pay attention to these storylines when the Cowboys open camp. Cowboys training camp starts July 28th in Oxnard, California , and I’m ready for the guessing and speculation about players and positions to start. We’ve spent the entire offseason thinking about what we think the roster will look like, what players will start, who will break out this season, and what will a Christian Parker defense actually look like. Everything up to this point is just talk until the pads come on. I don’t want everyone to lose their minds over every practice clip, either. Someone will catch an amazing pass over a practice squad player or camp body and start thinking that player is the second coming of Jerry Rice. Let’s pump the brakes right now. There are bigger storylines to watch. Will DeMarvion Overshown and Shavon Revel Jr. Look Like Themselves at Training Camp? I haven’t heard anything to make me think these two will not be ready for training camp. Overshown’s game depends on speed , reaction, and playing without hesitation. Will he be thinking about his knee while trying to chase down offensive players? We will know pretty quick. I’ll be watching how quickly he closes, how his change of direction is, and how he responds after getting a few physical practices in. Shavon Revel Jr. has similar issues, just at a different position. We know a cornerback cannot play scared. I want to see how Revel plants his foot, turns, runs, and if he trusts his body with a receiver coming out of a break. If we see an aggressive Revel in press coverage and fighting with receivers, that will tell me more than a practice report. As a Cowboys fan and watching what this defense went through last season, two great players don’t just need to be available, I want to see them being explosive. The Running Back Two Job Is Wide Open at Training Camp Javonte Williams enters training camp as the unrivaled number one back and that was solidified with statements from Will McClay . Even without Will McClay’s comment, I don’t think anyone was going to argue who the lead dog is. The real battle will be behind him. As we all know, and I have heavily talked about in the past, Jaydon Blue has speed on top of speed. This guy has the attributes to be the home run hitter on the ground. Blue’s biggest issue last season was maturity and I think that has been fixed. Phil Mafah is the opposite of Blue. He’s big, real big, and plays with force and a blatant disregard for defensive players safety and I like it. This could be the guy who helps solve our red zone woes. Malik Davis came on strong at the end of the season and should not be counted out. Yes, he has bounced around on a few teams, but seemed to put it all together at the end of 2025. He’s not great at anything, but seemed to be good at just about everything. Sounds like a RB2. The two other running backs headed into training camp are Israel Abanikanda and rookie Dominic Richardson. Israel is a player the Cowboys liked coming out of the University of Pittsburgh in 2023. He is a speedy back who broke Tony Dorsett’s single-game rushing record while at Pitt. The best Dallas Cowboys player to wear No. 19 might surprise some people – Luke Norris, The Landry Hat What do you guys think? Do you agree this is the best player in Cowboys history to wear number 19? Welcome back to The Landry Hat’s series covering the best Dallas Cowboys players to wear every jersey number from No. 0 to No. 99 . Well, we’ve officially reached the one-fifth mark of our journey, as we’ve come to our 20th entry, and we’ve got a nice little battle here for the No. 19 slot. So, without further ado, let’s take a quick look at everyone who’s donned the digit for America’s Team over the years. Lance Alworth, WR Miles Austin, WR Brice Butler, WR Amari Cooper, WR Ryan Flournoy, WR Noah Igbinoghene, CB John Jett, P Keyshawn Johnson, WR Trey Lance, QB Clint Longley, QB Brett Maher, K Lance Rentzel, WR Kevin Sweeney, QB From an overall historical perspective, the most notable name on this list is Lance Alworth, who’s the only player listed above to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. But as he made his name with the San Diego Chargers and only played a pair of seasons with the Cowboys, he’s out, although it should be noted that he won a ring in the first of those two campaigns, catching 34 passes for 487 yards with a pair of touchdowns in 1971. Going back to that same era, Lance Rentzel had a solid four-year run with Dallas from 1967 to 1970, catching 183 passes for 3,521 yards with 31 touchdowns. But he’s on the outside looking in as well. When all was said and done, though, this became a two-man race between players who suited up in this century. Now, many might go with Amari Cooper in this slot. And he’s certainly got a strong case, as he had a strong three-and-a-half-year run in Big D, catching 292 passes for 3,893 yards with 27 touchdowns and earning a pair of Pro Bowl selections. But our call here is Miles Austin, which might surprise some people. But it might also surprise some to know (or remember) that he also made a pair of Pro Bowls and that his best season was better than any that Cooper had during his entire career. Throw in the fact that he also returned kicks, and his value was just higher. 8 offense vs. defense training camp battles to watch-Mike Poland, Blogging the Boys As things heat up, keep a close eye on these hotly contested battles. Training camp is where roster battles are decided, but some of the most interesting work in Oxnard come from players competing on opposite sides of the football. The Cowboys have a strong mix of established stars and young players looking to break out, which should create plenty of entertaining one-on-one matchups. These battles will not determine starting jobs on their own, but tell us a lot about which players are improving, who may be ready for a bigger role and where Dallas could still have concerns entering the season. Here are eight matchups Cowboys fans should be watching closely throughout training camp this year. 8. Anthony Smith vs. Devin Moore This rookie-on-rookie matchup could affect the back end of two unsettled position groups. Smith’s size and vertical speed will test Moore’s ability to turn and run, while Moore’s length should challenge Smith to beat press coverage and win contested catches. 7. Drew Shelton vs. L.T. Overton Two fourth-round rookies will have plenty to prove when the pads come on. Shelton’s athleticism will test Overton’s ability to push the edge, while Overton’s power and versatility should provide an early examination of Shelton’s technique and anchor. 6. Brevyn Spann-Ford vs. Jalen Thompson Spann-Ford has an opportunity to overtake Luke Schoonmaker and establish himself as the Cowboys’ second tight end. His size will create problems at the catch point, but Thompson’s experience, instincts and physicality should provide a difficult test in both coverage and the running game. Daily discussion question: What do you believe will 100% happen through the first few practices of camp?

title: Denver Broncos roster review: Running back J.K. Dobbins
summary: J.K. Dobbins is heading into his 7th season in the NFL with a checkered, injury-laden career to date. He spent his first four years in the NFL with the Baltimore Ravens, playing in just 24 games in his time there. Dobbins then headed to the Chargers in 2024 and churned out a 905-yard rushing season […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 26: J.K. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos stiff arms DaRon Bland #26 of the Dallas Cowboys during the second quarter in the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 26, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images J.K. Dobbins is heading into his 7th season in the NFL with a checkered, injury-laden career to date. He spent his first four years in the NFL with the Baltimore Ravens, playing in just 24 games in his time there. Dobbins then headed to the Chargers in 2024 and churned out a 905-yard rushing season in 13 games before getting sidelined with an MCL injury. Dobbins joined the Broncos in 2025 and made it 10 games before being put on injured reserve with a Lisfranc injury. Dobbins signed a two-year $16 million extension this year and enters as the #1 RB on the roster, looking to chase that elusive full season of play. Player Profile J.K. Dobbins | Running Back | Denver Broncos Height: 5′ 10″ Weight: 212 pounds Age: 27 years old Experience: 7th season College: Ohio State 2025 stats: 153 rushes for 772 yards (5.0 ypc), 4 TD, 11 receptions 2026 outlook with the Broncos When healthy, Dobbins is an excellent NFL starting running back. He runs with power, has great vision, and is a capable blocker. The Broncos offense last season started hitting its stride midseason with Dobbins and was the best offense we’ve seen in Denver in a very long time in any consistent manner. The question about his durability is still front and center. He’s on a prove-it deal with the Broncos. The Broncos shrewdly drafted a guy in Jonah Coleman who is more than capable of becoming a starting back just in case Dobbins misses time. We’re all knocking on wood, throwing a pinch of salt over our shoulders, and hoping that Dobbins can stay healthy this season, as having a competent running game will go a long way to getting this team back into the playoffs for the third straight season. Final Word There is no doubt in my mind that Dobbins is at the top of the depth chart for the Broncos’ running back roster. He’s a talented ball carrier who forces defenses to stack boxes to slow him down. He churns out runs and is one of the guys I trust to be able to see blocks open up before they happen and hit the hole in time to crank out positive runs. This is a make-or-break season for him at the end of the day. If he can just put together a healthy season for the first time in his career, it will silence a lot of the naysayers. More importantly, it will incentivize the Broncos to extend him to a longer-term contract.

title: Broncos place OL Nick Gargiulo on the PUP and LB Jordan Turner on the NFI
summary: The Denver Broncos announced on Sunday that they have placed offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo on the Physically Unable to Perform list (PUP) and linebacker Jordan Turner on the Actice/Non-Football Injury list (NFI). Gargiulo, a former 7th-round pick, missed all of the 2025 season after suffering a season-ending knee injury during the preseason and now will […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - DECEMBER 21: Jordan Turner #55 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos announced on Sunday that they have placed offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo on the Physically Unable to Perform list (PUP) and linebacker Jordan Turner on the Actice/Non-Football Injury list (NFI). We've designated G Nick Gargiulo as Active/Physically Unable to Perform and ILB Jordan Turner as Active/Non-Football Injury. 📰 » https://t.co/adXK0dW15v pic.twitter.com/7T4iq77PCt — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) July 26, 2026 Gargiulo, a former 7th-round pick, missed all of the 2025 season after suffering a season-ending knee injury during the preseason and now will start camp on the PUP. He can be activated off the PUP at any time during camp when he is able to pass a physical, but in the meantime, he will be sidelined for the start of camp. Gargiulo is likely on the outside looking in when it comes to a roster spot, so he’ll need to get healthy quickly if he wants a spot on the Broncos’ 53-man roster. A spot on the practice squad seems more likely for him, but we shall see how it plays out. The team also announced that they have placed linebacker Jordan Turner on the NFI list. There is no word on why Turner has been placed on the NFI list, but he will start camp sidelined. Like Gargiulo, he can be activated off the list at any point during camp; he just needs to pass a physical and get healthy. Turner was expected to be a player in the Broncos’ linebacker competition, so this is a blow to his chances, especially if he is sidelined for an extended period of time. With Turner sidelined, this opens up an opportunity for Karene Reid, Levelle Bailey, and rookies Red Murdock and Taurean York. We shall see if any of these linebackers can separate themselves from the competition in the coming days and weeks ahead. I still wouldn’t rule out the team adding a veteran into the mix, but that all depends on how the young players look and how long Turner is going to be sidelined.
