title: Denver Broncos roster review: Quarterback Jarrett Stidham
summary: When Bo Nix suffered his season ending injury against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Playoffs, the weight of the world was placed on backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham’s shoulders. The veteran quarterback hadn’t thrown a regular season pass since finishing out the final three-game stretch of the 2023 season replacing Russell Wilson. But when […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 25: Jarrett Stidham #8 of the Denver Broncos looks on during the second quarter in the AFC Championship Playoff game against the New England Patriots at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Bo Nix suffered his season ending injury against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Playoffs, the weight of the world was placed on backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham’s shoulders. The veteran quarterback hadn’t thrown a regular season pass since finishing out the final three-game stretch of the 2023 season replacing Russell Wilson. But when Nix went down, Stidham was given a gargantuan task to help lead the Broncos to victory over the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game. After an early three-and-out to open the game, Denver’s offense rebounded with a second drive touchdown. At that point in time, it seemed like “Stiddy” and his offensive teammates could do enough to punch their ticket to the Super Bowl. Alas, their efforts fizzled the remainder of the game and zero points were added to the scoreboard through the final three quarters. Stidham’s lost fumble and interception proved to be costly and the Broncos’ miraculous season would come to a crushing end with a 10-7 loss. Entering his fourth year with the Broncos, the veteran quarterback hopes to be the primary backup to Nix for the 2026 season. Will Stidham earn the backup job with the Broncos once again or will Sam Ehlinger find a way to unseat him as the primary backup to Nix? Let’s discuss. Player Profile Age: 30 | Experience: Seventh Year | College: Auburn | Height: 6’3” | Weight: 215 pounds 2025 Statistics : 17 regular season appearances as Nix’s backup. No regular season passing statistics. 17 of 31 for 133 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception in AFCCG vs. Patriots. Three sacks taken, one lost fumble. Jarrett Stidham’s 2026 outlook with the Broncos At this juncture, I’d presume Stidham is the favorite to win the backup job. Nevertheless, it certainly isn’t an absolute guarantee. While many fans were upset with Stidham’s performance in the AFC Championship Game, there is no denying Stidham has more experience with and knowledge of Head Coach Sean Payton’s system than Ehlinger. That in itself is enough for me to have him as the early favorite in the competition. Also, I’d venture to say that Stidham’s overall mechanics and ability as a quarterback are a bit more advanced than Ehlinger’s. Though I would argue Ehlinger may have a slight edge when it comes to arm strength. But is an edge in one category enough to supplant a longtime NFL backup? It may also be of note that Stidham was the first outside free agent signing the Broncos made when Payton took over. He is a player Denver’s offensive staff clearly think high off. Both Payton and newly crowned Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb have given nothing but praise for Stidham during his stint with the Broncos. Final Thoughts My gut tells me that Stidham will wind up earning the Broncos’ backup job for their ‘26 gridiron campaign for the reasons above. In the final year of his two-year contract signed in 2025, Stidham is scheduled to make roughly $8 million this season. Ehlinger on the other hand, accounts for just $2 million against the salary cap. If the Broncos opt to roll with Ehlinger, the Broncos will gain a decent amount of salary cap space—$4.5 million vs. 3.5 million in dead money. At the end of the day, I don’t think salary cap savings will have an impact on the staff’s decision at backup quarterback. The only question that will matter to them is “Who gives us the best shot to win each week if Nix isn’t available?” In my opinion, I’d give the edge to Stiddy.

(Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! For the first time since January, Bo Nix will be a full go on a football field. With the Denver Broncos training camp set to start in a few days, it’s the first time Nix will be a full-go since the infamous gut punch. Not that anyone needs a reminder, but the Broncos had just recorded one of the best wins in franchise history after beating Josh Allen and the favored Buffalo Bills 33-30 in overtime. Broncos Country was giddy and in an absolute party mood. It was 30 minutes later that the news of Nix breaking his ankle hit, and the vibe swung to despair. All eyes will be on Nix when he steps foot on the practice field and will remain on him through the rest of training camp and the preseason. No amount of words will fight off the narrative battle and the questions of Nix’s ankle until people see. Still, Broncos head coach Sean Payton and Nix have done what they can to dispel those questions. Namely, that Nix will somehow be limited now, and he won’t have the same mobility because of the ankle injury. As Payton said to the media in the middle of June: “I think I mentioned this last week, and I think this is important. I don’t think when he’s fully recovered, and he’s out here participating (that) you’re going to see someone that doesn’t move. All of that, some of his superpowers, his ability to move and not get sacked, find throws — I don’t think any of that will be impacted at all. I think he’s working extremely hard on this recovery. I think he’s more than ahead of schedule.” Nix took the will he be the same QB and mobility question and flipped it on its head. “Well, my concern is they say it’s back healthy, as good as new, and I hadn’t really been like that in a couple years,” Nix said to the media in June, laughing. “So my concern is maybe moving around a little bit better.” This also isn’t the first time Nix has dealt with an ankle injury in his football life, so he knew what to do and how to approach it. “When I had an ankle injury in high school, we won the state championship,“ Nix said to the media. ”When I had an ankle injury in college, we went and won a lot of games at Oregon. Now I expect it to be the same thing. For me, it’s just another bump in the road. It’s another thing, but one thing I don’t necessarily worry about right now is my health. We play this game long enough, you get hurt, and you get bumps and bruises. We have great medicine nowadays and great training to where you get back on the field. “You look at some of the worst injuries you could get, and guys are playing the next year and feel stronger and better than ever. I think just where we are as a culture and a society, we just heal fast. We have a good operation of getting back healthy. I don’t worry about that at all. I think it probably won’t be the last time I’m injured and miss a couple games, but hopefully that’s not the case. Just take it however it comes and take it day-by-day. For right now, just getting back healthy and getting back to where once this season comes, it’s just right in the past for me, and I don’t even think about it.” Yes, all eyes will be on Nix as he steps on the football field as an active participant for the first time since his injury in January. What they see will be the quarterback who outdueled Allen for one of the best wins in Broncos’ history. And as Nix said, he may be even better.

(Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With training camp just days away, it’s time to start our Bubble Watch series. For those new to the site, every week during training camp and the preseason, our staff of 11 voters will make their predictions for every player we believe is currently on the roster bubble. We’ll both list out a chart of all of our votes, and break down all of the training camp battles and trends for each player. We kick off the series by predicting the fate of 15 different players who I picked as entering training camp on the roster bubble. Below are our predictions, and under that is a more detailed breakdown of each position battle. View Link Quarterback: Assumed in: Jared Goff, Teddy Bridgewater Luke Altmyer: 1 “IN” vote For now, I believe Detroit’s top two quarterback positions are set. That could certainly change if Teddy Bridgewater struggles this preseason, but I think the Lions value his mentorship abilities too much to put him on the bubble. That leaves the conversation as to whether undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer can justify a spot on Detroit’s 53-man roster as QB3. Entering camp, only one staffer—Brett Whitefield—has him in. Running back: Assumed in: Jahmyr Gibbs, Isiah Pacheco, Sione Vaki Jacob Saylors: 9 “IN” votes Again, some may take issue with Sione Vaki being an assumed in, but he’s arguably Detroit’s best special team player, and I don’t see the team departing with him. As of now, it really feels like only Jacob Saylors could justify keeping a fourth running back after a strong special teams outing in 2025. But if Kye Robichaux or Jabari Small show out in the preseason, they could work their way onto the bubble. Wide receiver: Assumed in: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, Greg Dortch Cedrick Wilson Jr.: 8 “IN” votes Dominic Lovett: 8 votes Tom Kennedy: 1 vote Jackson Meeks: 0 votes Detroit’s 1-4 receivers feel pretty set for the time being, and most of our staff has the Lions keeping two others: veteran Cedrick Wilson Jr. and second-year wideout Dominic Lovett. But a few staffers had Detroit only keeping five receivers, and Tom Kennedy snuck in a vote after some surprise special team contributions last year. I found it mildly surprising that Jackson Meeks didn’t receive a vote, but he also still feels like a bit of a project as he continues to work at both tight end and wideout. Tight end: Assumed in: Sam LaPorta, Brock Wright Tyler Conklin: 11 “IN” votes Miles Kitselman: 1 vote Zach Horton: 0 votes It should be noted that most Pride of Detroit staffers made their predictions before Conklin was placed on the Physically Unable to Perform list to start training cam p . However, we still don’t know the severity of the injury he suffered during spring practices, so it’s still very possible he wins the TE3 spot. That said, undrafted rookie Miles Kitselman—one of Detroit’s most praised UDFA signings—also managed to get in a vote. And if Conklin sits for an extended amount of practices, don’t be surprised if Kitselman, Meeks, or Horton start to get some hype. Offensive tackle: Assumed in: Penei Sewell, Blake Miller, Larry Borom Giovanni Manu: 3 votes Colby Sorsdal: 0 votes Is this the end of the line for Giovanni Manu? Interior offensive line: Assumed in: Tate Ratledge, Cade Mays, Christian Mahogany, Miles Frazier Ben Bartch: 11 votes Juice Scruggs: 11 votes Seth McLaughlin: 0 votes Michael Niese: 0 votes Even though the starting left guard position is up for grabs and there’s a lot of new competition among Detroit’s interior offensive line depth, the entire staff is unanimous agreement about the roster spots filled by this group. Ben Bartch will challenge for the starting left guard position—and should, at worst, be an upgrade of Michael Niese. author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Discussion: Who is the Lions’ most important positional coach?
summary: Head coaches and coordinators are among the first people praised for a good season or blamed for a poor one. However, a team’s success runs deeper than those spots on the coaching staff. Positional coaches are often underappreciated and overlooked, given that their successes or failures are typically not obvious to the untrained eye. If […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) talks to quarterbacks coach Mark Brunell during warm up ahead of the Cleveland Browns game at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 28, 2025. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Head coaches and coordinators are among the first people praised for a good season or blamed for a poor one. However, a team’s success runs deeper than those spots on the coaching staff. Positional coaches are often underappreciated and overlooked, given that their successes or failures are typically not obvious to the untrained eye. If a receiver runs a great route, the offensive coordinator often gets praised for the play call, not the receivers coach that taught it. If a defensive back makes a great read and breaks up a pass, the defensive backs coach does not always get credit for helping with a week’s worth of film review and play recognition. When a backup linebacker steps into the game and plays well, our first thought is not about how good of a job the linebackers coach did preparing that group ahead of time. The Detroit Lions have an ample number of position coaches that play a key role in their success (and failure at times). Of these names, who is the most important? Today’s Question of the Day is: Who is the Lions’ most important positional coach? My answer: Hank Fraley. There are no shortage of important coaches on the Lions staff. The relationship between quarterback and quarterback coach is critical to growth and success, and the Lions seemingly have a good duo with Jared Goff and Mark Brunell. Scottie Montgomery (wide receivers) and Jim O’Neil (safeties) have the subtitle of associate and assistant head coach, respectively, highlighting their importance to Dan Campbell’s crew. Elsewhere, Kacy Rodgers’ role as defensive line coach and run game coordinator, coupled with his extensive resume, make him an excellent pairing with a young defensive coordinator in Kelvin Sheppard. However, the Lions live and die by their offensive line, and the man at the center of it is himself a former center, Hank Fraley. When the Lions were thriving in 2023 and 2024, it was Fraley’s offensive line that was paving the way. From protecting Goff and allowing plays to develop downfield to creating massive running lanes for Jahmyr Gibbs to sprint through, the blocking up front made the Lions a successful team. Last season was the first time that the Lions took a step back since Campbell took over in 2021, and it is no coincidence that the Lions also underwent a significant reshuffle on the offensive line that same year. Losing Frank Ragnow and Kevin Zeitler was a difficult task, and while rookie Tate Ratledge performed admirably, cohesion across the line faltered. Fraley has proven himself to be a brilliant mind when it comes to blocking schemes, hence his recent title of run game coordinator. However, a coach can only do so much when his starting lineup is changing every week. In 2026, the Lions took some significant actions towards establishing a consistent offensive line going forward. Penei Sewell shifts to left tackle, replacing the veteran Taylor Decker. The team signed Cade Mays to firm up the interior. In the draft, they selected Blake Miller to man the right side of the line. Ratledge returns at right guard, while Christian Mahogany is the frontrunner for an open competition at left guard. Aside from the uncertainty at left guard—a battle that will play out in training camp—the Lions have put forth a lot of answers in response to a subpar 2025 campaign. Now that the team has restocked their talent pool, the onus is now on Fraley to get the best out of this offensive line group. If that happens, the Lions could be looking at a quick rebound.
author: John Whiticar

title: Kerby Joseph among 3 Detroit Lions players placed on PUP
summary: The Detroit Lions have placed three players on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list ahead of the start of training camp. The team announced on Sunday that Kerby Joseph, Brian Branch, and Tyler Conklin will start on the PUP list. It’s worth noting that all three players are free to come off the PUP […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31), left, and safety Brian Branch (32) walk off the field after practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The Detroit Lions have placed three players on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list ahead of the start of training camp. The team announced on Sunday that Kerby Joseph, Brian Branch, and Tyler Conklin will start on the PUP list. It’s worth noting that all three players are free to come off the PUP list at any time, and it’s quite common for players to be taken off within days of the start of training camp. However, if the players remain on the PUP list throughout training camp and through roster cutdowns, they move to the reserve/PUP list and must miss at least the first four games of the season. Branch is likely to stay on the list for some time. He suffered a torn Achilles at the start of December, and coach Dan Campbell did not sound optimistic about his chances to return to the field at any point in training camp. “Uh, I don’t know. I mean, I guess there’s always a chance,” Campbell said. While Branch was expected to start on PUP, the same can’t be said for Joseph. The other Lions starting safety teased earlier this weekend that he may avoid the PUP list , tweeting, ‘“How much yall wanna bet im not on there.” Joseph has been dealing with a knee injury that caused him to miss the last 11 games last season. The condition, while unknown, apparently does not have surgery as an option, and Detroit has been doing everything they possibly can to manage it. That may include giving him a late start to training camp. “We are trying to be as smart as we can and not push this until we absolutely have to because once we’ve done that,” coach Dan Campbell said in the spring. “then we’ll know one way or another.” Tyler Conklin suffered an unknown injury during spring practices. We’ll likely get some clarification on his status when Campbell is expected to meet with the media ahead of Wednesday’s first training camp practice.

title: Discussion: Where will the Detroit Lions’ offense rank in 2026?
summary: With Detroit Lions training camp officially opening up this week, it’s time to fit in some last-minute predictions for the 2026 team. In a lot of ways, this team will likely sink or swim by their offense. When Detroit’s offense is humming, they’re one of the most dangerous teams in football. When it struggles… well, […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16), left, talk to offensive coordinator Drew Petzing before practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images With Detroit Lions training camp officially opening up this week, it’s time to fit in some last-minute predictions for the 2026 team. In a lot of ways, this team will likely sink or swim by their offense. When Detroit’s offense is humming, they’re one of the most dangerous teams in football. When it struggles… well, you saw what happened last year. Obviously, if this team plans on making a Super Bowl run, they’ll need help from both sides of the ball. However, most week’s their offense is likely going to carry them. So today’s Question of the Day is: Where will the Lions’ offense rank in 2026? My answer: Well, last year felt pretty close to a worst-case scenario, and here’s where Detroit ranked in many statistical categories: 6.0 yards per play — 3rd 28.3 points per game — 4th 7.4 yards per pass attempt — 4th 103.6 passer rating — 3rd 4.6 yards per carry — 9th 7th in DVOA 9th in EPA per play 12th in success rate So by almost every measure, they were a top-10 offense. But when you get to some of the more revealing, advanced statistics, it was closer to 10th than fifth. The question, to me, isn’t whether this will be a top-10 offense. It absolutely should be. The question is will it be a top-five offense? A top-two offense? The best offense? Obviously, the Lions invested in the offensive line with the signing of Cade Mays and the drafting of Blake Miller. Will the completely reformed offensive line be a noticeable improvement out of the gate? That’s hard to say with so many moving parts, including a completely new offensive coordinator. Speaking of which, that’s a reason to be hopeful with the Lions offense in 2026. While Drew Petzing certainly doesn’t have a spotless resume, he’s shown more in the OC role than last year’s coordinator John Morton. But, again, all of these “improvements” are theoretical at this point. Not to mention the backfield is almost certainly worse with the trade of David Montgomery. Still, the Lions have a top-10 quarterback, a top-five receiver, a top-five tight end, a top-two running back, and arguably the best offensive tackle in football. I am willing to say with confidence they’ll be a top-five offense, but I can’t commit to much more than that until I see the offensive line come together and Petzing find some comfort in this offense. Where do you think the Lions will rank in offense in 2026? Vote below and share your thoughts in the comment section.

title: Penei Sewell exclusive interview: Lions OC Drew Petzing already impressing
summary: As part of the celebration of bringing back their fan-favorite, Hot Orange Chicken, Panda Express partnered with Detroit Lions star left tackle Penei Sewell for an event at their location in Livonia, Michigan on Middlebelt road. In between the pictures and questions from fans, I was able to sit down with Sewell for a few […]
full_text: As part of the celebration of bringing back their fan-favorite, Hot Orange Chicken, Panda Express partnered with Detroit Lions star left tackle Penei Sewell for an event at their location in Livonia, Michigan on Middlebelt road. In between the pictures and questions from fans, I was able to sit down with Sewell for a few minutes to talk about the upcoming season, his early thoughts on Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, and where he stands on the cheeseburger saga that is currently taking place in the receiver room. How have you been prepping to move to the left side this offseason? “Just been doing the same things, but just now I’m flipping it. The training didn’t change, other than technique. And putting more hours into those techniques and trying to fine-tune them and get ready for camp.” Does it feel like you are going home almost? “A little bit, yeah. It wasn’t as uncomfortable as I thought it would be going back, but yeah, day by day, just trying to build on the foundation part and keep working.” We know you are going to be playing next to someone new this year, any thoughts on that competition between Mahogany, Frazier, and Bartch? “No, it’s still too early to really say. I haven’t even seen Bartch out there yet, but once camp starts and everybody is actually out there on the field, and at the end of the day, camp tells it all.” I know you are still only 25, but obviously you have been a leader in your room and the locker room for a minute–how do you think your upbringing and everything prepared you for that? “My upbringing definitely played a part. I think it was the people that I met along the way growing up. From high school, to college, and even to the league. Every step of the way gave me a piece that is important for right now. And just being myself, is ultimately the most important part of it all.” Last football question, any conversations with Drew Petzing? “Yeah, he is a smart guy. He talks really fast, but you can kinda just tell that there is a lot running in there (Petzing’s head), and that’s a smart man. But yeah, just still trying to get time together. In camp we will all be with each other from 8 to 8, so a lot of time to spend together.” Shifting to a couple of food questions now: what is your favorite go-to pre-game meal? “It depends. If it’s a 1 p.m. game, big breakfast, so eggs, bacon, waffle, and a smoothie. If it’s a night-time game, I am doing that in the morning, and then I gotta have a burger.” That pivots well into my last question then. I don’t know if you have seen the feud in the receiver room between Amon-Ra and TeSlaa, but have you had In-N-Out and Culver’s , and if you have, where do you stand? Sewell : “I haven’t had Culver’s, so I am going to say In-N-Out for now, but I’m not really a big In-N-Out fan, so yeah.” Cannon: “I want you to have Culver’s then, and maybe we can circle back.” Eric Loves Cooking: “Culver’s is fire!” ( If you like Detroit sports, food, or Pokémon, be sure to follow Eric’s Instagram ) Cannon: “See, Eric knows, too.” Sewell: “Really? Oh I gotta try it. Maybe on the way home.”

title: Detroit Lions 2026 training camp preview: Overcoming injuries at safety
summary: In this installment of our Detroit Lions 2026 training camp preview series, we wrap up the defensive side of the ball by examining the Lions’ safeties, speculating on current and future roles, and discussing how many players from this group could make the 53-man roster. Previous training camp previews: Roster construction Under the Brad Holmes […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31), left, and safety Brian Branch (32) walk off the field after practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images In this installment of our Detroit Lions 2026 training camp preview series, we wrap up the defensive side of the ball by examining the Lions’ safeties, speculating on current and future roles, and discussing how many players from this group could make the 53-man roster. Previous training camp previews: Quarterback: Can Luke Altmyer force a QB3 role? Running back: How RB roles could shift in 2026 Wide receiver: WR depth roles up for grabs Tight end: How many TEs will make the roster? Offensive tackle: Can Blake Miller win the starting RT job? Interior OL: How quickly will Cade Mays adapt to scheme? Defensive tackles: DT has upgraded starters, questionable depth Edge rushers: 4 big questions at the EDGE Linebackers: Adapting the LB room Cornerbacks: Nickel sets mean more opportunities for CBs Roster construction Under the Brad Holmes and Dan Campbell regime, the Lions have maintained a fairly consistent roster of safeties, typically keeping four or five safeties on the active roster. Let’s take a look at what they’ve done at safety in the previous five seasons: 2021 : Opened the season with four safeties but ended up with six at season’s close. 2022 : Started and ended the season with five safeties. 2023 : Started and ended the season with just four safeties. 2024 : Started with five safeties on the roster but operated and ended with four. 2025 : Opened with five safeties, fluctuated as high as six mid-season to deal with injuries, then ended with only four. Overcoming injuries The Lions entered 2025 with the best safety tandem in the NFL, with Brian Branch earning a spot in the Pro Bowl and Kerby Joseph coming off an All-Pro season. Unfortunately, Branch would suffer a torn Achilles in December , and Joseph failed to see the field after six games due to a lingering knee injury. The Lions turned to their depth for the majority of the season, with Thomas Harper and Avonte Maddox proving to be the steadiest contributors. This offseason, with Branch and Joseph’s statuses in question, the Lions secured a lot of safeties in the offseason with the plan of letting them battle it out for roles. Harper returns to Detroit for the third season on his rookie contract, and they re-signed Maddox , then added Christian Izien and Chuck Clark in free agency . Additionally, 2025 seventh-round pick Dan Jackson is returning from injury, practice squader Loren Strickland was re-signed, and rookie UDFA Aamaris Brown was added following the conclusion of the NFL Draft. There’s a chance Joseph will be able to overcome his knee injury to start the season, and Branch will quickly return to form once he fully recovers from injury, but until they have better answers, the Lions will open up their options in one of the most competitive training camp battles of 2026. The battleground Latest injury updates for Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph Branch is more than likely going to start training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list , and if he remains on the list at the start of the regular season, he’d have to miss the first four games of the season, at a minimum. Coach Dan Campbell said it’s still unclear if Branch will take that route, and declined to put a timetable on his return (he joked “December” so that the media would stop asking him), but he did also note that there have been “no setbacks” and that Branch is “putting in the work” to be ready as soon as possible. Things are even less clear for Joseph. His lingering knee problems are not something that can be fixed by surgery, and instead will need to be managed by him and the team throughout the season. In addition to allowing the knee to rest and recover this offseason, Joseph has worked with the team through a variety of different rehabilitation/treatment efforts, with the overarching plan being “not push this until we absolutely have to,” according to Campbell . The slow push forward has been designed to strengthen his knee, so that when it comes time to test it, he’ll be as prepared as possible—which may be sooner than most anticipated. On Saturday, Joseph offered some reassurances surrounding his health , taking to social media and suggesting that he will avoid starting training camp on the PUP list, meaning he’ll be able to practice as soon as he feels ready. How much and when the Lions test Joseph’s knee will be something the team figures out as camp progresses, but this is certainly a step in the right direction toward him finding the field in 2026. Assessing the potential challengers to start Because Joseph’s knee is still being assessed, the Lions will likely enter training camp believing they will need at least one, if not two, safeties to step into starting roles for Week 1. Let’s take a closer look at the players most likely challenging for the starting roles and what they need to show in camp to earn a spot. Thomas Harper (nine starts for Lions in 2025, 14 career) was released by the Raiders at cutdowns and claimed by the Lions in 2025. When Joseph proved unable to play, Harper was the first player coaches turned to, and he stepped into the starting single-high safety role in Week 7. When Branch went down in December, Maddox was promoted to the starting lineup, but coaches preferred him at single-high, and Harper showed his range by shifting to the other safety spot. With the experience and range to play both of the Lions’ safety spots, Harper’s biggest obstacle to a starting role is likely his overall NFL experience. Still only in his third season as a pro, Harper is still developing his game, but if he can show consistency in camp, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Lions turn to him again. Avonte Maddox (three starts for Lions in 2025, 44 career) has the positional range to play both safety spots, as well as in the slot, and provided a young Lions secondary with veteran leadership last season. Maddox meshed immediately with the Lions roster, with several giving him high praise in a recent video posted by the Lions social media team , including labeling him a leader, intelligent, smart, a playmaker, energy, a dawg, stud, and the ever-affectionate “unc.” For Maddox to make the 53-man roster and challenge for a starting role, he’ll need to prove that his skills are not redundant to other safeties on the roster, or that he is the better option. For example, his veteran leadership will surely be compared to Clark, while Maddox’s positional range will look very similar to Izien. Christian Izien (one start for Bucs in 2025, 15 career) was a starter for the Bucs in 2024, but was passed over in 2025, and he’s hoping a fresh start in Detroit will get him back in the starting lineup in 2026. With experience playing all five spots in the secondary and on five phases on special teams, Izien is a hungry, young player who is incredibly valuable to have on a 53-man roster. With Izien’s experience and versatility, he feels like a near lock for the roster, but how far he climbs up the depth chart will depend on his performance in training camp. The Lions put him in a starting role in OTAs/Minicamp in order to get him exposed to the Lions’ scheme and up to speed quickly. He’ll need to show coaches that he has retained what he learned in the spring and can grow even further. The potential is there for Izien to jump to the top of the chart, but he’ll need to show he can keep pace with players who have already been in the system for a season. Chuck Clark (five starts for the Steelers in 2025, 80 career) brings a load of experience to the Lions roster, and safeties coach Jim O’Neil noted in the spring that the veteran was an “alpha communicator” in the secondary . Like Izien, Clark was dropped into the starting lineup in the spring to help him acclimate quickly to the…

title: Packers to work out kicker Lenny Krieg on Monday
summary: Rookies report to Green Bay Packers training camp on Monday, which means that the full coaching staff will be back to work starting this week. The Packers haven’t made many transactions since the signing of their initial group of undrafted free agents post-draft, but that seems to be changing soon, as Matt Zenitz of CBS […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 8: Lenny Krieg #46 of the Atlanta Falcons warms up on the sideline during the first half of the NFL Preseason 2025 game between Detroit Lions and Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 8, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Rookies report to Green Bay Packers training camp on Monday, which means that the full coaching staff will be back to work starting this week. The Packers haven’t made many transactions since the signing of their initial group of undrafted free agents post-draft, but that seems to be changing soon, as Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports is reporting that the Packers will be working out kicker Lenny Krieg tomorrow. The #Packers are set to work out kicker Lenny Krieg tomorrow, a source tells @CBSSports . The 23-year old was 14 of 14 on field goals at the NFL scouting combine last year and was on the Falcons practice squad last season. Made a 57-yard field goal during the preseason last year. pic.twitter.com/3I14NIfzOh — Matt Zenitz (@mzenitz) July 26, 2026 Krieg, a German national, originally played soccer before transitioning to American football after his brother spent time in Wisconsin. Eventually, Krieg played in both the German league for the Berlin Adler and the European League with the Stuttgart Surge. In 2025, after kicking a perfect series of attempts at the NFL Scouting Combine, he earned an opportunity with the Atlanta Falcons. Krieg was the Falcons’ international exemption player last year and was not counted against the team’s practice squad numbers. After the year, he signed a reserve-futures deal with the New York Jets, as the Falcons cleared their coaching staff and front office. Krieg remained a member of the Jets until he was waived by the team on June 1st. Two days later, the Jets signed veteran kicker Jason Sanders. If Krieg ends up joining the Packers, he has the opportunity to become their international exemption player. Right now, Green Bay’s exempt player is edge rusher Dante Barnett, who was signed by the team in late October last year. Don’t be surprised if there’s a Krieg for Barnett swap tomorrow. If Krieg is added, this move would give the Packers three kickers, including rookie draft pick Trey Smack and also Lucas Havrisik. Generally, Green Bay doesn’t keep more than two kickers on the roster, so Havrisik could be on thin ice moving forward. Since the Packers inked their first round of undrafted free agents, here are the moves they’ve made leading up to training camp: Released QB Desmond Ridder Signed QB Tyrod Taylor Released K Brandon McManus Released DL James Ester Claimed CB MJ Devonshire Jr. off waivers Claimed WR Brenden Rice off waivers Signed CB Marlon Jones Released WR Jakobie Keeney-James Signed TE Luke Lachey

title: Colts futures watch: Which team bets are worth considering?
summary: Odds courtesy of FanDuel, please gamble responsibly The Colts are not a difficult team for sportsbooks to price right now. They have been stuck in the middle for years, and the current futures market reflects that. Indianapolis is listed at +370 to win the AFC South, +166 to make the playoffs, and -125 to go […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - JUNE 1: rIndianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen watches a drill during the Indianapolis Colts OTA on June 1, 2026 at the Indiana Farm Bureau Football Center in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Odds courtesy of FanDuel , please gamble responsibly The Colts are not a difficult team for sportsbooks to price right now. They have been stuck in the middle for years, and the current futures market reflects that. Indianapolis is listed at +370 to win the AFC South , +166 to make the playoffs , and -125 to go over 7.5 wins . Those numbers all point to the same general view: the Colts are not a bad team, but they are also not being priced like a team that has clearly made the jump. We won’t even look at the Super Bowl odds at +4500… The roster has talent, but the problem is that most of the team’s futures value still comes down to the same question that has followed the franchise for years: can the quarterback play be good enough? To win the AFC South: +370 The division price is interesting, but it is not screaming value. The Titans are probably not ready to fully take over the division, although they should be better and could absolutely take a game off the Colts. The Texans still look like a team in that 10-to-12 win range, especially with a defense that should remain one of the stronger units in the conference. The Jaguars are coming off a fantastic season with 13 wins and a close playoff loss, and while some regression is possible, they still have to be treated like one of the main teams to beat. That makes the math difficult for Indianapolis. With Houston and Jacksonville both reasonably expected to be around 10 wins or better, the Colts likely need 11 wins to feel good about winning the division. At 10 wins, they may have a chance, but they would need help and tiebreakers to break their way. At +370, the implied probability is about 21 percent, and that feels close to right. The Colts need to find roughly three more wins compared to last season, and it is hard to say the roster has improved enough on paper to assume that happens automatically. If Jones is fully healthy and plays like he did during the best stretch of last season, then the Colts can absolutely be competitive. If he is average, limited by the Achilles, or inconsistent against better teams, winning the division will be impossible. This is not a crazy bet. It is just not one with much clear value. To make the playoffs: +166 This is the most intriguing team future. The path to a playoff spot is much more realistic than the path to a division title. The Colts probably need 10 wins to feel good about making it, while nine wins at least keeps them in the conversation depending on the AFC wild-card picture. Finding two more wins is a lot easier to imagine than finding three or four, especially when last season had several games that slipped away. The Chiefs, Seahawks and Rams games come to mind. Those were the types of games that separate an average team from a playoff team. Indianapolis did not close enough of them, and that is why it stayed in the middle. If Shane Steichen takes a step forward as a coach, the defense performs better in bigger games, and Jones gives the offense steady quarterback play, the Colts can absolutely get to 10 wins. Taylor can still carry games, the offensive line should be strong, and the secondary has enough talent to be a legitimate strength. The question is whether the Colts can stop playing like a team that finds ways to finish around .500. At +166, making the playoffs is worth a look. It is not a lock by any means, but it gives you a better risk-reward profile than the division number because Indianapolis does not need to beat out both Houston and Jacksonville. It just needs to be good enough to get into the field. Of the team futures, this is the one I like best. Over 7.5 wins: -125 The win total feels properly priced. The Colts have lived around this number for years. They have been average, and sportsbooks are treating them like an average team again. That makes it hard to find a major edge. The over is very possible if Jones stays healthy. If he gives the Colts stable quarterback play for a full season, eight wins should be within reach, and there is a path to nine or 10 if the defense improves and the team closes games better. The roster should be good enough to avoid a complete collapse. The concern is that the number is not generous. At -125, you are paying extra juice on a line that already feels sharp. You also have to trust Jones’ health and consistency, which is not a small ask. If he misses time or regresses, the Colts could easily slide back toward seven wins or worse. This is not a bad bet because 8-9 wins is a very realistic outcome. It is just not an especially attractive one at the price. Final verdict The Colts’ team futures are mostly well priced. That makes sense because the market has figured out what this team has been for years: talented enough to stay relevant, flawed enough to miss the playoffs, and usually somewhere close to .500. The division bet at +370 is not unreasonable, but the Colts probably need 11 wins to win the AFC South, and that requires a bigger jump than I am comfortable betting on. The over 7.5 wins is also fair, although the price makes it less appealing given the quarterback health question. The best play is Colts to make the playoffs at +166 . It still depends heavily on Jones, Steichen and the defense being better in key moments, but it does not require Indianapolis to become the best team in the division. It only requires the Colts to turn a few close losses into wins and finally climb out of the middle.

title: Jaguars’ Cole Van Lanen To Open Camp on PUP List
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have placed starting left tackle Cole Van Lanen on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform list as the team is set to open their 2026 Training Camp, the organization announced Sunday. Offensive lineman Garrett DiGiorgio was also placed on the Active/PUP list in the same set of roster moves. Not Unexpected The decision […]
full_text: The Jacksonville Jaguars have placed starting left tackle Cole Van Lanen on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform list as the team is set to open their 2026 Training Camp, the organization announced Sunday. Offensive lineman Garrett DiGiorgio was also placed on the Active/PUP list in the same set of roster moves . Not Unexpected The decision comes as little surprise to anyone who tracked Van Lanen’s recovery throughout the spring. The lineman suffered a knee injury during the regular season finale against the Tennessee Titans on January 4th and was unable to suit up for the Wild Card playoff matchup against the Buffalo Bills the following week. With few details of the specific injury suffered, but multiple offseason reports outlining a possible accompanying offseason knee surgery, his presence throughout the offseason program has been heavily limited as a result. This combination of factors made it apparent from the earliest organized team activities that his return to full practice would extend well into the summer. No Harm, No Foul The coaching staff nonetheless expressed early confidence that Van Lanen would be back on the field at some point during Training Camp. Importantly, the timing of this roster designation works in Jacksonville’s favor. Because the team placed Van Lanen on the Active/PUP list before the league’s 53-man roster cutdown deadline, the Jaguars retain the ability to activate him at any point prior to that date with no restrictions on regular season availability. The Active/PUP designation simply reflects CVL’s current physical status. Once the medical staff determines he is ready to return to practice, he can be cleared and reintegrated into the active roster without any real consequence. This isn’t the first or last time this organization has navigated this process with a key contributor being on the offseason, Active/PUP. Defensive tackle Arik Armstead began the 2024 offseason on the Active/PUP list following offseason surgery, before being activated in August and going on to have one of his healthiest seasons, playing in all 17-games. The Jaguars will be hoping the timeline for Van Lanen follows a similar path as the regular season approaches. The stakes surrounding Van Lanen’s recovery are significant, with a tough early season slate for Jacksonville. After being acquired in a 2022 trade with the Green Bay Packers for a seventh-round pick under then-general manager Trent Baalke, CVL developed into one of the most valuable and versatile pieces on Jacksonville’s offensive line. In 2025, he appeared in all 16 games he was active for, making ten starts at four different positions along the line before ultimately settling in as the team’s primary left tackle. His performance at that spot was quietly among the best on the roster. According to Pro Football Focus, he allowed just nine total pressures and zero sacks at left tackle, while ESPN Analytics ranked him tenth among all offensive tackles in run block win rate. The Jaguars rewarded that production with a three-year extension signed late in the season. In Van Lanen’s absence, Walker Little is expected to fill the starting left tackle role once camp opens on Wednesday. If the recovery timeline pushes past the start of the regular season, swing tackle Chuma Edoga would also potentially be able to secure a roster spot as additional protection along the offensive line. That, however, is a future conversation for another day. Only time will tell. Van-Lanen’s recovery, and Walker Little’s performance, will both be major training camp storylines to watch over the coming weeks.

title: Chiefs News: Rookie Jadon Canady is making a good early impression
summary: The latest Over the first two days of training camp for the Kansas City Chiefs, it’s important to remember that these practices feature exclusively rookies, quarterbacks and select veterans before the real thing starts this week. So when a rookie stands out, it’s worth jotting down and anticipating a repeat performance among the veterans. There […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Jadon Canady #22 walks toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest Over the first two days of training camp for the Kansas City Chiefs , it’s important to remember that these practices feature exclusively rookies, quarterbacks and select veterans before the real thing starts this week. So when a rookie stands out, it’s worth jotting down and anticipating a repeat performance among the veterans. There are a couple of defensive backs who have been highlighted by local media in attendance this weekend, but the fourth-round pick from Oregon, Jadon Canady, flashed man-to-man coverage skills in the eyes of an old friend of the site, Pete Sweeney. Jadon Canady flashes early as Kansas City Chiefs look for answer at nickel | The Kansas City Star At Saturday’s initial workout — of the team’s three-day jumpstart for rookies and quarterbacks at training camp — Canady stood out during the red-zone 7-on-7 session. First, Canady broke up a pass by Patrick Mahomes intended for receiver Andrew Armstrong. Three plays later, he climbed over undrafted receiver Xavier Loyd and dove to pick off Justin Fields at the goal line. “I just grabbed my man, stayed attached to his hip,” he said Sunday. “The ball came out, and from there, pretty much for me, it’s ‘see the ball, get the ball.’” 2026 Kansas City Chiefs training camp: Latest intel, updates | ESPN One of the highlights at practice Sunday was during the 7-on-7 period inside the red zone. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes surveyed the field and then completed a pass to rookie receiver Cyrus Allen, who made a leaping catch in the back of the end zone between two defenders. “It’s still a surreal moment for me because I used to play the [Madden NFL] game with Pat a lot,” Allen, the Chiefs’ fifth-round draft pick this year, said of Mahomes. “I’m pretty familiar with what he [does]. That was my favorite team.” Chiefs Training Camp Notebook July 25: An unexpected rookie shines; Mahomes participates in practice | KSHB 41 Rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa got the best of Mahomes on Saturday when he almost picked off one of his passes. He kept an eye on Mahomes while in his zone coverage. Nwankpa stayed discipline and timed his jump when Mahomes thought the route was open. He also had a couple of additional deflections and an interception on quarterback Justin Fields on an option route. One Starting Job the Chiefs Are Happy They Don’t Have to Answer Today | Sports Illustrated Plenty of spots seem to be sorted out, but there’s a handful remaining to decide on. One of them appears to be the third linebacker job. There’s a world where starter Drue Tranquill shifts to a base SAM role and allows someone to slot in elsewhere, especially considering the departure of Leo Chenal to the Washington Commanders. Until proven or told otherwise, however, the race likely comes down to the duo of Jeffrey Bassa and Cooper McDonald. Kansas City may feel very relieved that it doesn’t have to make any decisions right now, as there’s plenty left to learn about both players. Chiefs cornerback volunteers before heading to training camp | KCTV5 Kristian Fulton volunteered with Habitat for Humanity in Olathe on Friday, July 24. Members of the Chiefs Red Coaters joined him for the project. Habitat KC is working to build 14 homes near 158th and Black Bob Road. The families who eventually live in the homes will be helped through Habitat’s affordable mortgage program. Nuggets for the Win: Tyson Foods gives Chiefs fans a shot at season tickets | KCTV 5 What’s New This Season Chiefs fans can enjoy the branded nuggets at home or at Arrowhead Stadium – but Tyson says it is sweetening the deal with a season ticket giveaway running through Sept. 9: Five winners will each receive a pair of season tickets Winners will be notified by Sept. 10 by Tyson Foods Enter the giveaway here Around the NFL Kraft: Patriots’ Gonzalez has offer to be ‘highest-paid’ CB ever | ESPN “We love Christian Gonzalez. We love him as a player, as a person, and that’s why we’ve made an offer to him to make him the highest-paid player to ever play that position in the NFL,” Kraft said Saturday morning before the team’s first practice of training camp. “And coincidentally, it is the highest contract in Patriots franchise history. So we’re glad we drafted him, he’s developed here, and we hope he’ll be with us for a long time.” Cardinals, QB Jacoby Brissett agree to reworked $15.5 million deal for 2026 season | NFL.com Brissett, 33, skipped most of the team’s offseason work, but reported for mandatory minicamp and on time for training camp. Heading into the second season of a two-year deal, Brissett was slated to make $4.88 million in base salary and has been seeking compensation more in line with other starting quarterbacks. Rookie head coach Mike LaFleur said Sunday that Brissett would begin working with the team’s starters on Tuesday with the plan of having him start to open the season. Chris Foerster: Coaching the 49ers in Kyle Shanahan’s absence is “really a group thing” | Pro Football Talk With 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan limited at training camp due to a severe concussion suffered in a recent car accident, assistant head coach/offensive line Chris Foerster is running the team. In his first media session with reporters on Sunday, Foerster made it clear he’s not doing it alone. “It’s really a group thing,” Foerster told reporters. “The title puts me in this position, and I was very grateful that [General Manager] John [Lynch] and Kyle felt that some of the things I could take the lead on, like this right here.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Cyrus Allen and Emmett Johnson responding to ‘hard coaching’ early in Chiefs camp The approach of Bieniemy and Reid reminds Allen of the environment in his last college season with the Cincinnati Bearcats. “They don’t play,” he said of the staff. “That’s all I can say. title: 4 things we think we’ve learned this weekend from Chiefs training camp
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs held practice sessions on Saturday and Sunday this weekend, featuring just the rookies, quarterbacks and select veterans before the entire team arrives in St. Joe at Missouri Western State University on Tuesday. While we await the practices opening to public attendance next week, we’re relying on observations from local media on […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Quarterback Justin Fields #6 watches quarterback Patrick Mahomes #15 participate during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs held practice sessions on Saturday and Sunday this weekend, featuring just the rookies, quarterbacks and select veterans before the entire team arrives in St. Joe at Missouri Western State University on Tuesday. While we await the practices opening to public attendance next week, we’re relying on observations from local media on the scene. After two days, let’s summarize what we’ve learned so far about the Chiefs from camp: 1. Patrick Mahomes is off and running On Friday, head coach Andy Reid revealed that starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes was fully cleared for practice to begin training camp. Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes on practice field this morning pic.twitter.com/CgrA8HhAlc — Jesse Newell (@jessenewell) July 25, 2026 On Saturday, in a video posted by Jesse Newell of The Athletic on X , Mahomes showed off his ability to get out from under center and into a handoff action while wearing the brace he is wearing for the time being. In his press conference, he said he was comfortable with it because he wore it in college ; there are no plans for how long he will wear it. Mahomes had a beautiful no look pass right between the hashes in redzone 7-on-7 work on a slant. He hit it spot on in timing, velocity and placement between the two zone defenders and it got dropped. #Chiefs #ChiefsCamp41 #ChiefsKingdom — Nick Jacobs (@Jacobs71) July 25, 2026 According to Nick Jacobs of KSHB 41 , Mahomes made a few touchdown-worthy throws towards the end zone on Saturday during a seven-on-seven period. This was his description of Mahomes’ day in his training camp notebook . Quarterback Patrick Mahomes continued to participate in all individual and 7-on-7 drills without any issues. He started off with a good back pylon throw to wide receiver Jimmy Holiday for a touchdown in 7-on-7. Mahomes later followed that up with a spot on no-look pass in timing, placement and velocity to wide receiver Andrew Armstrong. He placed it in the end zone on a slant route in between two zone coverages. The pass was unfortunately dropped. Based on the observations of ESPN’s Nate Taylor , Mahomes’ touchdown throw to Holiday featured rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane trailing in man coverage. Speaking to reporters after Saturday’s practice, Delane said Mahomes is “as advertised. He’s a great quarterback.” On Sunday, Mahomes continued to show off his movement out of under-center looks and throwing on the run in the beginning portion of practice. Another Day, more observations of one Patrick Mahomes. #Chiefs pic.twitter.com/Iaw95KTzaz — Harold R. Kuntz (@HaroldRKuntz3) July 26, 2026 The two-time MVP quarterback would go on to have a prolific day in team work. According to Harold Kuntz of FOX4 , who tweeted out the video above, Mahomes finished the first seven-on-seven period of Sunday with five completions over five throws , including a “deep route caught by Omari Evans,” an undrafted rookie receiver. 2. Mansoor Delane is embracing a slow start to camp After being selected with the No. 6 pick in the NFL Draft, cornerback Mansoor Delane has not been on the field as often as anyone would like during the Chiefs’ offseason practices. He injured his shoulder during OTAs and began wearing a yellow, non-contact uniform that he has worn to start practices this weekend. As mentioned earlier, Delane was beat by a reserve receiver for a touchdown during seven-on-seven periods, aided by a Mahomes throw. If that negative play, or any other, figures into any anxiety Delane has about beginning camp as a limited participant, he doesn’t seem like the type to let it drag his effort or mentality down. “I’m a guy if I lose reps, it motivates me to get better,” Delane told reporters on Saturday. “That just means I’ve got more room to grow. I almost get excited about those things, but at the same time you don’t want the same mistake to keep happening.” 3. Eric Bieniemy is back, and he won’t let you miss him From Jacobs’ observations of the team’s initial practice , offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy is making his presence felt — or heard — in his return to Kansas City. Jacobs noted how “vocal” Bieniemy was during seven-on-seven periods, coaching the skill-position players with consistent energy. EB .. ready for practice. Eric Bieniemy "getting them right" #Chiefs pic.twitter.com/7NF6DchO6g — Harold R. Kuntz (@HaroldRKuntz3) July 26, 2026 If you visit training camp this year, you’ll likely be able to hear Bieniemy “getting them right.” By all accounts, it’s a noticeable difference compared to the previous offensive coordinator. 4. Wide receiver Cyrus Allen is taking advantage of time with Mahomes, Reid Without the main core of receivers at camp until Wednesday’s practice, Mahomes has been throwing to lesser-known players this weekend. One player seems to be doing his best to get familiar with the two-time MVP. From Taylor’s observations of Sunday’s practice , Allen was on the receiving end of “one of the highlights” of practice. After scanning the field, Mahomes put up a ball for Allen to jump up and secure in traffic towards the back of the end zone. Cyrus Allen .. a look at the #Chiefs Wide Receiver. Had a couple nice catches in 7-on-7 today. pic.twitter.com/LZPh9Fd5is — Harold R. Kuntz (@HaroldRKuntz3) July 26, 2026 All offseason, Allen has been regarded as a strong route runner; it’s important to remember that not all of that comes from physical skills. He “spent a few minutes” listening to head coach Andy Reid in a one-on-one session between reps, according to Taylor. He apparently has been tasked with improving on “pre-snap awareness so that he can better anticipate the secondary’s coverage.” Our Jared Sapp wrote about Allen’s willingness to take coaching so far . The real competitors for the No. 4 receiver spot seem to be Nikko Remigio, Jalen Royals and Allen. Only one of them is getting three days as Mahomes’ top target while the other two wait, potentially get lost in the mix once the full-team practice begins.

title: Chiefs rookie Mansoor Delane admits it’s hard to turn down aggression
summary: Being selected sixth overall in the NFL Draft comes with expectations. For Kansas City Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, it doesn’t come with guarantees. As Delane works through his first training camp in Kansas City, the first-round pick is focused on finding the balance between the aggressive style that helped get him drafted and the […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Cornerback Mansoor Delane #5 walks toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Being selected sixth overall in the NFL Draft comes with expectations. For Kansas City Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, it doesn’t come with guarantees. As Delane works through his first training camp in Kansas City, the first-round pick is focused on finding the balance between the aggressive style that helped get him drafted and the discipline required at the NFL level. Head coach Andy Reid has already addressed that aggression, noting that there are times when the rookie may need to dial it back during practice. He implied it had something to do with the shoulder injury that has him donning a yellow, non-contact jersey to begin camp. When asked about Reid’s comments and whether there is a happy medium, Delane acknowledged that adjustment won’t necessarily come naturally. “That’s something that’s gonna be hard for me to turn down — my aggression,” Delane said. “Obviously you got to be smart.” Part of that is understanding that training camp is about preparing teammates for the season, not treating every rep like a Sunday afternoon. “It’s the NFL,” Delane added. “You got to protect your teammates. That’s the most important thing.” For Delane, learning when to unleash that physicality is simply another part of his transition to the league. And there is plenty he still wants to learn. Asked what defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo and defensive backs coach Dave Merritt have taught him so far, Delane summarized their message in two words. “Chasing perfection,” he said. Day 2 of “pre-camp” practices in St. Joe. pic.twitter.com/BQAsCjyxpT — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs_Matt) July 26, 2026 “You may not always get it, but I’m trying to get the closest thing to it. There’s little room for error, so [I’m] trying to be the best I could be.” That pursuit also shapes how Delane responds when things don’t go his way. His first training camp practice wasn’t perfect. Delane didn’t expect it to be. “First day is always ups and downs,” he said. Rather than becoming frustrated by a lost rep, Delane sees it as information he can use. “I’m a guy, you know, [when] I lose reps, I don’t do good or whatever, it motivates me to get better,” Delane explained. “That just means I got more room to grow.” There is even part of him that welcomes those moments. “I almost get excited about those things,” he said, “but at the same time, don’t let the same mistakes keep happening.” That mentality fits with something Spagnuolo noticed about Delane long before the Chiefs drafted him. After playing at Virginia Tech, Delane chose to transfer to LSU rather than enter the NFL Draft, giving himself an opportunity to compete in the SEC before making the jump to the league. Spagnuolo recently pointed to that decision as something that impressed him during Kansas City’s evaluation. Asked why he chose that path, Delane’s explanation was simple. “I run to competition,” he said. #Chiefs 1st round pick Mansoor Delane says he's "chasing perfection" despite being a rookie. He'll wear a yellow no-contact jersey for the time being as he recovers from a shoulder injury during OTAs. #ChiefsKingdom @KSHB41 pic.twitter.com/CPS4s434yi — Matt Foster (@MattFosterTV) July 26, 2026 Delane believed there was still something left for him to prove before turning professional. “I felt like I had more on the table, more on the plate,” he said. “So I just wanted to finish that off.” That desire for competition hasn’t changed now that he’s in Kansas City. “I’m excited to go against the best every day in practice,” Delane said. “That makes me better.” Delane’s attention is on the preparation required to eventually make Sundays feel easy. He’s not trying to win training camp; he’s trying to master it. Every rep, every mistake, every correction is part of the same goal: stack enough consistency that when the lights come on, nothing feels new. In a room full of veterans and expectations, the rookie corner is betting on the same thing that got him here: that competing every day is the fastest way to become ready for any Sunday.
author: Maurice Elston

title: Cyrus Allen and Emmett Johnson responding to ‘hard coaching’ early in Chiefs camp
summary: As the Kansas City Chiefs attempt to rebound from a disappointing 2025 season, the team has made coaching a focus. This is particularly true on offense. Tough-nosed Eric Bieniemy returns as offensive coordinator after three seasons away from Kansas City. Rookies have already reported to the team’s training camp at Missouri Western State University in […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Cyrus Allen #13 walks toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Kansas City Chiefs attempt to rebound from a disappointing 2025 season, the team has made coaching a focus. This is particularly true on offense. Tough-nosed Eric Bieniemy returns as offensive coordinator after three seasons away from Kansas City. Rookies have already reported to the team’s training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph. Even the early portion is living up to the brutal reputations of training camps under Bieniemy and head coach Andy Reid. “It definitely was right that it’s one of the hardest training camps, for sure,” said rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen after practice. “I’m just getting my feet wet and understanding the playbook and everything. Just keep going.” The approach of Bieniemy and Reid reminds Allen of the environment in his last college season with the Cincinnati Bearcats. “They don’t play,” he said of the staff. “That’s all I can say. Everything is intentional. Everything is process oriented. We did that a lot at Cincy, so I’m coming back into it. Coach EB is definitely pounding us every day about [having] our shirts tucked in. Everything is structure.” Running back Emmett Johnson is all for Bieniemy’s fiery nature. “He’s going to push you,” remarked the rookie. “He’s going to push you a lot. He wants the best from you at the end of the day. I don’t take anything personally. I pride myself in hard coaching, so I really love that he’s here pushing me to be better every single day.” Allen also reportedly had some one-on-one coaching from Reid during Sunday’s practice. “[He was] just making sure I’m looking at the coverages,” the wideout recalled. “Pre-snap awareness and stuff like that. Just being where my feet are and making decisions quicker.” As both players enter the league, they are showing a humble nature as they work to earn rookie roles on this year’s Chiefs squad. “It’s surreal for me,” Allen acknowledged. “A lot of people are proud of me back home. I appreciate them for that. I worked extremely hard to be here. Nothing was given. I earned everything. I’m pretty happy with myself, but I still have that underdog mentality that I live by every day. Every day, I come to work, and I’m willing to learn.” Johnson’s professionalism showed as he was unofficially credited as Sunday’s first player down the hill for practice. RB Emmett Johnson is first Chiefs player down the hill today (cc: @mattderrick ) pic.twitter.com/VbnYeEcfj9 — Jesse Newell (@jessenewell) July 26, 2026 Expect to see more early appearances from Johnson as he continues a routine dating to high school of getting 200 receiving reps each day from the JUGS machine. Johnson knows that extra time will be required to be successful as a pro. He has meticulously planned his transition and sought advice from players such as Jacksonville Jaguars running back Ameer Abdullah. “At this level, especially,” he explained, “I feel like you have to do the extra things like recovery. You’ve got to get in the building early. You’ve got to stay late, I feel, to be successful at this level. So, I’m kind of learning through my routine right now. [I’m] asking older guys like Ameer Abdullah who played at Nebraska. Just picking his game on recovery because he’s been playing a long time. That’s what I’m doing.”

title: Chiefs rookie pass rushers talk first impressions of training camp
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs rookies and quarterbacks reported for training camp ahead of the rest of the veterans, who will arrive in St Joseph, Missouri, this Tuesday, July 28th. Saturday gave the Chiefs 2026 rookie draft class its first taste of what an NFL training camp is all about. And not just any NFL training […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Defensive players participate during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs rookies and quarterbacks reported for training camp ahead of the rest of the veterans, who will arrive in St Joseph, Missouri, this Tuesday, July 28th. Saturday gave the Chiefs 2026 rookie draft class its first taste of what an NFL training camp is all about. And not just any NFL training camp, but one led by one of the league’s last old war horses, head coach Andy “Long-drive Drill” Reid. And you could see it on the face of second-round draft pick R Mason Thomas when he stood at the podium in front of reporters after practice. He looked a bit tuckered and said that he was reminded by the words Reid said to him this offseason, “We don’t have to condition because the practice is that hard.” As for his cohort and fellow top-100 draft pick, first-round defensive tackle Peter Woods said that he came away liking what he’s seen out of his teammates thus far, and that he could tell they spent the offseason getting their minds and bodies ready to go. “A lot of guys impressed me from the aspect,” Woods told reporters. “Just knowing what they were supposed to do when they weren’t here.” Which is good, because both Woods and Thomas know that once the veterans show up, things are going to escalate quickly. “The veterans have a standard for what they want to see from us young guys,” said Woods, explaining that there is an expectation he needs to live up to in the eyes of his teammates being the new guy. Both guys also highlighted the importance of working on their technique to make sure they have the little things locked down. “You know sometimes in college you can get away with some stuff,” said Woods quite frankly. “But these guys are very detail-oriented…I’m going against some of the best guys in the whole world at their position, and they don’t make a lot of mistakes.” Similarly, Thomas highlighted that, because he’s undersized for his position (standing 6 feet 2 inches tall and weighing in at 241 pounds), he needs to play with more power; he believes being fundamentally sound is the path to reaching his goal. “I think technique outweighs the weight room,” said Thomas. “Technique kind of saves you when you might not be the ideal weight.” That, and studying the scheme, of course. “Knowing the playbook,” Thomas assured. “That helps you play fast.” Both Woods and Thomas talked about refining their footwork to make sure they play with a strong base and don’t sacrifice power by overstriding or getting off balance. Due to Thomas’ size, technique will always be more important for him than other players on the line of scrimmage, which is why he said he has tried to model his game after Denver Broncos star pass rusher Nick Bonito, another former Oklahoma Sooner, who is nearly the exact same size as Thomas is. “That’s going to be my answer for a long time,” joked Thomas. “Guys who fit my stature.” Thomas went on to say that playing for the Chiefs is a dream come true for him. “I never would have thought Kansas City, Missouri, area code would have called me on draft day,” laughed Thomas, saying that other than one official meeting at the combine, the Chiefs had no other pre-draft contact with him. “I guess they’re low-key and like to be quiet.” As for Woods, he’s just excited to get the pads on and hit somebody. “That’s why I play the game… I’m super eager; it’s been almost a year since I’ve been able to put some pads on and hit somebody.” You’re not the only one, Mr. Woods. I think I speak for everyone in Chiefs Kingdom when I say that we are all pretty jazzed to see you playing full speed, looking to lay somebody out in full pads.
author: Rocky Magaña

title: 50 Days until Chiefs football, we are ‘Justin Houston’ days away
summary: We are 50 days away from the Kansas City Chiefs‘ season-opening game against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football” in Week 1. The No. 50 jersey will be worn by undrafted rookie center Pete Nygra going into training camp after linebacker Brandn George was waived in May; he wore the number during the preseason […]
full_text: Football: Kansas City Chiefs Justin Houston (50) at line of scrimmage during game vs San Francisco 49ers at Arrowhead Stadium. Kansas City, MO 9/23/2018 CREDIT: David E. Klutho (Photo by David E. Klutho /Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X162158 TK1 ) We are 50 days away from the Kansas City Chiefs ‘ season-opening game against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football” in Week 1. The No. 50 jersey will be worn by undrafted rookie center Pete Nygra going into training camp after linebacker Brandn George was waived in May; he wore the number during the preseason last year. There is one all-time Chiefs pass rusher that comes to mind when visualizing No. 50 in the red and gold: The memorable No. 50s in franchise history Justin Houston (2011 – 2018) Anthony Davis (1994 – 1998) Willie Gay Jr. (2020 – 2023) Kawika Mitchell (2003 – 2006) Mike Vrabel (2009 – 2010) At the dawn of head coach Andy Reid’s tenure, the defense was the catalyst in team success, and the top pass rusher was outside linebacker Justin Houston in his prime. In 2014, he nearly eclipsed the NFL’s all-time single-season sack record when he racked up 22.5. He was one of the most unique combinations of power and athleticism in football before a knee injury took him off an all-time career path. Willie Gay Jr. is still a member of the Miami Dolphins after never realizing his potential in Kansas City, once a second-round pick with playmaking upside. He will always be remembered fondly in Chiefs Kingdom for his personality and charisma. New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel wore No. 50 during his two years with the Chiefs, catching two touchdowns wearing that jersey. 50: The number of solo tackles by former Chiefs safety Bryan Cook last season 50 solo tackles ranked fourth among Chiefs defenders last season, with Chamarri Conner (75), Nick Bolton (73) and Drue Tranquill (55) finishing above the safety who moved onto sign with the Cincinnati Bengals in free agency this offseason, Bryan Cook. That role is projected to be filled by veteran safety Alohi Gilman, but can he be as reliable of a tackler as Cook was? Cook missed just 5.6% of his tackle attempts last year, according to Pro Football Focus . Gilman missed 16.4% of his tackle attempts last season, with his focus primarily on being back-end support in coverage. Conner and third-year safety Jaden Hicks may be counted on to make up for the sure tackling that will be missing with Cook’s absence this year.

title: Warren McClendon has Pro Bowl pedigree
summary: Last season Warren McClendon took the Los Angeles Rams’ right tackle job away from entrenched veteran Rob Havenstein in Week 12 and never looked back. According to Pro Football Focus (PFF), Warren ranked 15th among all tackles with at least 647 blocking snaps. Considering every team needs two starting tackles, that squarely puts him in […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 2: Warren McClendon Jr. #71 of the Los Angeles Rams stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at SoFi Stadium on October 02, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last season Warren McClendon took the Los Angeles Rams’ right tackle job away from entrenched veteran Rob Havenstein in Week 12 and never looked back. According to Pro Football Focus (PFF), Warren ranked 15th among all tackles with at least 647 blocking snaps. Considering every team needs two starting tackles, that squarely puts him in the top 10 of his position. McClendon finished with PFF grades in the following facets followed by tackle peer rankings: Offensive grade: 78.7 (15th) Run blocking grade: 81.9 (13th) Pass blocking grade: 69.1 (35th) With the Rams reporting to training camp over the weekend, McClendon enters the season as the starter for the first time in his career. It’s realistic to think there is room for improvement, and McClendon may even ascend to Pro Bowl considerations in 2026. Still, there is a clear gap between the best tackles in football and McClendon—even if the young tackle has already established himself among the upper echelon. The Rams will need to make the difficult decision to either extend McClendon’s contract and retain his services for 2027 or beyond or take on the improbable task of replacing a player top 10 at his position. 2026 isn’t necessarily a “make or break” year for McClendon. It still is a “prove it” season where he must sustain his level of production if not take a noticeable step forward. The Rams have plenty of other difficult contract decisions on the horizon, including but not limited to the following: Puka Nacua Kobie Turner Byron Young Kevin Dotson Steve Avila Alaric Jackson Colby Parkinson And if McClendon finds that the Rams intend to allocate their salary cap resources elsewhere, he could realistically enter free agency at age 26 and be the top-billed tackle to hit the market. Young, capable tackles rarely every change hands. There will be plenty of suitors if Los Angeles is not McClendon’s long-term home. McClendon took the Rams by surprised and usurped long-term start Rob Havenstein. He enters his first season as a full-time starter with room to grow from a production standpoint. That only complicates a tough contract dilemma and escalates his price tag. McClendon has Pro Bowl pedigree. Will he outplay his chances to remain in Los Angeles?
