title: As a passer only, Jalen Hurts’ rankings make some sense
summary: Jalen Hurts is one of the most perplexingly great players in the NFL and, perhaps, Eagles history. He has won a Super Bowl, played in two of them, and was the best player on the field in both. He is 56-22 in the regular season as a starter. He has been to three Pro Bowls […]
full_text: Jan 11, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) runs under pressure from San Francisco 49ers defensive end Bryce Huff (47) during the fourth quarter in an NFC Wild Card Round game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Jalen Hurts is one of the most perplexingly great players in the NFL and, perhaps, Eagles history. He has won a Super Bowl, played in two of them, and was the best player on the field in both. He is 56-22 in the regular season as a starter. He has been to three Pro Bowls and was MVP runner-up in 2022. And yet, the football world, including all of us in Philadelphia, don’t quite seem to able to put our finger on just how good he is. This off-season, two sets of rankings have generated a lot of conversation. The first was ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler’s survey of NFL executives , coaches and front office personnel who collectively rated Hurts as the 17th-best quarterback in the NFL. This week, as the NFL Network runs through its list of the top-100 players in the NFL, Hurts became the first Eagle to appear on the list, at No. 56 overall . Last year, following a Super Bowl victory in which he was named the game’s MPV, he was No. 19. The year before, he was No. 15 and, following his incredible performance in a losing effort in Super Bowl 57, he was the third-best player in the entire league. That’s not a great trend, but he may also be one of the hardest player to get a handle on in the NFL. Jalen Hurts has never been the QB with the golden arm. His incredible success during his five years as the Philadelphia Eagles starter has always rested on his abilities as a dual-threat, plus-one in the running game, a skill that has always masked his limitations as a passer. And that’s all fine. It’s good that, if you’re not a prototypical NFL passer that you compensate for it in some other way. Hurts has always compensated by being a great runner. Last season, he stopped doing that. In 16 starts he ran for only 421 yards, a drop of 209 yards from 2024, and a decrease of 363 yards from his all-time high of 784 yards rushing in ‘21. His success rate as a runner fell to 50.5% a year ago, down from 55.3% in ‘24 and 61.1% in 2023. He averaged just 26.3 yards per game on the ground, far below his 42.0 average in 2024. In his first two full seasons, he averaged more than 50 yards a game rushing. As a pure passer, Hurts has generally been a middling QB. Below are Hurts’ numbers over the last four seasons in terms of QB rating, passing yards, passing touchdowns, interception percentage and passing success rate. 2022: Rate (101.5, 4th), Yards (3701, 10th), TDs (22, 14th), INT% (1.3, T-4), Succ% (46.4%, 13th) 2023: Rate (89.1, 20th), Yards (3858, 14th), TDs (23, T-13), INT% (2.8, 27th), Succ% (46.7%, T-13) 2024: Rate (103.7, 5th), Yards (2903, 20th), TDs (18, T-20), INT% (1.4, T-5), Succ% (46.6%, 16th) 2025: Rate (98.5, 12th), Yards (3224, 16th), TDs (25, T-9th), INT% (1.3, T-2), Succ% (41.8%, 29th) It’s fair to note Hurts has only once had the same offensive coordinator for two seasons in a row and, in that second season with Shane Steichen calling the shots, he had his best overall year. But Brian Johnson and Kevin Patullo were ill-suited for the job and had to be replaced. Now, Hurts once again begins a season with a new offensive coordinator, and yet another first-time play caller, in Sean Mannion. Mannion’s offense is expected to place Hurts under center more frequently and will largely move away from the all-shotgun, all-the-time, RPO offensive “scheme” that Hurts has played in during his first five seasons. It’s likely Mannion’s new offense will ask Hurts to run less, something Hurts appeared to be trending towards a season ago, anyway. If the running game is going to be less a feature of Hurts’ overall portfolio, his historical numbers as a passer accurately reflect some of the rankings we’ve seen this off-season. He has simply not shown that he can lead a pass-first offense yet. But “yet” is the key word. When Hurts has had a coordinator who could scheme up open receivers and give him places to throw the football, he’s thrived. This may be exactly the change he needs at this stage of his career. We simply have no idea what the 2026 Eagles offense is going to look like, or how Hurts will perform in it. It is one of the greatest unanswered questions in the NFL heading into the season. Based off last year’s performance, it’s fair to be skeptical of him being one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL right now (although ranking him 17th is wildly dumb). If he’s not going to run, he must improve notably as a passer. And Mannion has to help him get there.

(Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Saquon Barkley on missing A.J. Brown, another new OC and that hurdle | Exclusive – USA Today Looking back on the play two years later, Barkley said he never thought it would continue to carry this much cultural relevance. “When I got to the locker room and got to see the play, I realized I was able to do something pretty cool. It’s something, it’s a play I’ll never forget. But I also don’t want to be remembered for that play. I’m happy I was able to make that play. But I’m ready for the next one.” Maybe NFL execs should look more at winning in evaluating Jalen Hurts – BGN It’s a week now since ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler put out his exhaustive annual work on how NFL executives, coaches and scouts view quarterbacks. It’s a provocative, thankless, comprehensive look at what decisionmakers feel. Somehow, someway, Jalen Hurts fell from No. 9 in 2025 to No. 17 in 2026. There is no question that Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow, Matt Stafford and Lamar Jackson are among the best in the NFL. But are Dak Prescott, Justin Herbert, Drake Maye, Jared Goff and Caleb Williams really better than Hurts? Prescott, in terms of what he did last year (30 TDs vs. 10 INTs, 4,552 yards passing) has an argument. The others may not. Let’s simplify things. Let’s go with who of the previous 16 named above Hurts won more. Eagles notes: Quinyon Mitchell’s and Cooper DeJean’s next contracts – PhillyVoice The current highest-paid corner in the NFL is Trent McDuffie, who signed four-year, $124 million deal in Los Angeles after the Rams traded a first-round pick to the Chiefs for him this offseason. That’s $31 million per year. Gonzalez is obviously angling for more, and the Patriots have decided to try to put pressure on him by negotiating through the media and general public. (Bush league tactic, in my opinion, but whatever.) Gonzalez isn’t the only top cornerback in negotiations for a new deal. The Seahawks’ Devin Witherspoon could cash in this offseason as well. Quinyon Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, and Texans Pro Bowl CB Kamari Lassiter will all be eligible for contract extensions next offseason. Assuming he stays healthy and has another good season, Mitchell will likely be looking to top any deals given to Gonzalez and/or Witherspoon. The better the deals Gonzalez and Witherspoon get, the more leverage Mitchell will have to ask for a commensurate deal. DeJean’s earning power isn’t a true apple-to-apples comparison, as he’ll play a mix of slot corner and safety in 2026, but certainly he’ll be rooting for Gonzalez and Witherspoon to break the bank as well. A lot of corners will soon land monster second contracts. Let’s Talk About Donovan – Iggles Blitz Jalen Hurts has a good chance to go down as the best QB in Eagles history. His career numbers are about halfway to Donovan McNabb’s numbers, but Hurts is only 27 (about to be 28 in August). He can either catch McNabb or come close if he stays in Philly long enough. Hurts does have the advantage of two Super Bowl appearances and one ring. Plus he played at a high level in those games. As of now McNabb is the best QB in team history. Ron Jaworski had a good run and got the team to its first SB. Randall Cunningham is the most dynamic QB in team history. He finished second in MVP voting in 1988 and 1990. He gave us a lifetime of memories, but struggled in the postseason. Norm Van Brocklin was only in Philly for three seasons, but his teammates swear he is the main reason they won the NFL Championship in 1960. They speak about him with reverence. McNabb had individual and team success. He also did it over the course of a decade. Roob’s Observations: Can Jihaad Campbell make the Eagles forget Nakobe Dean? – NBCSP THE MOST INTRIGUING STORY OF CAMP: There are a ton of intriguing stories as we head into training camp, a bunch of guys whose every move we’ll all be watching. Can Marcus Epps and Drew Makuba hold down safety or will Howie have to go out and find someone? Will Makai Lemon perform well enough to slide into that WR2 role? Can Jonathan Greenard live up to that massive contract and become the double-digit sack guy the Eagles need? Can Riq Woolen return to his Pro Bowl form and give the Eagles the NFL’s best cornerback group? Will Landon Dickerson and Cam Jurgens hold up physically after their stem cell treatments in Columbia? But for me, the most compelling storyline is how will Jihaad Campbell manage as a full-time linebacker replacement for Nakobe Dean. Let’s not forget just how good Nakobe was over the last two years. In just 25 games, he piled up 183 tackles, 7.0 sacks, 16 tackles for loss, an interception, two fumble recoveries, 12 quarterback hits and three forced fumbles. The only other players to put up those numbers were Frankie Luvu, one-time Eagle Eric Wilson and current Eagle Zack Baun. Dean was such a playmaker the last couple years and will definitely be missed. But the Eagles did invest a 1st-round pick in Campbell last year, and he did some good things in the 10 games he started, notably that athletic fumble recovery against the Bills, an interception off Baker Mayfield in Tampa and a red-zone forced fumble off Miles Sanders in the opening-day win over the Cowboys. He also had 80 tackles, which is a lot for someone who only played 710 snaps. Vic Fangio was forced by circumstance to play Campbell out of position as an edge rusher for about 150 snaps last year, but Campbell isn’t an edge, he’s an off-ball linebacker, and while he wasn’t all over the field like Dean I thought it was a promising rookie year for a 21-year-old rookie. Out of 64 linebackers who played at least 500 snaps, Campbell’s overall Pro Football Focus grade of 76.2 was 12th-highest, which is awfully good, and his 78.6 coverage grade was 4th-highest. Without the distraction of having to change positions this year, Campbell can just focus on becoming a better linebacker, and I expect he will. He’s a fast, big, tough, athletic player, and I’m looking for a big step forward in Year 2. Philly, you deserve this – Liberty Ballers In 2013, the Sixers brought on Sam Hinkie as general manager. The Daryl Morey protege took a sledgehammer to the roster, hoping to pull the franchise out of NBA purgatory and into perpetual relevancy. You could liken the next decade-plus to getting on a rollercoaster that never stops and is on fire. Sure, there have been thrilling moments, but sometimes, you just really wanted to get off the ride. Now, 13 years later, LeBron James is a Philadelphia 76er. You did it, Sixers fans. You trusted the process. It wasn’t easy. In fact, it was downright tortuous at times, but you’re here. Like Andy Dufresne, you crawled through a river of shit and came out clean on the other side. NBA Power Rankings for all 30 teams updated after LeBron James signs with 76ers – SB Nation LeBron James wasn’t lying when he said he didn’t care about money when assessing his options in NBA free agency. Any team in the league could have landed James for essentially the veteran’s minimum if they could make the case that they gave him the best chance to win a fifth championship. In the end, the Philadelphia 76ers won the LeBron sweepstakes. James is joining a lineup that already includes Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe, and Joel Embiid. The bench is pretty strong too with Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons, Labaron Philon, Dominick Barlow, Adem Bona, Justin Edwards, and Ariel Hukporti. I predicted the Sixers were the favorites to sign James last weekend, but it’s still hard to believe it actually happened. Cowboys were allegedly very interested in Brendan Sorsby – Blogging The Boys It makes sense for the Cowboys…

title: Seattle Seahawks 2026 training camp preview: Which UDFAs have the best shot to make the team?
summary: The Seattle Seahawks begin training camp on Saturday with the first of 10 publicly held practices. One of the most consistent aspects of John Schneider’s tenure as general manager is his ability to find rookie undrafted free agent gems. Jake Bobo, George Holani, and Patrick O’Connell are among the UDFAs Seattle signed right away, while […]
full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JUNE 11: Lance Mason #42 of the Seattle Seahawks runs into a block during practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on June 11, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks begin training camp on Saturday with the first of 10 publicly held practices. One of the most consistent aspects of John Schneider’s tenure as general manager is his ability to find rookie undrafted free agent gems. Jake Bobo, George Holani, and Patrick O’Connell are among the UDFAs Seattle signed right away, while Drake Thomas and Jalen Sundell eventually made their way to the Seahawks roster as rookies after their original teams let them go. With Seattle maintaining the bulk of its roster and drafting more players than expected, the UDFA class for 2026 was much smaller than usual. Only four of the seven initial UDFA signings are still on the team , while they added a couple more later on in the offseason. Here’s a quick rundown of the UDFA rookies as of July 26, so as to account for any signings made after this article goes live. Aidan Hubbard, EDGE The former Northwestern star not getting drafted was a bit of a surprise, especially with 13.5 sacks over his final two seasons on an otherwise mediocre (at best) power conference school. Hubbard won’t amaze with blinding speed but he has a quick first step and has shown effectiveness defending the run. Hubbard’s guaranteed money is $267,500, which is the highest of any Seahawks UDFA by far, and maybe speaks to their interest in having him compete for what is effectively the fifth EDGE spot behind Derick Hall, Uchenna Nwosu, DeMarcus Lawrence, and Dante Fowler Jr. Hubbard’s competition figures to be Jared Ivey (or maybe not, given Ivey’s huge frame for the position could lead to a switch or versatility along the line), Connor O’Toole, fellow UDFA rookie Marvin Jones Jr, and Jamie Sheriff. I think Hubbard has a very real chance to crack the 53-man roster. Uso Seumalo, Nose Tackle The big fella from Kansas State is 330 pounds and may be a fun preseason watch. Nose tackle is not a glamorous position and therefore not one where the box score is valuable. You won’t see high sack totals, tackle numbers, or anything of that sort in the traditional stats. For nose tackles, it’s about taking on/creating double teams, clogging running lanes, disrupting the pocket so that there’s interior pressure, etc. The only true nose tackle on last year’s roster was Brandon Pili. Jarran Reed and Byron Murphy have had snaps at 0-technique but neither of them is a traditional nose. The problem for Seumalo is less of Pili and more of a numbers game. When Pili was on the roster, he averaged about 11 snaps per game in 13 regular season appearances. He was inactive for the Super Bowl and in two of the final three regular season games. As much as Mike Macdonald values big bodies, there’s no guarantee either Seumalo or Pili is on the active roster for 2026. However, they kept a few guys on the practice squad (Pili included before he was promoted), so it’s a matter of whether or not the Seahawks want to dedicate a spot to a true nose again. I think they will, so Seumalo has a shot. Watch out for Bubba Thomas and J.R. Singleton as other possibilities after their PS stints last year. Marvin Jones Jr, EDGE Jones is very much traits over production. He went from Georgia to Florida State to Oklahoma and had eight total sacks. Jones has an 81-inch wingspan and has an interesting athletic profile. Much like Hubbard, his positioning on the squad is whether or not he can snag that fifth EDGE spot. I’m less bullish on his prospects compared to Hubbard. Lance Mason, Tight End Mason comes to the Seahawks from Wisconsin, where he caught 30 receptions for 398 yards and four touchdowns on an otherwise horrific offense that managed the rarity of shutout home losses in consecutive weeks. He’s probably got more upside as a receiving tight end than Nick Kallerup, but that’s about the only feasible chance he has to make the roster, particularly with Nick Vannett now added to the fold. Seattle has a mix of veterans and young talent at the top of the depth chart that put Mason in a spot where the practice squad is the realistic goal. Rashad Rochelle, Wide Receiver Not to be mean or sound crude, but Rochelle is almost certainly not making this roster as a wide receiver. There are too many people to contend against and Seattle’s top five is set in stone, so Rochelle’s pathway is exclusively through his deep kick and punt return experience from his days at Indiana State. Hubbard and Seumalo have the best opportunities to be the UDFA stars, whereas I believe everyone else is a long shot to no shot. Myself and fellow Field Gulls staff writer and The Hawks Eye host, Bryce Coutts, talk a bit more about the UDFAs in the timestamped video below! If for some reason the timestamp doesn’t work, go to 32:25 and we talk through 44:34.

title: Seahawks Reacts Results: Seahawks fans predict top-ranked scoring defense again
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. Training camp for the 2026 Seattle Seahawks is now underway. Because of this, it is prediction […]
full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JULY 25: Ernest Jones IV #13 of the Seattle Seahawks takes the field before practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on July 25, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys. Training camp for the 2026 Seattle Seahawks is now underway. Because of this, it is prediction time around NFL circles. Around the league, it is believed that the Seahawks will be one of the favorites to win the Super Bowl. A large part of that reasoning seems to be because of Mike Macdonald and his defense. Last season, Seattle allowed only 292 points throughout the entire season . That is an average of 17.2 points per game, good enough for first in the league. Do Seahawks fans think they can repeat this impressive stat? It appears that Seattle fans are feeling very confident entering the 2026 season. Of Seahawks fans polled, 49% believe that Seattle will repeat as the NFL defensive leaders in points allowed in 2026. Of the other 51% of fans, 48% think the Seahawks will finish in the top five, with only 3% believing they will finish out of the top five. This confidence is not surprising. The Seahawks nearly brought back every player on defense from 2025. The notable departures were Boye Mafe, Riq Woolen, and Coby Bryant. However, John Schneider didn’t leave those spots unfilled. Dante Fowler Jr. was signed to the roster to help make up for the loss of Mafe. Meanwhile, at cornerback, Schneider brought in former first round pick, Noah Igbinoghene, as well as a trio of drafted cornerbacks, led by third round pick, Julian Neal. Bud Clark was also taken in the second round to help replace Bryant. On top of the continuity on the defense, there is added optimism that the defense can get even better with young players like Nick Emmanwori and Byron Murphy II having another year with Mike Macdonald. Of course, repeating as the NFL leaders in points allowed in a season is a very tough feat to do. It is wild to think that the Legion of Boom era Seahawks were able to accomplish this for four consecutive seasons (2012-2015). 2026 will be another opportunity for this Dark Side defense to add to their trophy case and show that they are also an all-time NFL defense, just like the Legion of Boom. title: 49ers news: It sounds like Nick Martin will get the first shot at SAM linebacker
summary: This morning you’ll read about some training camp updates from some of the San Francisco 49ers beat. And good old Mike Florio’s thoughts on Kyle Shanahan’s accident. User KeepThemGuessing shared his thoughts in The Feed about John Lynch’s press conference from this past weekend. 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates More observations […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 24: Nick Martin #45 of the San Francisco 49ers gets set during the first half of an NFL football game against the Carolina Panthers at Levi's Stadium on November 24, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images This morning you’ll read about some training camp updates from some of the San Francisco 49ers beat. And good old Mike Florio’s thoughts on Kyle Shanahan’s accident. User KeepThemGuessing shared his thoughts in The Feed about John Lynch’s press conference from this past weekend. 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates More observations from the day: Defensive back Nate Hobbs was the only player on the active roster not participating at the beginning of practice. Hobbs dealt with knee issues last season. Offensive tackle Vederian Lowe and wide receiver Christian Kirk were hobbled a bit during the session. It was a strong day for QB Brock Purdy , who went 10-of-12 in team drills with the highlight coming on a deep ball down the left sideline to WR Mike Evans for a big gain against CB Deommodore Lenoir . Conversely, we saw a couple of interceptions for backup QB Mac Jones , including one thrown right to S Marques Sigle . LB Nick Martin appears to be getting the first crack at the Sam linebacker spot, though the Niners have multiple options to work through there. The same is true of Connor Colby at left guard. He took all the reps with the starters Sunday, though Chris Foerster said Robert Jones will also compete there. 49ers first impressions: Shanahan arrives, Purdy and Evans connect, and Bosa returns “Nick Bosa looks better than he did before he got hurt last year,” 49ers left tackle Trent Williams said. “I see him every day. I can’t tell he had an injury and came back from anything. Most people with an injury that catastrophic, you can see it with something, like with atrophy in the leg.” Bosa looks like a player who can singlehandedly rectify one of the 49ers’ most glaring weaknesses from last season: the pass rush. The team finished last in the NFL with just 20 sacks. Their struggles came after the 49ers actually sealed two early-season wins, including one over the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, with their pass rush. 49ers wanted to keep Shanahan accident quiet, and some in the media complied Others who cover the 49ers knew about it, too. Before the news was released, Tim Kawakami of the San Francisco Standard dropped a hint: “I think there’s going to be some news later this morning.” Kawakami later admitted that he was aware of the situation, but that he didn’t report it because he “ knew about 15% of the details .” Still, he apparently knew 100 percent of the fact that there was an accident. Not every detail related to the story needed to be reported, especially when plenty of the basic information about the collision was available from public sources. News regarding events that entail the involvement of the police and/or other first responders rarely gets held. It’s public information. (For example, news regarding Tony Romo’s recent arrest was shared as soon as Fox News 6 in Wisconsin obtained the public arrest detention report.) In this situation, the conduits for publicly-available information to the general public either were asleep at the switch or made a deliberate choice not to perform one of the core functions of journalism. Day 1 of 49ers training camp shows glimpse of change on LB depth chart Big changes appear to be coming for the San Francisco 49ers linebacking corps. At least that’s what Day 1 of training camp taught us. The Sacramento Bee’s Chris Biderman reported second-year linebacker Nick Martin was running with the first-team defense as the Sam linebacker alongside veterans Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw. This could be an indicator of some of the changes coming from defensive coordinator Raheem Morris. Warner will take his usual Mike LB spot, while Greenlaw slots back in as the Will LB where he spent his first six NFL seasons in San Francisco. The third LB wasn’t used as frequently in past iterations of the 49ers’ defense and the prototypical player at that spot was bigger than Martin’s 6-foot, 220-pound frame. 49ers training camp report: Kyle Shanahan on hand for Day 1 after car accident Offensive play of the day Quarterback Brock Purdy and veteran wide receiver Mike Evans figure to get quite familiar with each other through training camp and heading into the regular season. Those two gave an early preview of what might be expected this year, as they hooked up on a couple of pass completions. The top play was a deep pass down the left sideline in which Evans was matched against cornerback Deommodore Lenoir. Safety Marques Sigle was a split-second late, as Evans made the reception. Defensive play of the day Linebackers Garret Wallow and Jalen Graham teamed up for the most-notable defensive play of the day for an interception of backup quarterback Mac Jones. Jones looked to fit a throw into Jordan Watkins over the middle, but Wallow made a leaping deflection of the pass. The ball was deflected again before hitting the ground, and Graham finally gathered it in and returned it back the other way. Competition to watch Connor Colby appears to be in the lead in the competition for the starting job at left guard. Now, all he has to do is give the 49ers no reason to try anyone else in that spot. Colby and veteran pickup Robert Jones separated themselves during the offseason program, Foerster said. Colby, who started six games for the 49ers last season, is playing with a lot more confidence and decisiveness, Williams said.

Anderson, 6’3″, 326 pounds, didn’t have the same range as Collins and West […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers officially announced that they waived defensive tackle Evan Anderson. Anderson showed promise as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024, but the additions of Alfred Collins and CJ West made it difficult to find playing time for Anderson. Anderson, 6’3″, 326 pounds, didn’t have the same range as Collins and West do in the running game. Add that to the lack of pass rush, and the writing was on the wall for Anderson. The 49ers will see if one of their undrafted free agent rookies from this class can make the roster. Bryson Eason comes from the University of Tennessee. He’s 6’3″, 315 pounds. You can’t miss the second UDFA. James Thompson Jr. is 6’6″, 308 pounds, out of Illinois. The team announced they brought back Kevin Givens. He signed a one-year deal. Givens first joined the Niners as an undrafted free agent in 2019. He’s spent the previous seven seasons with the 49ers. Givens is more than likely a training camp body.

title: Chris Foerster’s experience and tenure with the 49ers makes him the least-disruptive option as interim head coach
summary: With Kyle Shanahan recovering from a car accident, San Francisco 49ers offensive line coach Chris Foerster will be interim head coach for the next few days, or even weeks, depending on Shanahan’s recovery. According to 49ers general manager John Lynch, at this stage of the season, it just might be a title in name only. […]
full_text: Jan 5, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; San Francisco 49ers offensive line coach Chris Foerster against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images With Kyle Shanahan recovering from a car accident , San Francisco 49ers offensive line coach Chris Foerster will be interim head coach for the next few days, or even weeks, depending on Shanahan’s recovery. According to 49ers general manager John Lynch, at this stage of the season, it just might be a title in name only. “The way Kyle’s thinking about it,” Lynch said. “And has communicated to me that he wants to see things done as that it’s a collective effort.” It’s not like Shanahan is completely off the field as he recovers. Lynch said the head coach would be seen on the field, but it’s a matter of “what he can tolerate.” The plan for training camp is already written, and installs are put together per Lynch. Now it’s just someone to handle a few things Shanahan would have. Lynch noted talking to the team and media as two things Shanahan isn’t ready to do. That’s where Foerster comes in. At first, seeing the offensive line coach become the front-man might appear a bit odd. Foerster has over thirty years of experience in coaching within the NFL, but he’s never gone beyond the position of offensive coordinator—something he last did with the Miami Dolphins in 2004. So why Foerster? When you look at the coaching roster, it’s actually the only—and least-disruptive—decision to be made. That didn’t stop a question from coming up during Lynch’s press conference about what went into the decision. “He’s been in the league for 34 seasons,” Lynch said. “He’s been around Kyle; he is our assistant head coach.” Well put. A quick look at the 49ers coaching roster lists Foerster as the only assistant head coach. So, years of experience and the current job title. It is also important to note that Foerster has been on the staff since 2019 in some capacity. He has seen how Shanahan does things and is one of the longest-tenured assistants on his staff. That at least means (or at least we can hope) things can go as normal as possible in Shanahan’s absence. It’s important to remember the 49ers don’t want to change anything at this point. They don’t need distractions or disruptions to the way Shanahan does things. Furthermore, it’s the beginning of a season without a practice, not the middle of a lost season with jobs on the line. This isn’t a person on a coaching staff picked to coach out the last two or three games after the head coach has been fired. As Lynch said, the 49ers need someone out front, but it’s going to be a collaborative effort, minus Shanahan. But why the decision on the offensive line coach? Well, they could go to defensive coordinator Raheem Morris. He just got off a stint as head coach of the Atlanta Falcons. Whether that’s successful or not isn’t relevant; he at least can run meetings and hold down the fort in Shanahan’s absence, especially when this might just be a name on paper to talk to the media anyway. The problem is, this is Morris’ first year as the defensive coordinator of the 49ers. Which means he needs to install his defense. While we have speculated the familiarity might be a simple transition, that doesn’t mean it’s going to be easy. Lynch said at his press conference that things would be a bit different. Not to mention we’ve gone from Steve Wilks to Nick Sorensen, to Robert Saleh, and now Morris. Four names in just as many seasons. Morris needs to focus on the defense, period. If this does wind up being a bit more involved, Morris doesn’t need more work on his plate. Next there’s Klay Kubiak, the offensive coordinator. This would be Kubiak’s second season as offensive coordinator. Shanahan already is unavailable, and the offense lives and dies through him. To pull one of his right-hand men could stretch the offensive coaching staff even further. Without Shanahan, Kubiak already has more work on his plate as it is. To make him do head coaching responsibilities, in only his second year, would be irresponsible. Special teams coordinator Brant Boyer could be a decent option. But like Kubiak, he’s only been a coordinator on the 49ers for two years. Unlike Kubiak, he wasn’t on the 49ers before that, instead on the New York Jets. Two years isn’t a rookie, but given the complexities of any coaching staff, putting him at the helm is also a bit too soon. Compared to Foerster, Boyer has way less experience coaching in the NFL as well. As we’re rattling off the top names, it should start to seem obvious why Foerster is assuming what we hope is a one- or two-week front position where all he’ll do is talk to the media and anchor a few meetings. Lynch was optimistic that Shanahan would make the Week 1 flight to Melbourne, Australia, but it’s not a guarantee. Who else could do it? Matt Eberflus? He’s assistant head coach for the defense, and was head coach of the Chicago Bears a few years back. Again, Morris is going to be installing the defensive scheme, and the last thing anyone wants is dysfunction on that side of the ball. Putting any defensive coach over there with a new coordinator seems like an ill-advised move. For now, it is the best decision given where the 49ers are. There’s nothing more to read from this.
author: Patrick Holloway

title: Breaking Down Sonny Styles, Commanders’ high-upside linebacker corps
summary: Following the massive overhaul general manager Adam Peters has done to Washington’s front seven, the Commanders’ linebacker unit has a chance to be special. The group boasted high football intelligence with Bobby Wagner’s leadership the past two seasons, but lacked athleticism and dynamic playmaking ability. Wagner played 99% of the team’s defensive snaps; he never […]
full_text: Following the massive overhaul general manager Adam Peters has done to Washington’s front seven, the Commanders’ linebacker unit has a chance to be special. The group boasted high football intelligence with Bobby Wagner’s leadership the past two seasons, but lacked athleticism and dynamic playmaking ability. Wagner played 99% of the team’s defensive snaps; he never got off the field, and at times, depending on the matchup, he struggled covering or running in space. This unit easily has become Washington’s highest-ceiling position group in 2026, and that potential starts and ends with their athleticism, versatility, and schematic flexibility. Washington made it a priority to upgrade the second level of its defense this offseason, pairing first-round pick Sonny Styles with the free agent addition Leo Chenal . Styles is the most important player in this unit’s ascension. His ability to impact the game in multiple ways makes him one of the most intriguing defensive rookies in the NFL. Whether he’s rushing the passer, dropping into coverage, defending the slot, penetrating the line of scrimmage, or flowing sideline to sideline against the run, Styles has the skill set to stay on the field in virtually every situation. The question with Styles, when you discuss this projection, is how quickly he adjusts to the speed of the NFL. If the transition time is quick and effortless, Washington’s defense could unlock a level of flexibility it has not had in years. Chenal, who spent his first four seasons in Kansas City behind an established linebacker corps, now has an opportunity to earn a significant role in Washington and cement himself as something bigger than just a depth piece. His profile undoubtedly complements Styles and gives the Commanders two linebackers capable of wreaking havoc on the first two levels of the defense. With Styles and Chenal being expected to play large roles in Daronte Jones’s defense, the biggest unknowns of the position group are the two returning linebackers, Frankie Luvu and Jordan Magee . Stylistically, both are exactly what Jones could use in his defensive scheme. Luvu’s ability to create pressure as a blitzer and disrupt plays as a penetrating linebacker is a weapon that Jones needs. Despite entering the final year of his contract , Luvu, if utilized correctly by Jones this year, could reestablish himself as one of the league’s dynamic linebackers as he was in 2024. While on paper things could work out in Luvu’s favor, it will still be interesting to know if Washington would be entertaining calls on the vet LB as they get closer to the regular season. Magee was Washington’s most explosive linebacker on the team the last two seasons, but the biggest hindrance for him was his ability to stay on the field. In 2024, injuries kept him off the field, and in 2025, while healthy and seeing more defensive snaps, he was overshadowed by Wagner and Luvu. The best news for Magee heading into his third season is that Jones doesn’t owe loyalty to anyone in front of him on the depth chart. The competition is the most important separator moving forward, and his athletic traits make a difference on the field. But Magee’s athletic ability alone won’t keep him on the field. There are still questions surrounding the interior defensive line, and that group will ultimately help determine just how dominant the linebackers can become. But if Washington’s front can consistently occupy blockers, this linebacker corps has the speed, range, and versatility to dictate as many matchups as they want. I break down in detail on YouTube why this is the position group that could change everything for Washington. Like, subscribe, and comment your thoughts on whether you think the linebacker unit has the highest ceiling on the team.

Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The Daily Slop – 26 July 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Tim Settle Appears Ready for Commanders Training Camp After undergoing offseason foot surgery, defensive tackle Tim Settle was not among the players Washington placed on the PUP ahead of Wednesday’s first practice. Settle spent the offseason working his way back from the foot injury he sustained in December last year that caused him to miss the rest of his second season in Houston. Settle not being included with Trey Amos, Dorance Armstrong, and Deatrich Wise Jr. does not mean he is 100 percent. But clearly the non-designation indicates he has recovered enough to participate, even if the staff decides to limit his workload. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (this story is free to read from beginning to end) This is a throwback link to an April 2026 article Can Antonio Williams play the St. Brown role for David Blough? Commanders general manager Adam Peters spoke after drafting Williams and said they feel he can play both outside and inside, or as he put it, both “the Z and the F”. The Z is the term for the outside receiver that lines up off the line of scrimmage while the F is a common term used for the slot receiver. The receiver that played this role in Detroit back in 2023 was Amon-Ra St. Brown. He was extremely productive in that role, catching 119 passes for 1515 yards and 10 touchdowns in that 2023 season. He actually got a four year, $120 million contract extension off the back of that season. Now, that’s a high bar for Williams to meet and it’s not fair to expect him to be St. Brown right away. But when you watch how St. Brown went about his game in that 2023 Lions offense and then watch Williams, you can see some similarities. In the games I watched, I didn’t get to see Williams run too many choice routes, though in 2024 he did run a few from the backfield in some interesting looks. But even in 2025, he showed the traits that suggests he could be a very good choice route runner. I mentioned earlier that the Lions had two other very effective choice route runners in Laporta and Gibbs, so St. Brown had to be able to do other things. One of those things worked with choice routes. If Williams can prove he can run choice routes and these pivot/return routes effectively, then the Commanders have a potentially very productive receiver on their hands. Those types of routes are very commonly used in the type of offense we’re expecting David Blough to run. But they’re not the only routes Williams would have to run, though the skills needed on those routes translates a lot to the other routes St. Brown ran with the Lions in 2023. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Heavy.com Commanders warned off Stefon Diggs for 2 reasons Most of those potential pitfalls involve how Diggs’ presence could block the path of other viable pass-catchers on the roster. Including 2026 NFL draft third-round pick Antonio Williams, who is already tipped to emulate an All-Pro in the style of offense Blough is expected to call. Harrison pointed out that if the Commanders “want to elevate Antonio Williams over Stefon Diggs, they need to have the ability to do that knowing that there’s not going to be a veteran receiver in the locker room throwing a fit, pouting on the field, whatever it is that he might be able to do.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Hogs Haven Washington Commanders Camp Battles: Luke McCaffrey vs. Jaylin Lane While both McCaffrey and Lane should make the team unless one falls completely flat, playing time could be impacted by how this battle goes. When comparing McCaffrey and Lane, their on-field production is similar thus far in their young careers. In McCaffrey’s first two seasons, he played in 26 games with 29 receptions on 39 targets, totaling 371 receiving yards and three touchdowns. McCaffrey’s 2025 season was unfortunately cut short after he suffered a broken collarbone against Seattle in Week 9. McCaffrey’s special teams impact was also felt in 2025 on kickoffs, as he finished with the third-highest kickoff ( 29.6 yards ) return average in the NFL. Lane’s rookie campaign included 16 catches on 32 targets, finishing with 225 receiving yards in 15 games played. Lane’s impact was certainly felt more so on the punt-return team, as he finished 5th in the NFL in yards per return (13.7) along with two return touchdowns (tied for league-lead). The underlying question remains: Does Washington have the roster space for two receivers who are also special teams returners? To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Hogs Haven NFL players who made it from the roster fringe to the Super Bowl from 2020-2025 In the six Super Bowls from 2020 through 2025, 48/353 (13.6%) of the major contributors on offense and defense initially made their way onto their team from the roster fringes. The average Super Bowl roster contained four former roster-fringe players on offense or defense. The maximum number was eight (2020 Chiefs) and the minimum was two (2025 Patriots, 2020 Buccaneers). It is worth noting that the decision to only count seventh-round draft picks as roster-fringe was arbitrary. Had I included sixth-round picks, the percentage of former roster-fringe players would have been even larger. The takeaway message from this analysis is, before anyone dismisses the chances of a seventh-round pick or UDFA making the final 53-man roster, remember, every one of the past 12 Super Bowl teams had at least two players who started out the same way making significant contributions on offense or defense. Two of the roster-fringe players who made good during this period went on to become stars in the league. Several became starters or major contributors on offense or defense. Even more became important rotational players, backups or special teams contributors. To weather a 17-game season and emerge as a championship contender, an NFL team needs all of the above. Now, let’s take a look at the journeys of a selection of these players from camp hopeful to the Super Bowl. We’ll end with five players who got their start with the Redskins or ended up on the Commanders’ roster. title: Washington Commanders Camp Battles: Mike Sainristil vs. Rasul Douglas
summary: Editor’s note: We have been running down some key battles for playing time in the the leadup to Washington Commanders training camp later this month. Today, John Portis wraps up our coverage with a look at the cornerbacks. We hoped you enjoyed this series and come back for all our coverage as training camp finally […]
full_text: Editor’s note: We have been running down some key battles for playing time in the the leadup to Washington Commanders training camp later this month. Today, John Portis wraps up our coverage with a look at the cornerbacks. We hoped you enjoyed this series and come back for all our coverage as training camp finally arrives . The cornerback spot opposite Trey Amos is still an unknown heading into Commanders training camp, as new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones has made no clear declarations of his intentions. Mike Sainristil and Amik Robertson profile similarly on the inside, but neither has Rasul Douglas’s length and experience on the boundary. Amos’ latest injury update, directly from the corner himself , indicates he will be fully healthy for the start of training camp, but the team put him on the active/PUP list on Saturday. Washington’s staff is typically slow to reinsert players who have previously missed time due to injury, preferring instead to allow the player to ramp up . While this may slow Amos’s development somewhat, it does provide an opportunity for the team to put Mike Sainristil and Rasul Douglas on the field with the first unit for a side-by-side evaluation of their performance in the new defense. The scheme would seem to be a fit for Sainristil, a third-year cornerback and 2024 second-round pick. Miscast in press-man assignments, Sainristil has looked better in zone coverage when allowed to keep his eyes in the backfield and lean on his natural instincts and ball skills. Jones’ system should be a welcome change for Sainristil, who is in desperate need of one. Shifted outside during his rookie season, Sainristil was credited for performing well in a less-than-ideal situation. According to Pro Football Reference , his 2024 allowed passer rating was 96.7, but he actually allowed more passing yards than he did in 2025, which was a regression. Mike Sainristil finishes regular season as one of the WORST CORNERS in football 👇 #90 in TD Allowed (6th) #80 in Separation Rate (1.8) #92 in Receptions Allowed (55) #93 in Yards Allowed (655) #99 in Man Success Rate (62.1%) #77 in Passer rating Allowed (107.5) https://t.co/deQzPT1HBm — Intrinsic (@intrinsicvalyou) January 9, 2025 His plus ball skills have always been evident, with 14 passes defended and four interceptions in 2024 to go with 12 passes defended and four interceptions last season. Sainristil also recorded 93 tackles in his rookie season and 85 tackles in his sophomore campaign. Versatility, ball skills, and tackling are three things Daronte Jones covets in his cornerbacks. Expect Sainristil to have a role this season. Douglas is coming off a season in a scheme that was already a friendly fit, as former Dolphins defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver is a fan of zone coverage. Douglas responded well and demonstrated his own ball skills. In 2025 , he was targeted 82 times, allowing 54 catches for 515 yards and three touchdowns. He also defended 13 passes and recorded two interceptions, and over his career, Douglas has 21 interceptions . The Eagles’ 2017 third-round selection has plus size at 6-foot-2 and 209 pounds. He has spent the majority of his career on the outside but does offer some versatility to play the slot or occasional hybrid role. Douglas is also strong against the run, with 62 tackles and 2 tackles for a loss last season. Again, we have the three things Jones looks for in cornerbacks: versatility, ball skills, and tackling. So where does that leave us? Hogs Haven’s camp battle series has not been about claiming roster spots. Instead, it focuses on players fighting for playing time in new schemes. Jones’ teachings promote them to learn the system as a whole and not by individual assignment, as they will sometimes be asked to do multiple, different things. Both defensive backs should have a role this season, as will Amik Robertson. While some fans may say Douglas is just depth or insurance, Rasul hasn’t played less than 87% of a team’s defensive snaps in the last six years and chose to come to Washington after a strong season. Length on the outside matters, and it isn’t something Sainristil or Robertson can bring to the secondary. The team is still very high on Sainristil’s potential, and Jones mentioned the cornerback’s history at Michigan and inside/outside versatility during the offseason. However, Jones is ultimately about putting his players in the best position to make plays. Sainristil’s success this season will hinge on finding the proper fit, and the team will most certainly use camp and the preseason to find it. When Amos is medically cleared and returns to practice, will that primarily be on the outside, or will Mike give way to Douglas on the boundary for a more suitable role?
